2. Significantly improved market environment due to tightening truck capacity from regulatory enforcement and supply pressures.
3. Successful execution of cost-saving initiatives, removing over $135 million in structural costs, which helped drive a 32% increase in operating income.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Margin pressure in Truckload (JBT), where gross profit dollars declined 12% despite 14% volume growth due to higher purchased transportation rates.
2. Intermodal contract pricing lags the sharp increase in truckload market rates, presenting a future opportunity but a current headwind to realizing full margin potential.
3. Increased driver-related costs due to a tightening labor market, requiring sign-on bonuses and targeted wage increases to attract and retain talent.
rows.key_quote: While demand is improving gradually, the current market tightness is being driven primarily by supply conditions.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Financials: Achieved all-time high operating cash flow of $3.1 billion, driven by a strong realized oil price of $110/bbl.
2. Production Guidance Raised: Lifted the lower end of full-year production guidance to 380,000-400,000 boepd due to strong H1 performance.
3. Project Execution: Major projects Yggdrasil and Valhall PWP-Fenris remain on schedule for first production in summer 2027, with key milestones achieved.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Capex Increase: Increased investment estimates for Yggdrasil and Valhall PWP-Fenris by ~6% ($1.1B pre-tax) to manage final phase execution risk.
2. Impairment Charge: Recognized a $625 million impairment charge related to other intangible assets at Valhall.
3. Increased Quarterly Cost: Unit production cost rose to $8.8 per barrel for the quarter due to planned maintenance, though full-year guidance remains unchanged.
rows.key_quote: Strong premiums on our crude qualities... lifted our realized oil price to $110 per barrel.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Gross margin reached an all-time high of 51.0%, up 130 bps YoY, driven by operational leverage and supply chain efficiencies.
2. Strong organic growth across key segments, including First Aid & Safety (13.2%) and Fire Protection (10.7%), contributing to overall 8.4% organic growth.
3. Confident FY27 guidance with revenue growth of 7.4%-8.7% and adjusted EPS growth of 8.5%-11.3%, reflecting strong business momentum.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. The UniFirst acquisition faces regulatory delays, with the company confirming a second request from the FTC, creating uncertainty around the closing timeline.
2. The Fire Protection segment is expected to face a 100 basis point annual margin headwind in FY27 due to a planned SAP implementation.
3. Energy costs were a 20 basis point headwind in Q4 and are assumed to remain an unfavorable factor in the FY27 outlook.
rows.key_quote: We are adding many new customers. 2-thirds of which transitioned to a managed program after initially handling it on their own.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record EPS of $5.32 driven by the strongest quarterly loan growth since 2012 (excluding acquisitions and PPP), reflecting a $3B increase in average loans. 2. Positive inflection in Commercial Real Estate (CRE) balances for the first time since 2021 and broad-based C&I growth across nearly all businesses. 3. Asset quality improved for the 9th straight quarter, with net charge-offs down to 23 bps and criticized commercial loans falling by $0.7B.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Full-year expense guidance revised to the 'high end' of the $5.5B-$5.6B range, indicating rising investment costs. 2. Full-year NII guided to the 'lower half' of the $7.2B-$7.35B range, suggesting NIM compression is expected despite strong loan growth. 3. Average total deposits declined $0.7B in the quarter, requiring an increase in borrowings to fund loan growth, though end-of-period balances improved.
rows.key_quote: NII was supported by the strongest quarterly loan growth since 2012, excluding acquisitions and PPP during COVID.

rows.positive_highlights: Non-aeronautical revenues grew 23.9% (17% excluding CBX) due to strong performance in cargo and other directly operated businesses. The consolidation of Cross Border Xpress (CBX) contributed MXN 168 million in revenue during its first two months. EBITDA margin expanded by 230 basis points to 69.3% due to cost controls and revenue diversification.
rows.negative_highlights: Total passenger traffic declined 5.6% year-over-year. International traffic at Puerto Vallarta dropped 27% due to security concerns and travel advisories. Operations in Jamaica continued to be negatively impacted by the recovery from Hurricane Melissa.
rows.key_quote: Despite the 5.6% overall decline in passenger traffic, the stronger underlying airport business protected the company earnings capacity.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record net fee and commission income of SEK 7.2B (+8% YoY), driven by a >100% Q-on-Q rebound in capital markets activity.
2. Inflection in corporate lending, with broad-based demand driving 5% FX-adjusted loan growth Q-on-Q within the CIB division.
3. Achieved positive operating jaws (income growth > cost growth) and on track to meet or come in below the full-year cost target.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. A one-off Lithuanian pension reform caused an SEK 11 billion outflow from Wealth and Asset Management, materially impacting net sales.
2. Net other income was negatively impacted by SEK 300 million due to market valuations of non-core assets held within Corporate Investment Banking.
3. Management cautioned that the seasonal Q3 slowdown in capital markets may be 'somewhat more pronounced than usual' after strong Q2 pipeline execution.
rows.key_quote: The one that clearly has contributed this quarter is the corporate and investment bank. Both the corporate loan book that grew 4% or 5%...

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record order backlog grew 8% year-over-year to SEK 22.4 billion, providing visibility for future growth.
2. Utilization rate improved for the third consecutive quarter, reaching 73.5%, demonstrating progress on operational efficiency.
3. The Energy division remains strong with a record backlog of over SEK 7 billion, driven by the global energy transition.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Sales declined, with total growth at -2.4% and adjusted organic growth at -5.3%, primarily due to strategic capacity reductions.
2. Continued market weakness and price pressure in key sectors, including real estate, automotive, and pulp & paper.
3. Gross margin contribution was pressured by lower sales volumes, offsetting some gains from restructuring and efficiency improvements.
rows.key_quote: The EBITDA margin remained stable year-over-year, while sales volumes are lower, much due to the strategic capacity adjustment.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Innovative Medicine grew over 14% excluding STELARA, driven by key brands and new launches.
2. TREMFYA sales grew 71%, fueled by market share leadership in new IBD indications (Crohn's and ulcerative colitis).
3. New launches ICOTYDE and INLEXZO showed strong early uptake, with over 11,000 patients on ICOTYDE and 1 in 3 eligible patients starting INLEXZO.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. MedTech growth was weak at 3.6%, held back by underperformance in the Cardiovascular segment.
2. Abiomed (heart recovery) sales declined 2% due to increased physician caution following a neutral clinical trial.
3. STELARA sales fell 55.7% due to biosimilar competition, creating a 460 basis point headwind to total company growth.
rows.key_quote: Worldwide sales increased 5.6% despite a 460 basis point headwind from STELARA. Excluding STELARA, Johnson & Johnson grew double digits for the quarter.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Raised full-year revenue guidance to EUR 43-45 billion, driven by surging customer demand for capacity. 2. Memory-related net system sales are now expected to grow by over 75% and advanced logic sales by over 25% in 2026, fueled by AI. 3. Backlog strength provides visibility into 2027 and 2028, prompting plans to increase Low-NA EUV and immersion capacity by 30% in 2027.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Q2 R&D expenses were higher than guided due to costs from a technology and IT transformation initiative. 2. Immersion DUV shipments were weak in H1 2026 and need to ramp substantially in H2, indicating previous output was misaligned with current demand. 3. Strong demand is creating tension in the supply chain, requiring significant effort to increase output within the existing manufacturing footprint.
rows.key_quote: The rapid growth of AI-related demand in advanced logic and DRAM is accelerating the move toward more advanced lithography solutions and increasing lithography intensity.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Exceptional capital markets performance: Investment Banking fees grew 50% to $2.1B and Sales & Trading revenue rose 33% to a record $7.2B.
2. Strong Net Interest Income (NII) of $16.2B (+9% YoY), leading to a raised full-year growth forecast to the high end of the 6-8% range.
3. Significant operating leverage of 660 bps achieved, prompting an increase in full-year guidance from >200 bps to a 300-400 bps range.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. The "All Other" segment reported a widened net loss of $292M, though management noted no significant specific drivers.
2. Non-interest expense increased, partly driven by higher activity-related costs from trading and wealth management incentives tied to strong revenue.
3. Net client flows in wealth management were noted by an analyst as tracking below the long-term 5% target, although client balances hit a record.
rows.key_quote: Wealth management, investment banking, and markets all benefit from healthy client activity in favorable capital markets conditions.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to NOK 50-55bn and EBITDA margin to ~7.5% due to strong execution on the Aker BP portfolio and new contract wins. 
2. Successfully renewed all 5 major frame agreements in the Lifecycle segment over the last 12 months, including a new 5-year deal with Cenovus in Canada. 
3. Strong operational execution in the Renewables and Field Development segment, with EBITDA margin of 9.4% driven by project performance and profit from new renewable projects.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Q2 revenue decreased 14% YoY to NOK 13.1 billion, as activity normalized from a 'peak activity period' in 2025. 
2. The tender pipeline was reduced to NOK 77 billion, mainly due to the loss of an offshore wind project in Europe. 
3. Operational cash flow was negative at NOK -195 million, driven by a planned NOK 1.2 billion working capital reversal.
rows.key_quote: [Renewables/Field Dev EBITDA] was driven by solid operational performance as well as profit recognition from two second-generation renewable projects in the period.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Exceptional U.S. market growth: Revenue surged 24% in constant currency, making it the largest market with 51% of group sales.
2. Strong performance in growth categories: E-commerce sales grew 21% and the pre-owned business grew 22%, both outpacing overall group growth.
3. Successful acquisition and jewelry performance: The Deutsch & Deutsch acquisition was successfully integrated, and the Roberto Coin jewelry brand saw sales grow 20%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Margin Compression: Adjusted EBIT margin declined 60 bps to 8.5%, and net product margin fell 70 bps due to tariffs, gold prices, and product mix.
2. One-Off Write-Off: EBIT was negatively impacted by a £3.5 million bad debt write-off related to a department store partner (Saks).
3. Subdued U.K. Market: The U.K. business grew only 5% for the full year, described as a "somewhat subdued market backdrop," significantly lagging the U.S.
rows.key_quote: The U.S. was +24% in constant currency, which saw it become our largest revenue and profits market.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Broad-based growth: Revenue grew 9% and diluted EPS grew 25% ($2.00/share), with all operating segments posting higher net interest and non-interest income.
2. Strong loan and deposit growth: Average loans increased 12% and average deposits grew 10% YoY, reflecting the benefits of the asset cap removal and strategic investments.
3. Record Investment Banking and Markets performance: CIB revenue grew 16%, with record investment banking fees and a 24% increase in Markets revenue, validating the strategy of deploying more balance sheet.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Net Interest Margin (NIM) compression: NIM declined 4 basis points from Q1, driven by deliberate growth in lower-spread markets financing and a mix shift to interest-bearing deposits.
2. Further NIM pressure expected: Management guided for modest NIM compression to continue in Q3 before stabilizing in Q4, raising analyst concerns about the near-term outlook.
3. Short-term profitability drag from growth: Rapid growth in new credit card accounts (up 46% YoY) has significant upfront costs, which is currently offsetting some profitability gains from more mature vintages.
rows.key_quote: what we are seeing in NIM is not happening to us. What we are seeing in NIM is because things that we are doing.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Corporate & Investment Bank (CIB) revenue surged 27% year-on-year, driven by an 86% increase in Equities revenue and a 30% increase in Investment Banking fees.
2. Raised full-year Net Interest Income (NII) guidance to ~$105.5B, citing stronger deposit balances across consumer and wholesale segments.
3. Asset & Wealth Management client assets grew 19% to $7.7 trillion, propelled by strong net inflows of $50B and positive market performance.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Full-year adjusted expense guidance was increased by $2.5B to ~$107.5B, primarily due to higher volume and revenue-related costs.
2. Management expressed caution on sustainability, noting the exceptional equities performance is 'a little bit hard to imagine that being repeated' and the overall environment is 'getting close to as good as it gets'.
3. Continued criticism of pending regulations (Basel III endgame, G-SIB surcharge), which management believes will create unfair competitive dynamics and harm the ability to serve clients.
rows.key_quote: The equities business delivered an exceptionally strong quarter, with revenue up 86% year-on-year, reflecting the highly dynamic market conditions.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong Fee Growth: Net commission/fees up 4.6% YoY, driven by Investment Banking (Corporate Finance up ~20% from M&A/DCM). 2. Record Asset Management Inflows: Record NOK 46 billion net inflow into Asset Management, driving segment income up 13% YoY. 3. Strong Capital & Shareholder Return: CET1 ratio at 17.4% enabled the announcement of a new 1% share buyback program.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Net Interest Margin Compression: NIM fell 4 basis points to 1.70% and NII declined 1.1% QoQ, driven by competition and portfolio mix effects. 2. Intense Market Competition: Management repeatedly cited 'very high competitive pressure, notably within household and mortgages' as a key headwind. 3. Specific Fee Line Decline: Money transfer and banking services fees fell 29%, attributed to higher costs for capital efficiency measures like credit insurance.
rows.key_quote: The margin effect was NOK 264 million, fairly evenly split between competition and product and portfolio mix effects, roughly 1.5 basis points on each.

rows.positive_highlights:
Adjusted profit from property management grew 3% after excluding the effect of the Norion distribution. 
Like-for-like rental growth was 1.2% and current earning capacity increased 10% on an adjusted basis. 
Management sees a 'clear pickup in interest' for smaller office units in Stockholm and Gothenburg, suggesting an early recovery.
rows.negative_highlights:
Reported profit from property management decreased 10% year-over-year. 
Occupancy rate declined from 96% to 95%, driven by weakness in the office segment. 
Central administration costs increased due to investments in digitalization and wage inflation, creating a margin headwind.
rows.key_quote: Profit from property management is down 10%, but adjusting for the Norion distribution, we have an increase of 3%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Gross Margin Performance: Adjusted gross margin improved to 48.4%, up 2 percentage points year-over-year when excluding a prior-year one-off, demonstrating operational resilience.
2. Cloud Software & Services Turnaround: The segment grew 5% organically, reaching an adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.2%, which management called a 'new high level' and a solid base for future profitability.
3. Disciplined Cost Management: Operating expenses were reduced by SEK 1 billion year-over-year, and management successfully mitigated the financial impact of rising component costs in Q2.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant Component Cost Headwinds: Management explicitly stated the 'AI boom is driving up component costs,' with the financial impact expected to 'build up gradually in the coming quarters.'
2. Q3 Networks Margin Dilution: Guided Q3 Networks adjusted gross margin to 48%-50%, a decline from Q2's 50.4%, due to a higher share of lower-margin rollout projects.
3. Continued Enterprise Losses: The Enterprise segment recorded another adjusted EBITDA loss of SEK -0.8 billion, facing analyst questions over its consistent unprofitability and path to value creation.
rows.key_quote: The external environment continues to be rather challenging as the AI boom is driving up component costs.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Gross margin improved to 30.1% from 29.7% due to a positive channel mix towards Service & Aftermarket and restructuring savings.
2. Marine and Mobile Cooling segments continued to show organic growth of 3% and 5% respectively.
3. The restructuring program was extended to target SEK 900 million in total savings, with the run-rate savings reaching SEK 490 million.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. EBITA margin fell to 12.4% from 14.0% due to higher raw material costs and a SEK 50+ million bad debt provision for West Marine.
2. Land Vehicles segment declined 4% organically, dragged down by a 16% collapse in the Americas RV market.
3. Management issued a cautious outlook, stating full-year 2026 growth will be 'tough to achieve' amid market uncertainty and deterioration.
rows.key_quote: The margin reduction is primarily driven by the increased raw material and freight cost.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. NanoKnife revenue surged 64.5% in Q4, with probes growing 47%, driven by record procedure volumes and strong demand in prostate care following new CPT code and Medicare coverage. 
2. The Med Tech segment grew 16.7% in Q4, comprising 48% of total revenue and driving a 130 basis point gross margin expansion for the company to 54.0%. 
3. The Auryon platform posted its 20th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with revenue up 14.4% as it continues to take share in hospital settings.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Mechanical Thrombectomy revenue declined 1.1% in Q4, weakened by a 15.8% decrease in AngioVac sales, attributed to competitive intensity and market lumpiness. 
2. FY27 adjusted loss per share guidance (-$0.29 to -$0.24) is wider than the FY26 result (-$0.24), reflecting continued heavy R&D investment (targeting 10% of sales) outpacing gross profit growth. 
3. Tariff headwinds continue to negatively impact profitability, costing ~$500,000 in Q4 and $4.8 million for the full year, with a similar impact expected in FY27.
rows.key_quote: Total NanoKnife revenue was $11.8 million, an increase of 64.5%... primarily driven by demand for NanoKnife in prostate care.

rows.positive_highlights:
1) Delivered best quarterly revenue in a decade, up 14% to $24.8 billion, driving a 430 basis point improvement in ROTCE to 13%.
2) Strong broad-based growth, with double-digit revenue increases in 4 of 5 businesses, led by Banking (+34%), Services (+18%), and Markets (+17%).
3) Announced plans to increase the quarterly dividend by 12% and bought back $4 billion in stock, supported by a strong CET1 ratio of 12.8%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1) Maintained full-year ROTCE guidance of 10-11% despite H1 performance of 13.1%, implying a significant slowdown in H2 due to planned accelerated investments.
2) Management expects the typical H2 decline in Markets revenue could be 'greater' than the historical 20% due to an exceptionally strong first half.
3) In US Consumer Cards, expense growth is expected to outpace revenue growth in the next few quarters due to investments in acquisitions and customer engagement.
rows.key_quote: A stronger environment is not just upside to report; it is an opportunity we will put to work.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Achieved solid organic growth of 4.7%, driven by an impressive 7% increase in Global Sales (Western Europe & Rest of World).
2. Improved operational efficiency with the OpEx to sales ratio decreasing to 34.6% from 35.5% due to disciplined cost control.
3. U.K. market returned to growth and the sustainable solution business 'ReNu' recorded all-time high sales.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Gross margin declined due to unfavorable sales mix, increased transportation and material costs, and price pressure in the DVT business.
2. Incurred a SEK 10 million one-time transportation cost due to implementation challenges with a new management system.
3. Group rental margin declined, driven by weaker profitability in the U.S. rental business.
rows.key_quote: we experienced unfavorable sales mix driven by strong growth in global sales and relative lower growth in North America.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Equities revenue of $7.4B, with financing up 91% YoY and intermediation up 60% YoY, driven by strong activity in Asia related to AI capital formation.
2. Surging Investment Banking with equity underwriting up 130% YoY and a record debt underwriting quarter; the investment banking backlog increased to a 5-year high.
3. Record fundraising of $59B in Asset & Wealth Management, including $31B in private credit, with management fees up 20% YoY.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Sponsor-led M&A volumes remain 'still subdued versus historical averages,' representing a current weak spot despite a robust overall M&A environment.
2. The Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) fell 40 basis points to 4.3%, the lowest among peers, raising concerns about potential constraints on growing balance sheet-intensive financing businesses.
3. The firm acknowledged significant demand for financing is 'outstripping what we think is the appropriate quantum,' indicating they are turning away business to manage risk and resource constraints.
rows.key_quote: Client activity was particularly strong in Asia, driven in part by robust AI capital formation and investment.

rows.positive_highlights:
Record FY27 Guidance & Backlog: Issued guidance for $130M-$150M in revenue (160-200% YoY growth), backed by a record backlog that grew to $100.6M post-quarter-end.
Dominant AI Market Momentum: AI-related applications drove 71% of FY26 revenue. The lead AI customer is ramping significantly, and a successful benchmark with a second major AI supplier was completed.
Strong Margin Expansion: Q4 non-GAAP gross margin increased by 1000 basis points to 45% year-over-year, driven by higher revenue and a more favorable product mix.
rows.negative_highlights:
Continued SiC Market Weakness: While showing recovery signs, the segment that was 95% of revenue two years ago is now less than 5%, highlighting the steep prior-year decline.
Uncertain Memory Market Timing: Engagements with major memory suppliers are ongoing, but management explicitly excluded potential revenue from FY27 guidance, citing the need for a formal development agreement.
Customer Concentration and Lumpiness: Growth is heavily reliant on a few large customers in the AI sector, exemplified by a single hyperscaler customer's record $41M order, which contributes to lumpy revenue recognition.
rows.key_quote: Our lead AI processor wafer-level burn-in customer is significantly ramping their products driving an increase in forecasted capacity needs for our FOX systems.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Daily sales grew 14.7%, driven by market share gains, with heavy manufacturing sales growing 18% and construction 17%.
2. Key account strategy is working: customer sites spending $50k+/month grew 16.5%, with revenue from this group up over 26%.
3. Strong cost control led to SG&A leverage that offset gross margin pressure, maintained operating margin, and drove ROIC to a decade-plus high.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Gross margin contracted by 75 bps YoY, with a negative price-cost spread accounting for a 40 bps headwind.
2. Incremental margin of 21.5% was below management's target of mid-20s, which CEO Daniel Florness called a disappointment.
3. Full-year digital footprint target was lowered from 66% of sales to a new estimate of 63-64%, as strong non-digital sales growth outpaced expectations.
rows.key_quote: Customer sites spending $50 thousand or more per month grew 16.5% over last year with revenues growing over 26%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Balance Sheet Growth: Achieved 11.6% annualized loan growth and 7.7% annualized deposit growth, driven by broad performance across its footprint in markets like Birmingham, Huntsville, and others, offsetting flat results in Nashville.
2. Stable Profitability Amid Pressure: Maintained a stable Net Interest Margin of 3.95% and achieved a pre-tax pre-provision net revenue return on average assets over 2%, demonstrating disciplined execution in a competitive environment.
3. Significant Capital Return: Repurchased approximately 3% of outstanding shares during the quarter, including a large single transaction, while maintaining a strong CET1 ratio of 11%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Increased Credit Provision: Provision expense rose to $10.1 million, with the majority tied to loan growth and specific reserves on two individually evaluated real estate credits, leading to an increase in non-performing assets.
2. Intense Competitive Environment: Management repeatedly cited increased competition for both loans and deposits, with pressure on loan pricing and deposit costs rising, as competitors offer money market rates over 4%.
3. Moderated Deposit Growth Outlook: Expects full-year deposit growth to trend towards the lower end of the mid-to-high single-digit range due to the highly competitive funding environment.
rows.key_quote: If you look at where our growth came from...Nashville was flat, and the growth came from all the other places.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record production of 27,479 BOE/d (+4% YoY) and a 38% YoY increase in funds from operations to CAD 133.1 million. 2. Exceptional activity in the Duvernay play, with 51 wells spudded year-to-date compared to 55 in all of 2025. 3. Strong leading indicators for future growth, with leasing bonus consideration up 39% YTD and rig activity up to 215 from 170 a year ago.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Wet field conditions in the Eastern Alberta heavy oil region delayed some completion and drilling activity. 2. Net debt remains at CAD 186.6 million, though it is being paid down aggressively. 3. Inherent dependency on continued high commodity prices and third-party capital spending for future results.
rows.key_quote: A Viking well is CAD 1.1 million... and a Duvernay well is CAD 11 million... It's 10 times price for 10x the volumes.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Underwriting Profitability: The underlying frequency loss ratio improved by 4 percentage points year-over-year, driven by disciplined pricing actions that outpaced claims development.
2. Robust Revenue Growth: Insurance revenue grew 9.3% in the quarter, led by effective price increases across all segments.
3. Key Strategic Partnerships: Secured a new primary insurance partnership with Tesla in Norway and renewed/added other major agreements (Tekna, Huseierne), strengthening future distribution.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Danish Court Ruling: Incurred a NOK 419 million net negative profit impact from a Danish Supreme Court ruling on workers' compensation.
2. Volume Pressure from Strategy: Strategic termination of agreements with fire mutuals in Norway caused a short-term negative impact on volume growth in both private and commercial segments.
3. Weak Swedish Results: The Swedish business reported a NOK 56 million decrease in the insurance service result, mainly attributed to negative run-off losses.
rows.key_quote: We saw significant improvement in profitability this quarter with the underlying frequency loss ratio down four percentage points.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strongest leasing quarter since 2020 with NOK 131 million in positive net letting, driven by NOK 175 million in new contracts.
2. Signed two major, long-term leases with Coop (15,500 sq m) and Multiconsult (16,400 sq m), securing long-term occupancy.
3. Maintained a solid financial platform with NOK 7.6 billion in undrawn credit lines and successful issuance of over NOK 1 billion in new green bonds.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Reported a net loss of NOK 855 million, driven by a NOK 1.1 billion negative revaluation of investment properties due to higher interest rates.
2. Occupancy fell from 94.3% to 93.3% with management expecting "further near-term pressure before stabilization".
3. Leverage increased, with LTV rising to 48.6%, and financing costs climbed, with all-in net financial cost at 4.50% and expected to increase further.
rows.key_quote: Operationally, this was a strong quarter for us. We delivered net letting of a solid NOK 131 million, which is the highest we've seen since 2020.

rows.positive_highlights:
Record Revenue and Pricing Power: Revenue grew 14% to $17.7B with total unit revenue up 12.4%, driven by strong demand and the ability to recapture fuel costs through higher fares.
Strong Diversified Revenue Streams: Premium & loyalty revenue grew nearly 20%, with the Amex partnership expected to generate $9B in remuneration. Cargo revenue jumped 39% and MRO grew over 30%.
Affirmed Full-Year Guidance: Despite a multi-billion dollar fuel headwind, the company affirmed its full-year EPS guidance of $6.50-$7.50, signaling confidence in sustained revenue momentum.
rows.negative_highlights:
Massive Fuel Cost Headwind: Total fuel expense was $4.4B, up nearly $2B YoY, with the average a price of $3.93 per gallon significantly pressuring margins.
Constrained Capacity Growth: Capacity grew only 1% in Q2, well below initial plans, partly due to a strategic response to fuel spikes, which limited potential volume growth.
Refinery Outage Impact: A temporary refinery outage had a negative impact of $0.05 per gallon in Q2, with a further $0.05 to $0.07 negative impact expected to carry into Q3.
rows.key_quote: structural change has accelerated enabling the industry to recapture this year's fuel cost inflation at the fastest pace of any recent cycle.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong Norwegian performance with its best combined ratio in 10 years (77.3%). 2. Group underlying claims ratio improved by 50 basis points due to past profitability actions. 3. Private segment revenue grew a solid 5%.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. A DKK 1.2 billion one-off charge was booked for a Danish workers' compensation case. 2. Commercial segment revenue declined due to a weak January renewal cycle. 3. Full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook was lowered to around 3%.
rows.key_quote: The underlying claims ratio developing positively, improving 50 basis points thanks to the profitability actions taken the last few years to fight off inflationary pressures.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong sales growth: Net merchandise sales increased 12.5% (10.7% comparable), driven by a 7.1% increase in transactions.
2. Record membership metrics: Renewal rate hit an all-time high of 90.5%, and membership income grew 17.6%, fueled by Platinum member growth.
3. Aggressive expansion announced: Entering a new country, Chile, with a $100M investment plan for three clubs, plus five other clubs in the pipeline.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Rising operating costs: SG&A as a percentage of revenue increased to 13.3%, driven by pre-opening expenses in Chile and higher labor costs in Colombia.
2. Foreign currency challenges: Recorded a $10.5 million net loss in total other expense, up from $7.2 million, primarily due to increased foreign currency transaction costs, particularly in Trinidad.
3. Macroeconomic uncertainty: Management noted ongoing inflation impacting consumer purchasing power and geopolitical tensions affecting costs like fuel and freight.
rows.key_quote: Net merchandise sales increased 12.5%... Our average sales ticket grew by 5%, and transactions grew 7.1% versus the same prior year period.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Acquired Hero Defense Systems to add complementary, lower-price-point products to expand customer base.
2. Improved CL launcher first pass yield by 650% from May to June, targeting over 90% in Q4, reducing rework and cost per unit.
3. The 'try before you watch' program shows strong 30% conversion, and dedicated retail end caps significantly boosted sales at a partner chain, validating educational sales strategies.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Net revenue declined 42.5% to $16.4 million, significantly missing expectations.
2. E-commerce traffic fell 13% YoY and conversion rates halved to 0.59%, while retail was hit by slow watch-through from high channel inventory.
3. Reported gross margin collapsed to 11% (from 62% YoY) due to $9.4 million in one-time inventory/impairment charges from closing its ammo facility.
rows.key_quote: These results were driven by two things: continued e-commerce pressure with website traffic down 13% and slower retail reorders due to elevated partner inventory.

rows.positive_highlights: Quest brand household penetration increased 120 basis points year-over-year to 20.5%, demonstrating continued brand relevance. Quest chips segment consumption grew strongly by over 17%. Q3 financial results, while down year-over-year, came in ahead of management's internal expectations.
rows.negative_highlights: Atkins brand net sales collapsed by 24.6%, driven by a 220 basis point decline in household penetration. Consolidated gross margin declined significantly by 390 basis points to 32.5% due to input cost inflation and restructuring costs. Q4 revenue guidance implies an accelerated decline of 10-13%, worse than the 6.3% decline in Q3.
rows.key_quote: Atkins net sales declined 24.6%... due to declining household penetration from insufficient marketing support.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Exceptional revenue growth of 43% driven by a 35% comparable sales increase, with U.S. revenue accelerating 55%. 2) Digital channel net revenue surged 56%, fueled by the new mobile app which now accounts for ~30% of digital business. 3) Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 410 bps to a record 20.1%, and gross margin hit a record 50.3% despite tariff headwinds.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) Gross margin faced 190 basis points of pressure from tariffs and the de minimis suspension. 2) Management forecasts moderating gross margin expansion in the second half due to lapping historically low markdowns and new DC depreciation. 3) Potential for future tariff increases could add $25-30M in pressure, which is not yet reflected in guidance.
rows.key_quote: Our 43% top line growth was fueled by a robust 35% increase in comparable sales. This performance reflects broad based strength across the entire business.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record quarterly sales driven by the Metal Coatings segment, which grew 12.3% on strong infrastructure, industrial, and data center demand. 2. Raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance midpoint by over 20%, citing faster ramp-up of the new Washington facility and successful pricing/surcharge actions. 3. Increased quarterly dividend by 20%, signaling confidence in sustained earnings and robust cash flow generation.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Softer volumes in the Precoat Metals segment's construction, HVAC, and appliance end markets partially offset growth. 2. Transportation end markets declined 1.2% due to lower commercial trailer activity. 3. Metal Coatings segment margins dropped year-over-year, which management attributed to the impact of large projects and a one-time land sale in the prior year.
rows.key_quote: The new Washington site has hit its dates and commitments... and we are pushing price and adding surcharges on the zinc because zinc has stayed high.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. International business remains very strong, growing 7% with a full point of operating margin expansion in Q2. 2. US Foods (PFNA) affordability strategy successfully reversed category volume declines and led to market share gains. 3. Global volumes grew 3% in foods and 2% in beverages, marking the fastest volume growth since 2022.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. North American business was softer than expected in Q2 due to a weaker consumer environment. 2. High gas prices specifically hurt high-margin impulse channels (convenience & gas), reducing sales conversion. 3. Management guided to the 'low end' of the reaffirmed full-year EPS range, signaling lowered internal expectations.
rows.key_quote: The consumer is worse than what we had anticipated and it's driven mainly by gas prices.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Signed agreement to acquire SFE Group for $472M, expanding TAM by $1B into markets like defense, power gen, and data centers.
2. Achieved strong organic growth in key segments, with IT&S products up 5% and Cortland up 25%.
3. Grew HLT business through data center demand and secured a new ~$5M defense contract with a European contractor for fiscal 2027.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Lowered FY2026 guidance for organic growth to 1-2% and adjusted EPS to $1.84-$1.89.
2. IT&S services business declined 8% organically, impacted by a slowdown and a $3M project delay in the Middle East.
3. Underlying gross margins were negatively impacted by a product mix shift to lower-margin HLT business and dilution from the declining services business.
rows.key_quote: Gross margins were negatively impacted by mix given the higher growth rate of our HLT business and continued dilution from our service business.

rows.positive_highlights:
Rental income grew by 5.9% and the surplus ratio improved to 74% in Q2.
Occupancy rate increased from 86% to 87%, supported by new large leases in Solna Business Park.
Property values turned slightly positive with a SEK +120 million change (+0.15%) in Q2, driven by city properties.
rows.negative_highlights:
Net letting was significantly negative at SEK -86 million for the quarter, driven by two large pre-announced terminations (Max Matthiessen and Telenor).
Rental development in the identical portfolio decreased by 1.1% due to previously announced terminations kicking in.
Lease renegotiations during H1 resulted in an average change of -1.7%, indicating some pricing pressure in specific cases.
rows.key_quote: The net letting was SEK -86 million in the quarter...two large terminations from Max Matthiessen and Telenor represent this figure.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Major Strategic Acquisition: Acquired 95 properties from Castellum for SEK 13.3 billion, with an initial 5% yield and 15% vacancy offering future upside.
2. Record Financial Performance: Q2 rental income grew 7%, operating surplus +6%, and income from property management +6%, all reaching historic highs for the company.
3. Improved Market Activity: Management reported a significant uptick in tenant discussions and leasing activity after a 'frosty start of the year,' signaling a positive trend for H2.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Increased Balance Sheet Leverage: The debt-financed acquisition will push LTV close to the 60% policy limit, prompting analyst questions about future dividends and deleveraging via asset sales.
2. Occupancy Rate Dip: Overall occupancy declined by one percentage point to 89%, primarily caused by moving two large, not-yet-fully-stabilized projects into the active portfolio.
3. Minor Margin Compression: For Q2, rental income grew 7% while operating surplus grew 6%, indicating a slight deterioration in the surplus ratio (profit margin).
rows.key_quote: out of the increase of 77, 57 actually comes from renegotiations, new leases, and projects. That is the core business showing growth.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Beer gross margin improved to 39%, benefiting from 30 bps of fixed cost absorption on higher shipments and 20 bps from net pricing.
2. Beer shipment growth of 1.8% was better than anticipated, supporting cost leverage.
3. Strong double-digit growth in Corona Non-Alcoholic and continued momentum in other portfolio brands outside of the main flagship products.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Core brands Modelo Especial and Corona Extra are sluggish and facing headwinds, a primary concern highlighted by analysts.
2. A volatile consumer environment, with a slowdown in April/May attributed to a sharp spike in gas prices impacting the core consumer.
3. Future operating margin headwinds are expected in Q2/Q3 due to a planned spike in marketing spend (to over 10% of net sales) and increased SG&A.
rows.key_quote: A massive spike in gas prices, and we did see the consumer respond by slowing down.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Enterprise North America deferred revenue surged 18% year-over-year, validating the go-to-market transformation. 2. Consolidated subscription and committed invoiced amounts grew 17%, indicating strong future recognized revenue. 3. Services booking pace is up over 25% year-to-date, with a significant amount already contracted for FY27 delivery.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Full-year revenue guidance was lowered by ~$6M due to specific contract timing shifts, a delayed education contract, and international weakness. 2. Gross margin declined to 73.9% from 76.5% year-over-year, attributed to increased delivery costs and a shift in service mix. 3. International operations remain challenged, particularly in China and other regions affected by geopolitical tensions.
rows.key_quote: Growth in invoice amounts, coupled with significant service bookings... gives us high confidence in the year ahead.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strategic price investments in FY26 increased household penetration and grew base volume by 1% in invested areas after a prior 10% decline.
2. A new transformation initiative aims to deliver $750 million in cost savings in FY27 and $3 billion by FY30 to offset inflation and fund growth.
3. The company is pivoting to a strong innovation pipeline for FY27, including Cheerios Protein, new Old El Paso frozen snacks, and Tiki Cat to drive premium mix.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Guidance for fiscal 2027 includes negative organic sales growth, with Q1 expected to be weaker than the full-year average.
2. Poor execution on price pack architecture for Totino's and headwinds in the Wilderness brand were significant drags on FY26 performance.
3. Input cost inflation is expected to remain elevated at 4-5% in FY27, and the company anticipates a continued headwind from retail inventory destocking in the Pet segment.
rows.key_quote: We are entering the year with our base where we invested on price up about 1%, and we have household penetration growth.

rows.positive_highlights:
Sequentially improved aggregate gross margin to 14.1% driven by operational efficiency, cost discipline, and in-sourcing initiatives, despite low production volumes.
Significant expansion of the owned lease fleet to 20,600 railcars through the acquisition of 4,400 cars, while maintaining 99% utilization.
Secured new orders for 2,200 railcars valued at $340 million, with lease originations representing a strong 60% of total global orders.
rows.negative_highlights:
New railcar demand is at a trough, with industry forecasts for calendar 2026 at less than 25,000 cars, the lowest level since 2010.
FY2026 EPS guidance was narrowed to $3.00-$3.15, reflecting that some customer deliveries are moving from Q4 into fiscal 2027.
Facing regulatory uncertainty from a potential Section 301 tariff on tank cars (20% of backlog) and a separate EPA coupler case.
rows.key_quote: We have never had these kinds of margins at this low level of production in the history of Greenbrier.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Solutions growth momentum: Average daily sales in vending up 15% and in-plant programs up 16% YoY. 
2. Strong profit leverage: Achieved 32% incremental operating margin, with adjusted operating expenses as a percent of sales declining 150 bps YoY. 
3. Sales force productivity: Sales per rep per day improved in the high teens YoY, reflecting successful organizational changes and doing "more with less".
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Heavily reliant on price for growth: Pricing contributed 720 basis points to the 7.8% sales growth, while volume contributed only 50 basis points. 
2. Structural inefficiency: Management benchmarking indicates the company is "relatively heavy by 1,000 heads" compared to peers for its revenue level. 
3. Moderating Q4 incremental margins: Guidance implies incremental margins stepping down from over 30% in Q3 to the mid-20s in Q4 due to lapping prior-year cost-saving initiatives.
rows.key_quote: Sales per rep per day has improved high teens year-over-year, suggesting that at this point in time, we are fundamentally doing more with less.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Accelerating Core Growth: Reported 5th consecutive quarter of accelerating organic ASV growth, up 7.1% to $2.48 billion, its highest rate since Q1 2024. 
2. AI Adoption Driving Expansion: ASV growth among clients using FactSet AI solutions was 50% higher than for other clients, with over 10% of total ASV growth coming directly from AI SKUs.
3. Longer-Term Client Commitments: The average contract term for renewals extended by roughly 30% as clients shifted to multi-year enterprise agreements, locking in future revenue.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant Margin Contraction: Adjusted operating margin fell to 34.0%, down approximately 300 basis points YoY, due to deliberate investments, higher performance-based compensation, and AI token costs.
2. Increased Operating Expenses: Compensation expenses rose 7% YoY due to performance incentives linked to ASV growth, not headcount. Technology spending also increased significantly.
3. FX Hedging Loss: The company's FX hedging program created a 60-basis-point drag on operating margin, shifting from a gain in the prior year to a loss.
rows.key_quote: Overall ASP growth among clients using our AI solutions was 50% higher than for the rest of the book.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Exceeded guidance on all key metrics: Revenue grew 7% to $253M, EPS grew 16% to $1.62, and operating margin reached 40%.
2. Strong performance in Data Platform products, driven by customers leveraging their business data to provide context for AI.
3. Generated strong free cash flow ($79M), enabling aggressive debt repayment of $110M in H1 and lowering net leverage to 2.9x.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Underlying top-line momentum, measured by ARR, remains modest at 2% year-over-year growth.
2. Part of the Q2 revenue beat was due to deal timing, pulling some revenue forward from Q3, resulting in slightly soft Q3 guidance.
3. While M&A seller expectations are improving, they have not yet fully reset, potentially delaying the execution of a large, value-accretive deal.
rows.key_quote: We saw particularly strong performance in our data platform products, as our customers increasingly leverage their business data to provide context for AI.

rows.positive_highlights: Performance running grew double-digits for the 5th consecutive quarter, adding ~$1B to the business. A one-time tariff recovery of $986M significantly boosted reported gross margin and EPS. Wholesale grew 10% in North America, with revenue growth at Foot Locker positive for the first time in 4 years.
rows.negative_highlights: Sportswear and Jordan streetwear categories, representing ~50% of revenue, declined double-digits amid weak watch-through. Overall revenue fell 4% currency-neutral, with Nike Direct down 9%. Revenue guidance for the next two quarters was lowered due to macro pressures and plans to tighten inventory.
rows.key_quote: Our consumer is under pressure... we can particularly see it having a larger impact on sportswear which declined double digits in the quarter.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. LatAm ecosystem now drives over 50% of regional revenue with $1.5B in sales growing at 40%+.
2. EBITDA grew 84% to EUR 1.3 billion, and free cash flow improved by EUR 2 billion over two years to a positive EUR 1.5 billion.
3. Headline earnings per share grew 24%, boosted by the effectiveness of the share buyback program.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Next year's consolidated profitability is guided to be 'roughly flat' due to strategic investments.
2. In Brazil, 'irrational' competition is forcing higher investment in iFood, increasing cost-per-order (CPO).
3. Just Eat Takeaway.com (JET) turnaround is ongoing, with revenue still declining 4% year-over-year, requiring significant investment to fix.
rows.key_quote: The ecosystem besides food delivery today has revenues of $1.5 billion growing more than 40%... today, the ecosystem is more than 50% of our revenue.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record contract signings for the IX technology suite, with deal count up 400% year-over-year, on track to surpass $120 million in ARR.
2. Achieved record second-quarter adjusted free cash flow of $242 million, enabling accelerated debt reduction.
3. Increased internal efficiency, with revenue per non-billable headcount growing 14% year-over-year due to internal AI deployment.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Full-year revenue and EPS guidance was lowered due to external client pressures.
2. Experienced a 2% additional revenue headwind from a combination of accelerated offshoring and client spending cuts.
3. Increased restructuring charges to $175 million for the year to realign cost structure, impacting GAAP results.
rows.key_quote: Combined, this has resulted in approximately 2% additional headwind going into our third quarter that we see for the rest of the year.

rows.positive_highlights:
Record Q4 revenue of $642M, driven by 31% organic growth and strong demand in the Autonomous Systems (AXS) segment which grew 49% pro-forma.
Strong momentum in counter-UAS with Titan product sales more than doubling in FY26 and the Locust laser system achieving 100% success in a key maritime test.
Secured multiple key program wins for future growth, including LASSO (Switchblade 400), LRR (P550 drone), and MRR (Vapor CLE), positioning for large, long-term contracts.
rows.negative_highlights:
Q4 adjusted gross margin deteriorated to 34% from 40% YoY, impacted by business mix, a one-time forward loss, and lower service margins.
Space, Cyber, and Directed Energy (SCDE) segment revenue declined 8% pro-forma due to the SCAR program termination and government funding delays impacting the cyber business.
FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance is flat YoY ($3.02-$3.34 vs $3.31 in FY26) due to a projected $37M (77%) increase in depreciation and amortization from heavy capital investments.
rows.key_quote: The autonomous systems or AXS segment recognized 492 million in revenue... which represented a 49% increase over fiscal year 25 pro forma revenues.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strategic Acquisition: Announced the purchase of Kalwall, expected to add ~$85M in revenue at a high-margin (~15% adj. EBITDA). 2. Services Segment Strength: Services revenue grew 8.2%, its 9th consecutive quarter of growth, with backlog also increasing. 3. Metals Margin Expansion: Despite a 4.8% sales decline, the Metals segment expanded its adjusted EBITDA margin to 11.2% through productivity and cost controls.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Glass Segment Weakness: Sales declined 7.6% with lower margins due to soft demand in new construction. 2. Consolidated Margin Pressure: Adj. EBITDA margin fell to 9.4% from 9.9% a year ago, driven by higher material costs and lower volume. 3. Weak Q2 Outlook: Management guided for Q2 net sales to be slightly lower and adjusted EPS to be lower on a year-over-year basis.
rows.key_quote: Adjusted EBITDA margin decreased...driven by higher material and freight costs, and the impact of lower volume.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Credit quality improved significantly, with the FPD30+ rate declining to 0.76% from 1.16% in the prior year's comparable quarter. 2. Internet insurance revenue grew 38% quarter-over-quarter, helping the overall insurance segment achieve growth for the first time in six quarters. 3. AI-driven efficiency reduced customer acquisition cost as a percentage of revenue by over 50% year-over-year.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Total net revenue declined 41% year-over-year to RMB 915.1 million. 2. The company reported a significant net loss of CNY 494.7 million, though this was an improvement from the prior quarter. 3. The company recorded a fair value loss of CNY 89 million related to its digital asset holdings.
rows.key_quote: The most significant driver of our quarter-over-quarter earnings improvement was the normalization of the credit-related provisions.

rows.positive_highlights: Flavor Solutions segment delivered accelerated momentum with 3% organic growth, driven by a 2% volume increase in the Americas across CPGs, private label, and foodservice. Gross margin expanded 270 basis points (130 bps on an underlying basis), driven by pricing, cost savings, and a tariff refund. Total sales grew 14% largely due to a 12% contribution from the McCormick Mexico acquisition.
rows.negative_highlights: Americas Consumer segment volumes declined approximately 3%, impacted by shifting demand, price gaps, and heightened competition in U.S. spices and seasonings. The company guided Q3 adjusted operating income growth to high-single to low-double digits, indicating a slowdown from Q2 due to SG&A timing. QSR customer volumes in EMEA and parts of Asia Pacific were pressured by softer foot traffic.
rows.key_quote: Organic growth was driven by the accelerated momentum in Flavor Solutions, with growth across flavors and branded food service customers.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. QNX revenue grew 26% YoY to $72M, driven by development license revenue hitting an 8-quarter high, a leading indicator of future royalty growth. 2. Secure Communications revenue grew 24% YoY to $74M, propelled by a major multi-year expansion deal with Shared Services Canada. 3. Total adjusted gross margin expanded 400 bps to 79%, and the company generated positive operating cash flow in a seasonally weak quarter for the first time in 9 years.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. The dollar-based net retention rate (DBNRR) in Secure Communications was 92%, indicating some continued underlying customer churn. 2. Management cautioned that outsized growth in Secure Communications from large government deals is not expected every quarter and that overall growth will not be linear. 3. While a first design win for the high-potential Alloy Kore platform is expected this fiscal year, none have been secured yet.
rows.key_quote: QNX revenue grew 26% driven by development licenses, while Secure Communications grew 24% from a major deal with the Canadian government.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Gross margin improved by 120 basis points to 56.6% due to supplier consolidation and efficiency gains. 2. Operating margin (excluding one-offs) reached 12%, driven by a 2% reduction in SG&A costs. 3. Inventory as a percentage of sales improved, falling from 16.6% to 15.8% year-over-year.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Sales were flat year-over-year, hampered by weak consumer confidence in Western Europe and 3% fewer stores. 2. Efforts to improve stock efficiency led to unintended supply gaps, where inventory was insufficient to meet demand. 3. Logistics network consolidation in Europe led to product availability disturbances, negatively impacting sales in May and June.
rows.key_quote: we came in slightly short on supply in relation to the demand we could see.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Data Center Growth: Sales expected to grow ~60% from $80M to $130M in fiscal 2027, driven by new programs with hyperscale customers.
2. Customer Recoveries: Successfully negotiated ~$45M from automotive customers for EV program changes, with $19M recognized in fiscal 2026 earnings.
3. Operational Improvements: Realized 700 bps of margin improvement in the Egypt facility and expect ~$5M in annual savings from restructuring in Malta.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Automotive Segment Decline: Automotive sales fell 8.1% for the year due to program roll-offs and significant EV program delays in North America.
2. Mexico Under-absorption: Mexico facilities continue to be impacted by under-absorption and customer schedule volatility despite ongoing transformation efforts.
3. Interface Segment Contraction: Interface segment sales declined 47%, primarily reflecting the planned roll-off of a major appliance program and the divestiture of the DataMate business.
rows.key_quote: Excluding... portfolio refinement activity and customer recoveries, we expect adjusted EBITDA to grow approximately 82% year over year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Motorhome RV segment recovery: Revenue grew year-over-year, and operating margin improved to 3.0% from -1.1% in the prior year, driven by new products and operational improvements.
2. Barletta's market share gains: The pontoon brand continued to outperform a soft marine market, with its retail share reaching 9.3% on a trailing 12-month basis.
3. Operational and cost discipline: Management is actively reducing SG&A, improving working capital, and planning footprint consolidation to right-size capacity for the current environment.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Worsening consumer demand: 'Macro demand worsened as our fiscal third quarter progressed...Reflecting a more cautious consumer than we had anticipated heading into the spring watching season.'
2. Lowered full-year guidance: Cut outlook for revenue and EPS, citing a more cautious demand environment and increased competitive intensity.
3. Towable segment pressure: Revenues declined significantly, and the flagship Grand Design brand is facing 'targeted pressure, particularly in fifth wheels,' amid an intense competitive environment.
rows.key_quote: Macro demand worsened as our fiscal third quarter progressed, reflecting a more cautious consumer than we had anticipated heading into the spring watching season.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong pricing execution: Organic revenue growth was driven by 3% pricing, with management projecting high-single digit pricing in H2.
2. Significant margin expansion: Adjusted gross margin increased 200 basis points to 34.2% and EBITDA margin expanded 70 bps, driven by pricing and restructuring savings.
3. Raised profit guidance: Adjusted EPS grew 19% to $1.41, and the company raised its full-year EPS guidance midpoint due to strong execution.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Cautious volume outlook: Volumes were slightly down YoY, and management's outlook anticipates volumes declining by mid-single digits in the second half of the year.
2. Segment weakness: The Engineering Adhesives segment saw a 1% organic revenue decline due to the solar business exit, and the automotive market experienced mid-single-digit declines.
3. Increased leverage from acquisition: The announced acquisition of AMS will raise pro forma net leverage to ~4x, leading to analyst questions about investor concern and the associated risks.
rows.key_quote: Adjusted gross profit margin was 34.2%, up 200 basis points versus last year, driven by pricing execution and restructuring savings.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Significant market outperformance: Q4 same-restaurant sales and guest counts both exceeded the industry benchmark by over 300 basis points.
2. Exceptional LongHorn Steakhouse growth: Achieved 9.5% same-restaurant sales growth in Q4, outperforming the industry by 810 basis points, driven by quality investments and value perception.
3. Strong profitability and shareholder returns: Adjusted EPS grew 22.8% to $3.66, restaurant-level EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps, and the board approved an 8% dividend increase.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Anticipated inflation headwinds: FY2027 guidance includes total inflation of ~3%, with commodities at ~3% and labor at ~3.5%.
2. EPS drag from growth initiatives: Accelerated new unit growth (75-80 openings plus 11 conversions) is expected to create a ~$0.10 EPS drag in FY2027 from pre-opening and inefficiency costs.
3. Observed softness in a key demographic: Management noted a slight decline in visit frequency from guests under the age of 35.
rows.key_quote: Same-restaurant sales and same-restaurant guest counts each exceeded the industry benchmark by over 300 basis points for the quarter.

rows.positive_highlights: Core EBITDA increased 78.6% Y/Y to $354 million and core EBITDA margin expanded 440 bps to 14.2%, driven by metal margin expansion and Precast acquisitions. Management provided strong Q4 guidance, expecting a $40-50 million sequential increase in core EBITDA. The company is nearing a significant cash flow inflection point as major CapEx programs like the West Virginia micro mill conclude.
rows.negative_highlights: Q3 results were negatively impacted by approximately $20 million due to planned maintenance outages at 7 of 10 North American mills. Metal margins were temporarily squeezed by an unexpected rise in scrap costs. Weather-related disruptions delayed construction activity and shipments in key markets, costing an estimated $10M in volume just in the steel group.
rows.key_quote: Planned maintenance outages at 7 of our 10 mills negatively impacted results by approximately $20 million in the quarter.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Completed transformative acquisition of a 62% stake in Klöckner & Co, targeting $150 million in EBITDA synergies.
2. Direct sales volume grew 3% year-over-year, driven by market share gains in automotive (+5%) and strong growth in energy (+24%).
3. Implemented lean flow principles reducing inventory by 37% at one facility and developed an AI agent for order management with >90% accuracy.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Recorded a $94.5 million pre-tax non-cash impairment charge in the electrical steel unit due to market softness and competition.
2. Adjusted EBIT decreased to $54.0 million from $70.1 million a year ago, driven by lower direct spreads and reduced tolling volumes.
3. Toll processing volumes declined 15% YoY, and shipments to construction and heavy truck markets were down 14% each.
rows.key_quote: The year-over-year decrease [in adjusted EBIT] was driven primarily by lower direct spreads... and lower toll processing volumes.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Acuity Intelligent Spaces (AIS) revenue grew 15% to $304 million, with operating margin expanding 150 bps to 25.1%, driven by share gains and new product launches for data centers.
2. Core Lighting (ABL) business maintained a strong adjusted gross margin of 46.1% despite a revenue decline, and management reported that order trends are now 'firming'.
3. Strong cash flow generation ($520M YTD) funded an 18% dividend increase, $230M in share buybacks, and $200M in debt repayment.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Acuity Brands Lighting (ABL) revenue declined 2% year-over-year to $905 million due to a difficult prior-year comparison related to price increases.
2. ABL's adjusted operating profit margin declined 60 basis points to 18.2%, primarily as a result of lower sales volume.
3. Management cited ongoing inflationary pressures, including materials like metals and a notable 12% increase in the company's future medical costs.
rows.key_quote: In our core Eclipse controllers business, we are out-innovating the competition and taking share.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Secured commercial agreements with distributors for a potential of 360 CapEx system sales over the next 2-3 years.
2. Nanox.ARC system is now in commercial use and integrated into clinical workflow at RadNet, the largest U.S. outpatient imaging operator.
3. Teleradiology services revenue grew to $3.1M from $2.6M, with non-GAAP gross margin at 36%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Withdrew full-year 2026 revenue guidance due to 'longer than anticipated' commercialization and revenue recognition cycles.
2. Company reported 'substantial doubt as to the company's ability to continue as a going concern' due to high cash burn and the need for additional financing.
3. Consolidated non-GAAP gross loss widened significantly to $2.2 million from $0.4 million in the prior-year period.
rows.key_quote: We have experienced longer than anticipated timelines between the execution of commercial agreements... and the related recognition of revenue.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Hyve division non-GAAP gross billings surged 117% YoY to $5.5B, driven by program expansions with existing hyperscalers and securing business with all top 5 U.S. hyperscalers. 2. Distribution segment's Advanced Solutions billings grew 31% YoY, fueled by strong AI-related demand for infrastructure and security. 3. Non-GAAP EPS increased 62% YoY to a record $4.85, demonstrating significant operating leverage.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Free cash flow was a consumption of ~$330 million due to working capital investments needed to support rapid growth in the Hyve business. 2. Hyve's non-GAAP operating margin declined 50 basis points YoY to 3.3% due to business mix and costs associated with ramping new programs. 3. Management noted potential supply constraints for memory and CPUs, incorporating this risk into Q3 guidance.
rows.key_quote: AI is driving demand across both businesses, from hyperscale infrastructure build-outs to enterprise data center modernization, to AI-capable devices in our endpoint mix.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Revenue grew 17% in Q4, driven by acquisitions contributing $44 million and 3% organic growth.
2. Accelerating demand for ASME water tanks for data centers; shipped $13M in FY26 and expects to ship at least that much in Q1 FY27 alone.
3. Consumer Products adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 19.2% from 16.6% year-over-year, driving segment profit growth despite flat sales.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Gross margin declined to 27.4% from 29.3% YoY due to unfavorable product mix, acquisition accounting, and cost pressures.
2. Adjusted EBITDA decreased to $83.5 million from $85.1 million, primarily due to a $7 million drop in equity income from the ClarkDietrich joint venture.
3. Adjusted EPS for the quarter fell to $0.97 from $1.06 in the prior-year quarter, reflecting the decline in profitability.
rows.key_quote: We shipped $13M of ASME tanks for data centers in fiscal 2026 and expect to ship at least that much in Q1 '27.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Inbound travel gross bookings surged by approximately 90% year-on-year, driven by favorable visa policies and marketing efforts. 2. International OTA platform gross bookings increased by approximately 65% year-over-year, with broad-based demand. 3. Corporate travel revenue grew 20% year-over-year, signaling continued market penetration.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Weak Q2 revenue guidance of 3% to 8% YoY growth, a major deceleration from Q1's 17%. 2. Near-term performance impacted by adjustments to align with regulatory compliance, particularly affecting train ticketing services. 3. Macro headwinds from rising energy prices and geopolitical tensions are driving up airfares and moderating travel demand.
rows.key_quote: Q2 outlook reflects rising energy prices... and the near-term impact of upgrading our operational practices to align with updated compliance frameworks.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Very strong net book-to-bill of 1.42x, driven by $3.3B in gross bookings (up 22% YoY) and low cancellations. 
2. Net business wins increased 42% year-over-year to $2.88 billion, indicating strong future revenue potential.
3. Secured key strategic wins, including a new central labs partnership with a top 5 pharma customer and a new partnership with a midsized pharma company.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Adjusted EBITDA margin compressed to 15.6% from 19.8% YoY due to revenue decline and unfavorable mix shift to FSP.
2. Adjusted gross margin fell significantly to 24.4% from 28.4% in the prior year quarter.
3. Revenue declined 1.9% on a constant currency basis, reflecting the lag from previously elevated cancellations and challenging demand.
rows.key_quote: Revenue declined 1.9% constant currency, reflecting challenging prior demand dynamics, including elevated cancellations in earlier periods.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Revenue beat guidance, growing 4.4% YoY to $1 billion, led by North America Contract (+6.9%) and Global Retail (+5.5%).
2. North America Contract adjusted operating margin expanded 40 bps YoY to 10.4%, driven by higher volume and effective price realization.
3. Issued positive FY27 guidance, projecting 5% revenue growth and 7.5% adjusted EPS growth at the midpoints.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Adjusted EPS declined to $0.55 from $0.60 in the prior year, an 8.3% decrease.
2. International Contract segment sales fell 3.8% and adjusted operating margin dropped 470 bps due to macro uncertainty and deleverage.
3. Consolidated orders fell 6.3% YoY, and the underperformance of the Holly Hunt brand negatively impacted Global Retail margins.
rows.key_quote: Prior year orders included $55 million to $60 million of pull forward ahead of price increases in our North America Contract segment.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Meaningful progress on the Donlin Gold bankable feasibility study (BFS) with major contractors, targeting completion in 2027.
2. Strong treasury position, being well-funded to complete the BFS and cover corporate G&A for at least the next 12 months.
3. Advancement of project financing strategy, with the selection of financial advisors underway and an announcement anticipated 'in the coming weeks'.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Continued cash expenditure with a net loss of CAD 25.5 million and a treasury decrease of CAD 22.3 million to fund development.
2. Ongoing permitting uncertainty, with a pending decision from the Alaska Supreme Court on water certification and a supplemental EIS in progress.
3. Increased G&A expenses compared to the prior year, driven by higher professional fees, share-based compensation, and employee compensation.
rows.key_quote: Fluor Corporation is coordinating all specialized contracts with a single consolidated execution framework to improve schedule efficiency and cost accuracy.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong top-line growth with record annual revenue of $839 million (up 10.9%) and record annual orders, ending the year with a $356 million backlog. 2. Significant profit expansion, with Q4 adjusted EPS up 50% to $0.27 and Q4 gross margin rising to 28%, driven by pricing actions and efficiency gains. 3. Broad-based order strength across key segments, including a 24% increase in Transportation orders and winning all 5 available Major League Baseball stadium bids.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. The Commercial business unit was the only segment that did not grow orders in fiscal 2026, remaining 'relatively stable'. 2. Anticipated headwinds from input costs, citing tariff uncertainty as a risk requiring active margin management through strategic sourcing and pricing. 3. Cash from operations declined to $49.2 million for the year from $97.7 million in the prior year, with some working capital consumed in Q4 due to project payment timing.
rows.key_quote: Q4 gross profit margin rose...driven by stronger revenue conversion, operating leverage, manufacturing expense discipline and working capital efficiency improvements.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Q4 revenue grew 12% to $1.6B and adj. EPS grew 11% to $1.32, with organic growth accelerating each quarter of the year. 
2. PEO worksite employee growth was in high single-digits, outpacing the industry, while ASO engagements increased by over 60%. 
3. The Paycor acquisition exceeded synergy targets, contributing over 50 basis points to revenue growth and over $100 million in cost synergies.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. FY27 guidance includes a headwind from Interest on funds held for clients, expected to decline to $195M-$205M due to rate changes and lapping gains. 
2. The health and benefits insurance agency continues to be a slight drag on the PEO and Insurance segment's overall growth rate. 
3. Overall client count growth remains relatively flat, with the company focusing on acquiring and retaining higher-value clients rather than total unit growth.
rows.key_quote: Management Solutions revenue grew 14%... driven by product penetration, price realization, and approximately 8 percentage points of growth from Paycor.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record-breaking Q3 results: Revenue of $41.5B (up 346% YoY), gross margin of 84.9% (up 10 pts sequentially), and EPS of $25.11, all exceeding guidance.
2. Transformative Strategic Customer Agreements (SCAs): Signed 16 multi-year, take-or-pay contracts backed by $22B in customer deposits, providing unprecedented revenue and margin stability with floor prices set to deliver margins 'well above' prior peaks.
3. Exceptionally strong forward outlook: Guided Q4 revenue to a record $50B and EPS to $31, while extending the view of tight market conditions beyond calendar 2027.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Severe supply constraints: Management has 'no line of sight as to when memory supply will be able to catch up with increasing demand' due to long lead times for new fabs.
2. Rising cost structure: The company projects the 'blended DRAM cost per bit to rise from current levels' due to tech transitions and new greenfield capacity ramps.
3. Server content moderation: Customers are focusing on maximizing server unit shipments amid tight memory supply, leading to a 'modest reduction in average server DRAM content growth'.
rows.key_quote: The floor price [in SCAs] enables a very robust gross margin for Micron, well above our peak quarterly margins in any past cycle.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong FEC growth: Q4 revenue up 14% and adjusted operating income up 13%, driven by a focus on high-yield B2B segments. 
2. B2B vertical success: Profitable share gains in key verticals like healthcare (now a ~$10B business) and the emerging AI/data center ecosystem, which is seeing double-digit revenue growth. 
3. Confident future outlook: Initiated strong CY26 guidance for ~11% revenue growth and Adj. EPS of $16.90-$18.10, implying 20% growth in the transition period.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Consolidated margin compression: Q4 consolidated revenue grew 13% while adjusted operating income grew only 3%, reflecting pressure from higher variable compensation and fuel cost impacts.
2. FedEx Freight drag: Declining results at the now spun-off FedEx Freight division were a nearly $400M headwind to full-year adjusted operating income.
3. Stranded costs: The company will carry ~$350M in stranded costs from the Freight spin-off into CY26, with only ~$100M expected to be removed during the year.
rows.key_quote: Our results demonstrate that we are growing revenue in the most premium segments of the global economy.

rows.positive_highlights:
1) Record Q2 Performance: Achieved all-time high records for revenues, yields, EBITDA, net income, and customer deposits ($9 billion).
2) Exceptional Cost Control: Q2 cruise costs without fuel were flat YoY, outperforming guidance by 250 basis points and contributing $0.05/share to the beat.
3) Strong Capital Management: Repurchased $450 million in stock, continued deleveraging (Net Debt/EBITDA down to 3.1x), and invested in growth projects.
rows.negative_highlights:
1) Lowered Yield Guidance: Full-year yield growth guidance was revised down by ~1 percentage point due to the impact of the Middle East conflict on European bookings.
2) Demand Moderation in Europe: The guidance change was driven by a booking slowdown concentrated in European deployments, particularly the Mediterranean region.
3) Back-Half Occupancy Pressure: Management lowered Q3 occupancy expectations for Europe by 'a couple of points' to prioritize long-term price integrity.
rows.key_quote: The primary driver of our outperformance was exceptional cost discipline... outperforming our March guidance by approximately 250 basis points.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Technology empowerment business transaction volume reached RMB 1.52 billion, a sequential increase of 67.6%. 2. International business grew, with loan volume up 20% sequentially in Indonesia and 35% in Mexico. 3. AI integration improved development efficiency by around 20% and customer service intent recognition accuracy from 78% to 93%.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Transaction volume decreased 45.8% YoY to RMB 19.3 billion. 2. Recorded a net loss of RMB 61.7 million, a sharp reversal from a RMB 539.5 million net income in Q1 2025. 3. The 90+ day delinquency ratio increased sequentially to 2.25%.
rows.key_quote: There's a faster decrease in loan volume than the decrease in cost reduction, so that explains most of the difference in the loss.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strategic Shift to BTO: 73% of Q2 net orders were Built-to-Order, providing visibility and predictability on future margins before construction starts.
2. Backlog and Production Improvements: Backlog grew 26% sequentially, backlog is expected to grow YoY in Q3, and build times were reduced to a decade-low 100 days.
3. H2 Margin Expansion Drivers: Expect significant margin improvement from increased operating leverage, higher BTO mix, and a favorable shift to high-margin Northern California communities.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant YoY Declines: Revenue down 27%, EPS down 71% (to $0.43 from $1.50), and housing gross margin down 410 bps (to 15.2% from 19.3%).
2. Weak Spring Watching Season: A net absorption rate of only 4 orders per month due to low consumer confidence, high mortgage rates, and affordability pressures.
3. Reduced Lot Count: Total lot count has declined over 20% from its peak, raising analyst questions about the community count pipeline for 2027-2028.
rows.key_quote: Crucially, we know the margin we will achieve at delivery before we start. We view this as a fundamentally lower risk profile than a speculative model.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Fifth consecutive quarter of growth: Consolidated fee revenue grew 7% to $760 million, demonstrating the strength of the diversified business model.
2. Successful cross-watching strategy: Business referrals increased to 29.1% of fee revenue, indicating deeper client penetration from the "We Are Korn Ferry" initiative.
3. Strong segment performance: Professional Search & Interim revenue grew 14%, Consulting grew 7%, and Executive Search grew 7%, showing broad-based strength.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Slowing new business: New business ex-RPO grew only 2%, which management directly attributed to the war in the Middle East impacting EMEA and APAC.
2. Weaker sequential guidance: Q1 revenue ($725M-$745M) and EPS ($1.32-$1.38) are guided lower than Q4 results, signaling near-term headwinds.
3. Flat EBITDA margin: Adjusted EBITDA margin remained flat at 17% despite strong revenue growth, as higher bonus expense offset potential gains.
rows.key_quote: Yeah. it is a little thing called the war. So, the Middle East. It definitely had an impact in a big way on new business.

rows.positive_highlights:
