1. Exceptional fuel gross margins due to market volatility and supply chain capabilities, with the U.S. margin at $0.5244 per gallon. 
2. Strong U.S. same-store sales growth of 3.4%, the best in three years, which included positive customer traffic growth. 
3. Robust growth in key categories, including U.S. Fresh Food Fast sales up over 10% and Packaged Beverages up nearly 6%, driving merchandise margin expansion.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Same-store fuel volumes declined in key markets, down 2.1% in the U.S. and 4.4% in Europe, due to high prices weighing on demand. 
2. Canada same-store sales declined by 0.9%, primarily due to persistent pressure in tobacco and modern nicotine categories. 
3. The Netherlands market remained under pressure, lapping prior-year tobacco-related benefits which negatively impacted European comparisons.
rows.key_quote: When volatility exists, we are well positioned to capture the advantages there and margin that becomes available with that volatility.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Organic revenue growth of 8% (10% excluding Type 31 reversal) beat mid-single digit guidance, led by strong performance in Nuclear and Aviation sectors. 2. Operating margin expanded 70bps to 8.2%, with all sectors improving profitability, showing progress towards the 9%+ medium-term target. 3. Strong free cash flow of GBP 262M (84% conversion) supported a 15% dividend increase and a new GBP 200M share buyback program.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Took a GBP 140 million charge on the Type 31 frigate program due to higher-than-expected rework and rectification costs. 2. Land sector revenue declined 3% organically due to weaker performance in civil businesses (rail and South African vehicles). 3. The company was unsuccessful in its bid for a frigate contract in Sweden, which was decided on geopolitical rather than industrial grounds.
rows.key_quote: We've reconfirmed the medium-term guidance... whilst absorbing the Type 31 charge.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strategic M&A and TAM Expansion: Announced acquisition of Dragos and others to triple the OT security addressable market and launched 'Accenture Edge' to target the $240B mid-market segment.
2. Strong AI and Large Deal Momentum: Secured 104 clients with over $100M in bookings year-to-date, a 13% increase, with clients moving to larger AI transformation programs.
3. Robust Profitability and Shareholder Returns: Expanded operating margin by 20 bps to 17%, grew EPS by 9%, and increased full-year forecast for shareholder returns to at least $9.5 billion.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Middle East Conflict Headwind: Experienced a $100 million negative revenue impact from the conflict, entirely within consulting, causing indirect weakness globally in the quarter's final weeks.
2. Delayed Managed Services Deals: A few large managed services opportunities were pushed from FY26 into FY27 for client-specific reasons, impacting bookings.
3. Q4 Outlook Uncertainty: Provided a wide Q4 revenue growth guidance range of 1% to 5%, reflecting increased macro uncertainty from recent geopolitical events.
rows.key_quote: We saw a revenue impact of approximately $100 million from the Middle East conflict, which was all consulting type of work.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. eCommerce achieved profitability ahead of schedule, growing 19% and driven by improved store-based fulfillment. 2. Gained significant market share against traditional grocers, with the 'best performance against Circana's Rest of Market in over three years'. 3. Cost savings initiatives are exceeding targets, with COGS savings '30% ahead of our plan' in Q1, funding price investments.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Gross margin declined 9 bps, impacted by an unexpected 15 bps headwind from higher transportation costs. 2. Identical sales growth was constrained by major pharmacy headwinds, totaling a 170 basis point drag from the Inflation Reduction Act and the shift to generic drugs. 3. Consumers are under pressure from gas prices and lower SNAP benefits, with food-at-home market growth decelerating 100 bps.
rows.key_quote: Taking costs out of this business is not optional. It's the starting point for everything else we want to do.

rows.positive_highlights: EPS surged to $0.18 from $0.05 YoY, driven by higher Time Charter Equivalent (TCE) rates ($17,095 vs $14,655) and lower daily vessel OpEx (down 9%). The quarterly dividend was increased to $0.06/share. The outlook is positive, with dry bulk demand growth (3%) forecast to outpace supply growth (2%) in 2026.
rows.negative_highlights: Downside risks include potential softening of Chinese iron ore import demand in H2 2026. Global long-term coal demand is projected to decline, although currently supported by short-term factors. The market remains exposed to geopolitical volatility, particularly related to the Strait of Hormuz.
rows.key_quote: supply growth is expected to be 2%, versus demand growth of 3% for 2026.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Retail segment sales grew 9%, driven by acquisitions and new stores, with its adjusted operating margin strengthening to 13.9%.
2. Strong balance sheet with $303M in cash and no debt, generating $204M in operating cash flow and authorizing a new $300M share buyback.
3. Consolidated adjusted gross margin increased 230 basis points, and adjusted operating margin of 9.9% exceeded guidance, driven by retail mix and a one-time gain in the divested case goods unit.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Joybird business sales declined 10% on lower volume, resulting in a $20M non-cash goodwill impairment charge.
2. Underlying demand remains soft, with written same-store sales down 2% for the quarter, despite sequential improvement and positive trends in April/May.
3. Q1 margin guidance of 4.0%-5.5% reflects pressure from short-term inflation, supply chain project costs, and seasonal slowness.
rows.key_quote: Total written sales for our company-owned retail segment increased 11% versus last year's fourth quarter, driven by acquired and new stores.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. SG&A Leverage: Expenses decreased 4% YoY, resulting in $118 per unit leverage and keeping the company on track for its $200M savings target. 2. CAF Penetration Growth: CarMax Auto Finance penetration increased 150 basis points to 43.3% as it expanded into the Tier 2 credit spectrum. 3. Sales Momentum: Slight retail unit growth was achieved against a strong prior-year comp, driven by a dynamic pricing strategy that balanced a GPU reduction of $230 (less than guided) with demand generation.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Gross Profit Decline: Total gross profit fell 4% and used retail margin decreased 10% due to a deliberate reduction in per-unit profitability. 2. EPS Decrease: Diluted EPS declined to $1.31 from $1.38 in the prior year, a 5.1% drop. 3. Negative Comp Sales: Used vehicle comparable store sales declined 0.8% year-over-year, indicating the slight unit growth was driven by other factors like new stores.
rows.key_quote: Our pricing algorithms are incorporating market demands and also unit demands specifically. We're understanding pricing by markets so we can be more dynamic.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Intelligent Infrastructure grew 21% YoY, driven by AI demand; FY26 AI revenue outlook raised by $500M to $13.6B (50% YoY growth). 2. Secured a third hyperscale customer, which is expected to ramp to a billion-dollar scale over time. 3. Raised full-year FY26 guidance for revenue (to $35B from $34B), core operating margin (to 5.8%), and free cash flow (to over $1.4B).
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Net inventory days of 68 were above the target range of 55-60 days due to shipment timing, though expected to normalize in Q4. 2. Management remains cautious on the Automotive market due to continued demand volatility, despite recent outperformance. 3. Noted potential supply chain constraints and extended lead times for key components like High Bandwidth Memory and high-density PCBs.
rows.key_quote: AI infrastructure demand remained extremely strong, and our full-year AI outlook is now meaningfully higher than what we laid out 90 days ago.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. AI & Data Analytics Growth: AI revenue grew from $23M in FY24 to $49M in FY26, with recurring revenue scaling from $1M to $8M and corporate customers increasing from 10 to 19.
2. Record Margin Expansion: Adjusted EBITDA margin rose 220 basis points to a record 26.2%, driven by a 15% reduction in corporate expenses and operational efficiencies.
3. Research Segment Strength & Strategic M&A: The core Research segment grew 4% with article output up 11%. The post-quarter acquisition of Emerald Publishing for ~$450M is expected to be accretive to EPS in year one.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Learning Segment Headwinds: Revenue declined with Academic down 5% and Professional down 10% due to soft consumer/corporate spending and adverse Amazon inventory practices.
2. Cash Flow Timing Shift: Free cash flow was moderated by late journal renewal signings, pushing some cash collections from Q4 FY26 into Q1 FY27.
3. Softness in Research Solutions: Research Solutions sub-segment declined 4% in Q4, impacted by a soft corporate spending environment affecting recruitment and marketing services.
rows.key_quote: Research publishing feeds the trusted content and data that accelerates AI and analytics growth. And AI, in turn, powers the intelligence and productivity.

rows.positive_highlights: Comparable food and beverage sales grew approximately 5%, marking the 9th straight month of positive comps for the segment. New, cheaper remodels are driving a strong 7% comp uplift at half the cost of legacy remodels. The company generated $25 million in FCF, an $84 million year-over-year improvement, and reiterated its guide for >$100 million in full-year FCF.
rows.negative_highlights: Same-store sales declined 5.4%, falling below both internal and external expectations. Macroeconomic headwinds, including softening consumer sentiment, negatively impacted results in April. The company's 'dollar per day' marketing message failed to resonate with customers, contributing to the weak performance.
rows.key_quote: Our same store sales growth declined 5.4%... we found that our dollar per day messaging did not resonate as strongly as we hoped.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Revenue Growth & Mix Shift: Q4 total revenue grew 11% YoY to $114.5M, led by a 14% growth in higher-margin services revenue, which now constitutes 81% of total revenue.
2. Significant Profitability Expansion: Q4 Adjusted EBITDA grew 42% YoY to $26.4M with margins of 23.1% (+5.1 pts YoY); GAAP operating income turned positive at $11M vs. a prior-year loss.
3. Major Contract Wins & Strategic Outlook: Secured a landmark $100M-$120M contract with South Africa's National Treasury and guided for FY27 Adj. EBITDA of $122M-$125M and $30M-$35M FCF.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Back-Half Weighted FY27: FY27 financial performance and FCF generation (~90%) are heavily weighted to the second half due to upfront investments and the timing of contract ramps.
2. Near-Term Margin Pressure: Q1 FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to be ~1 percentage point lower than Q4 FY26 due to investments in go-to-market and restructuring before savings are realized.
3. Significant Upfront Investment: FY27 guidance includes $52M in CapEx, with a significant portion related to the South Africa deal creating a large cash outflow in H1 before customer payments are received.
rows.key_quote: Services revenue totaled $92.9 million, up 14% year-over-year, and now represents more than 81% of total revenue.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Gross retention improved significantly, up 240 basis points year-over-year to 86.7%.
2. Customers on consumption-based pricing showed strong metrics, with 92% gross retention and 108% net retention.
3. Achieved positive non-GAAP operating margin of 5.6% and operating income of $4.4 million, demonstrating operating discipline.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Breached minimum ARR covenant on its debt facility, forcing the debt to be reclassified as current; company is operating under a forbearance agreement.
2. Subscription revenue declined 2% year-over-year to $69.8 million.
3. Company suspended financial guidance and cancelled the Q&A session due to being in advanced negotiations for a strategic transaction.
rows.key_quote: The minimum ARR covenant under the existing facility was not met for the quarter, requiring us to classify the debt as current.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Sales incentive rate declined to 12.9% from 14.1% in Q1, the first 'potentially sustainable decline' in three years. 2. Operational efficiencies drove record-low construction cycle time of 121 days and reduced construction costs per square foot by 7% YoY to $81. 3. Gross margin improved sequentially to 15.6%, with guidance for further improvement to ~16% in Q3.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Lowered full-year delivery guidance to 82,000-83,000 homes, citing interest rate pressures and macro uncertainty. 2. Management described the macro environment as 'complicated and erratic,' with stubbornly high mortgage rates and a fresh inflation spike. 3. Consumer demand is inconsistent and lacks urgency, impacted by affordability challenges and anxieties about the economy and employment.
rows.key_quote: Our sales incentive rate on deliveries was 12.9% this quarter, down from 14.1%... the first real and potentially sustainable decline after three years.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Q1 revenue ($800.3M) and adjusted EBITDA (7.1%) exceeded the high end of expectations.
2. Raised full-year 2026 outlook to 4.5%-8.0% revenue growth, citing Q1 outperformance.
3. The new RH Estates concept is expected to contribute 5 percentage points of growth in the second half of the year.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Backorder and special order balances are $75M higher than a year ago, delaying revenue recognition.
2. International expansion is causing significant margin pressure, with a negative 270 bps impact guided for the full-year adjusted EBITDA.
3. Management is not counting on any improvement in the housing market, acknowledging the difficult economic environment.
rows.key_quote: A 5% incremental move on a on Estates is really conservative.

rows.positive_highlights: Accelerating utility demand: "Conversations have moved from education and evaluation to now being anchored on deployment pricing, and time to value." Strong financial execution: The company achieved a "net income and EPS positive year" and collected $127 million in cash, far exceeding its $80 million expectation. New strategic opportunities: Successfully completed initial tests with Link Global to explore direct-to-device (D2D) satellite capabilities, opening new potential markets.
rows.negative_highlights: Uncertainty on new product revenue: Management noted it is "a little early" to provide a financial model for new recurring revenue products like CatalyX. Rising operating expenses: Guided FY27 OpEx to "approximately $40 million OpEx at the most", an increase from the recent $37-38 million run-rate. Lumpy and unpredictable gains: CFO declined to guide on quarterly gains from spectrum sales due to the material impact of unpredictable FCC license timing.
rows.key_quote: Conversations have moved from education and evaluation to now being anchored on deployment pricing, and time to value.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Take 5 Oil Change segment grew system-wide sales 14%, same-store sales 4.5%, and expanded adjusted EBITDA margins by 120 basis points to 33.9%.
2. Net leverage was reduced to 3.2x, keeping the company on track to meet its 3.0x year-end target.
3. The Franchise segment delivered robust 60% adjusted EBITDA margins and saw a positive inflection in same-store sales growth to 0.9%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Management is observing traffic moderation from newer customers and value-oriented households (earning <$50k), prompting a cautious Q2 sales outlook.
2. Significant restatement costs ($9.1M in Q1, expected to exceed $15M in Q2) are pressuring reported EBITDA margins.
3. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin declined 140 basis points to 21.5% due to restatement costs, with further pressure expected in Q2.
rows.key_quote: We are monitoring some moderation in traffic among newer customers and more value-oriented customers, particularly households earning less than $50,000 annually.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong growth in high-value transactions, with mid-double-digit growth in orders over $6,000. 2. E-commerce sales grew 7.1% year-over-year, increasing channel penetration by 170 basis points. 3. High attachment rate for new products, with the Reclining Seat included in nearly one-third of configurations.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Gross margin decreased 160 basis points to 52.1%, driven by a 380 basis point headwind from inbound transport and tariff costs. 2. Weak demand for lower-priced products, with continued softness in transactions under $6,000. 3. Sactional and Sacs sales decreased by 1.4% and 22.5% respectively, contributing to flat overall revenue (-0.1%).
rows.key_quote: We've experienced mid double-digit growth in our over $6,000 transactions.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Raised full-year revenue and non-GAAP EPS guidance, citing strong H1 results and the SEMrush acquisition. 2. Massive user growth in freemium products; Creative Freemium MAU grew from 50M to 90M YoY. 3. Strong AI momentum with AI-first ARR tripling YoY to over $500 million, and Firefly ARR growing 50% QoQ.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Lowered second-half ARR growth expectations due to a strategic pivot to a freemium user acquisition model. 2. Deferred previously planned Creative Cloud price optimizations, removing a near-term revenue lever. 3. Leadership uncertainty with both the CEO and CFO roles in transition.
rows.key_quote: Early success of Firefly and Acrobat AI gives us conviction to aggressively serve new users with a friction free freemium journey.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Gross margin expanded 50 basis points YoY to 27.2%, driven by private label growth, sourcing optimization, and disciplined pricing.
2. Strong growth in strategic initiatives, with treatment plant solutions delivering double-digit growth and smart utility solutions delivering high single-digit growth.
3. Accelerated capital returns, with $125 million in share repurchases fiscal year-to-date, representing approximately 80% of the total for all of fiscal 2025.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Overall end-market demand declined by low single digits, with net sales flat and organic volumes down approximately 1% year-over-year.
2. Residential markets remain challenged with year-over-year declines, driven by slower lot development activity compared to a strong prior year.
3. Non-residential markets were mixed, with strength in data centers offset by softness in light commercial construction like retail and office projects.
rows.key_quote: We expanded gross margins 50 basis points year-over-year, driven by continued growth in private label, sourcing optimization and disciplined pricing execution.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Revenue grew 4.7% YoY, driven by an 11th straight quarter of Fix AOV growth from larger fixes and higher AUR.
2. Active clients grew sequentially to 2.3M, retention hit a 4-year high, and new client LTV has nearly doubled in 3 years.
3. Adjusted EBITDA of $13.2M beat guidance, leading to raised full-year estimates; company generated positive free cash flow and repurchased shares.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Management cited an "increasingly challenged consumer environment" and "macroeconomic uncertainty" as external headwinds.
2. A sequential active client decline of 0.5% to 1.0% is expected in Q4 due to seasonality.
3. Inventory grew 15.6% year-over-year, outpacing revenue growth.
rows.key_quote: Fixed average order value (AOV) increased for the 11th straight quarter, primarily due to higher items per fix from expanded adoption of larger fixes.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. New-to-brand customer acquisition saw slight YoY growth; these new customers are younger than the average and have a higher AOV. 2. Specific product categories like jackets and accessories performed well, with accessories showing 'strong growth'. 3. Early Q2 trends for the summer assortment are positive, with strong full-price watching on colorful items, indicating product evolution is starting to resonate.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Total company sales declined 6% and comparable sales fell 8.7%, driven by soft conversion. 2. Gross margin dropped 350 basis points to 68.3%, pressured by $4.7 million in net tariff costs and higher markdowns. 3. The direct (e-commerce) channel underperformed, with sales down 8% due to consumer price sensitivity leading to a higher mix of markdown sales.
rows.key_quote: In terms of key learnings, tops assortment skewed too far into shorter length and did not offer enough breadth in print.

rows.positive_highlights:
1) Record Profitability: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 7.5%, up 130 bps YoY, with a strong flow-through greater than 25%, driven by sponsored ads and efficiencies. 
2) Strong Autoship Growth: Autoship customer sales grew over 10% YoY, reaching 84.4% of total net sales, showcasing the durable recurring revenue base. 
3) Chewy Health/Vet Care Expansion: Acquired Modern Animal, accelerating clinic expansion to an expected ~60 clinics by year-end, which act as a powerful acquisition channel for high-value customers ($900 Year 1 NSPAC).
rows.negative_highlights:
1) Lowered Full-Year Revenue Guidance: Cut FY26 sales expectations, citing a more challenged consumer environment and removing the assumption of a back-half spending acceleration. 
2) Slowing Customer Spend (NSPAC): Management explicitly cited "a modest level of incremental pressure on premiumization and product attach rates," creating a "short-term NSPAC headwind." 
3) Weakening Macro Environment: The company stated the "consumer environment has become incrementally more challenged" than initially anticipated, particularly impacting discretionary purchasing behavior.
rows.key_quote: We are seeing modest incremental pressure on premiumization and product attach rates amongst our customer base, resulting in a short-term NSPAC headwind.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Massive AI Demand: Signed $67 billion in AI infrastructure contracts in Q4, leading to a record Remaining Performance Obligation (RPO) of $638 billion (+363%). 2. Explosive OCI Growth: Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) revenue grew 93%, demonstrating successful execution and capacity delivery. 3. Strong Future Guidance: Forecasts 34% revenue growth for FY27, well above long-term targets, providing exceptional visibility.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Gross Margin Pressure: Gross margin declined and is expected to step down further in FY27 due to the high upfront costs of ramping new data centers. 2. Heavy Capital Intensity: Announced a massive $70 billion net cash outlay for CapEx in FY27, requiring significant investment to fulfill demand. 3. Slower Apps Growth: Cloud Apps grew 10%, a solid but much slower pace compared to the hypergrowth in the infrastructure business.
rows.key_quote: We signed $67 billion in AI infrastructure contract this quarter, the majority of which was either bring your own hardware or prepaid.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Q4 fuel margin of $0.469/gallon, up $0.093 from prior year, was the primary driver of a 66% increase in diluted EPS to $4.37.
2. Strong inside same-store sales growth of +5.5% driven by a healthy balance of traffic (+3%) and ticket (+2.5%), with significant margin expansion in both prepared foods (+170bps) and grocery (+90bps).
3. Issued strong FY27 guidance for 8-10% EBITDA growth, supported by plans for 120 new stores and continued momentum from strategic initiatives.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Management guided to flattish same-store fuel gallons for FY27 (-1% to +1%), suggesting minimal volume growth expectations at the pump.
2. Full-year operating expenses are guided to increase 5% to 7%, with Q1 OpEx expected to grow in the high-single digits, outpacing the low end of inside sales guidance.
3. The record-high Q4 fuel margin creates a very difficult comparison for the fourth quarter of FY27, which management acknowledged as a factor in its planning.
rows.key_quote: The volatility on the way up...enabled us to capture a bit more margin than we might have otherwise done.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Massive AI Infrastructure Bookings: Signed $67 billion in AI infrastructure contracts in Q4, driving Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO) up 363% to $638 billion. 2. Explosive Cloud Infrastructure Growth: Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) revenue grew 93% in Q4, reflecting immense demand for AI workloads. 3. Extremely Strong Forward Guidance: Issued FY2027 full-year revenue growth guidance of +34% and Q1 FY27 guidance of +27% to +29%, well above typical growth rates.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Gross Margin Compression: Reported and full-year gross margins declined due to the high costs of ramping up new data centers ahead of revenue recognition. This pressure is expected to continue in FY27. 2. Massive Capital Expenditure and Financing: Announced a net CapEx outlay of ~$70 billion for FY27 and plans to raise ~$40 billion in debt and equity to fund the expansion. 3. Slower Cloud Apps Growth: Cloud applications grew 10%, a solid but much slower rate compared to the hyper-growth in infrastructure, highlighting the company's increasing reliance on OCI for growth.
rows.key_quote: We signed $67 billion in AI infrastructure contracts this quarter, the majority of which was either bring your own hardware or prepaid.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Tommy Bahama Strength: The largest brand delivered mid-single-digit positive DTC comps, driven by a 7.5% increase in its women's DTC business.
2. Gross Margin Resilience: Operational improvements in sourcing and pricing helped offset an $11 million tariff headwind, leading to an EPS beat.
3. Johnny Was Turnaround: The brand improved gross margin through tighter inventory and reduced promotions as part of its ongoing turnaround plan.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Lilly Pulitzer Underperformance: The brand's sales were significantly below expectations due to internal merchandising and execution issues, weighing on overall results.
2. Slowing Consumer Demand: Management noted sales trends softened in late Q1 and early Q2, leading to a more cautious view and lowered revenue guidance.
3. Gross Margin Contraction: Consolidated adjusted gross margin decreased 90 basis points to 63.4%, driven by a 280 basis point headwind from capitalized tariffs.
rows.key_quote: The positive comps at Tommy Bahama and growth in emerging brands were offset by sales declines at Lilly Pulitzer and Johnny Was.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Returned to positive comp growth of 2.9%, with total sales up 6.7%.
2. Outdoor category was the top performer, growing 12%, driven by a turnaround in the ammo business.
3. E-commerce sales grew by 17%, contributing over 100bps to comp, and new stores in the comp base performed strongly with high-single-digit comps.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Gross margin declined 71 bps to 33.2%, driven by a 110 bps negative impact from tariffs.
2. Management noted persistent consumer pressure from high gas prices, causing a slowdown to a 'roughly flat comp' at the start of Q2.
3. The company anticipates a cautious consumer who is increasingly shopping only during promotional periods.
rows.key_quote: Outdoor was our best performing category and up 12% driven by strength in fishing and shooting sports categories as our ammo business turned positive.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Brand Portfolio segment sales grew 19%, driven by strong performance in key brands like Topo (+32%), Jessica Simpson (+35%), and Keds (+35%). 2. Consolidated gross margin expanded by 240 basis points due to structural changes in inventory management, pricing, and disciplined sourcing. 3. Adjusted EPS of $0.07 beat expectations, prompting management to guide full-year EPS toward the high end of the initial range.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Consolidated comparable sales declined 1.1%, with the Retail segment impacted by unfavorable weather that dampened seasonal sales. 2. Softness was observed in the casual and athletic footwear categories as consumer preferences shifted towards fashion. 3. Management flagged future headwinds, including expected earnings pressure in Q3 and uncertainty surrounding potential new Section 301 tariffs.
rows.key_quote: Margin improvement... is being driven by structural changes we've made across inventory management, pricing, disciplined sourcing and channel profitability.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Profitability: Adjusted EBITDA grew nearly 17% to $183M, with margins expanding 40 bps, driven by network optimization and operational efficiencies.
2. Deleveraging and Cash Flow: Generated $54M in free cash flow, improving the net leverage ratio by 0.8x YoY to 2.5x and reducing net debt to its lowest point since 2018.
3. Operational Gains: Increased DC productivity by over 7%, improved on-time deliveries by 4%, and reduced miles per delivery by nearly 5% through technology and lean initiatives.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Revenue Decline: Net sales fell 4.2% to $7.7B, primarily due to a deliberate 450 basis point impact from "accretive optimization" actions to exit less profitable business.
2. Retail Segment Weakness: Sales in the company's retail segment (Cub) declined 10% due to store closures, with same-store sales down 4%.
3. External Headwinds: Management is factoring in pressure for Q4 from rising fuel costs and noted ongoing consumer strain from reduced SNAP funding and inflation.
rows.key_quote: "...a decline of 4.2% to last year, which includes an impact of approximately 450 basis points from our accretive optimization actions."

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Commenced production at Burke Hollow, the largest U.S. greenfield ISR uranium project in over a decade, with production expected in Q4.
2. Received regulatory approval for expanded production at Christensen Ranch (3 new header houses), setting the stage for higher Q4 production.
3. Maintained a strong balance sheet with $794 million in liquid assets, $488 million in cash, and no debt, supporting its unhedged sales strategy.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Cost per pound increased significantly to $54.61 due to regulatory delays pushing out production volumes from new wellfields.
2. The company generated no revenue, as it intentionally made no sales during the quarter to preserve inventory.
3. Existing well production declined, and overall Q3 production was only 32,000 pounds, impacted by the timing of new wellfield approvals.
rows.key_quote: Cost per pound did increase...a temporary and largely a timing related event. Regulatory approvals delayed production from new header houses.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. The 'core' portfolio, representing nearly 65% of portfolio value, was the primary growth driver, delivering an exceptional 26% return. 2. A post-period end funding round for portfolio company ICEYE increased its valuation significantly, implying a ~15% (117p) uplift to Molten's NAV per share. 3. Strong realization activity continued, with all exits at or above holding value and a post-period partial sale of Revolut adding ~GBP 70M to the balance sheet.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. The 'emerging' portfolio recorded a net valuation writedown, driven by issues at three specific companies, including Robin AI and Schuttflix. 2. Within the core portfolio, CoachHub was written down due to a slowdown in its growth. 3. Management continues to focus on narrowing the significant discount of the company's share price relative to its Net Asset Value (NAV).
rows.key_quote: So it's the core that's really driven the fair value returns... That 26% is much more what you would expect again for venture returns.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Cost Management & EBITDA Beat: Exceeded EBITDA expectations due to disciplined cost savings in G&A, advertising, and operations (food waste), leading to a significant raise in full-year EBITDA guidance to $120-$125M. 
2. Retail Turnaround: Retail comps outperformed restaurant comps for the first time in over 4 years, driven by SKU rationalization, improved merchandising, and strong sales in categories like toys and American Heritage items. 
3. Improved Guest Metrics & Loyalty Growth: Google star rating increased 4% and food/service scores rose 5%. The loyalty program grew to 12M members, accounting for over 40% of tracked sales and driving repeat visits.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Persistent Traffic Decline: Despite improving trends, comparable restaurant traffic was still down 6.7% year-over-year, leading to a 2.6% decline in comparable restaurant sales. 
2. Pressure on Lower-Income Consumers: Management acknowledged that the lower-income consumer segment remains pressured, a persistent headwind for the brand. 
3. Labor Cost Deleverage: Labor and related expenses increased by 80 basis points as a percentage of revenue, primarily due to sales deleverage from the traffic decline.
rows.key_quote: This performance was driven by strong cost management across the P and L. As well as improved traffic and check.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Reaffirmed strong full-year revenue guidance of RMB 600 million, signaling significant expected ramp-up in the remaining three quarters. 
2. Major positive shift in the regulatory environment, with China formally establishing the "low-altitude economy" as a strategic national industry with a solid legal foundation. 
3. Successful revenue diversification, with the Aerial Media business growing to contribute ~40% of Q1 revenue, offsetting weak eVTOL deliveries.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Weak Q1 eVTOL deliveries of only 4 units, a sharp sequential decline from 61 units in Q4 2025, attributed to seasonality and customer delivery timing. 
2. Widening operating loss, with adjusted operating loss at RMB 77.1 million, driven by increased spending on commercialization and R&D. 
3. The final CAAC approval for public, ticketed commercial operations remains pending, though the company states it is in the "final stage."
rows.key_quote: Our confidence is supported by our diversified revenue mix, continued global market progress, and the advancement of EH216-S commercial operations in China.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Completed transformational JV with WHP Global, using $300M in proceeds to eliminate term loan debt and significantly deleverage the balance sheet. 2. Strong underlying demand metrics despite negative headline results, including double-digit consumer traffic growth and 15% revenue growth in Europe. 3. Board authorized a new $100 million share repurchase program, enhancing capital return flexibility.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Revenue declined 9% year-over-year, primarily due to temporary shipment delays from a new warehouse management system rollout. 2. Gross margin decreased 410 basis points due to operational deleverage, new royalty payments to the JV, and tariff pressures. 3. Adjusted EBITDA fell to negative $6 million, a $16 million decrease from the prior year, reflecting the sales disruption and new cost structure.
rows.key_quote: Absent the temporary operational disruption from our DC upgrades, we had the orders needed to drive positive sales comps for the company.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Gross margin expanded 180 basis points to 17.1% due to stronger equipment margins and a higher mix of parts/service revenue.
2. Equipment margins improved 100 bps YoY to 7.8% sooner than expected due to successful efforts in clearing aged inventory.
3. Floorplan interest expense decreased 26% YoY, reflecting significant reductions in interest-bearing inventory levels.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Consolidated revenue decreased 12.1% (10.4% same-store) due to continued softness in equipment demand, especially in Domestic Ag.
2. The Domestic Ag environment remains very challenging for customers due to low commodity prices and high input costs, pressuring demand.
3. Europe segment revenue fell ~40% on a constant currency basis, reflecting softening demand after a prior-year subsidy program ended.
rows.key_quote: Equipment margin improvement arrived sooner than anticipated, and we view this as a direct result of the disciplined work...to clear aged inventory.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong EPS Guidance: The company projects $0.85 of EPS growth in FY27, driven by significant profit expansion in key segments.
2. Coffee Margin Recovery: Coffee profit is set to grow as the company laps prior-year tariffs and benefits from deflationary green coffee costs, with retail margins expected to return to the high 20s.
3. Hostess Profitability Turnaround: The Hostess business is stabilizing, with segment profit expected to grow ~30% in FY27 due to cost controls and a price increase.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Revenue Decline Forecast: Full-year net sales are expected to decline 3-4% due to passing on lower coffee prices to consumers.
2. Weakness in Spreads: The spreads business is under pressure from lapping promotional activity and is a drag on the Frozen Handheld & Spreads segment.
3. Segment Offsets: Profit growth in coffee and Hostess is partially offset by declines in the Frozen Handheld & Spreads and Pet segments, the latter of which is impacted by inflation.
rows.key_quote: $0.75 [of EPS growth] is coming through our portfolio which is driven by segment profit growth from both coffee and Hostess...

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Fire Services revenue grew 11% year-over-year to $23.4 million, with a historic-level open order backlog due to new NFPA product certifications.
2. Significant profitability improvement with net income of $0.4 million compared to a net loss of $3.9 million YoY, and adjusted EBITDA excluding FX up 79.6%.
3. Strong growth in the ISP (service) business, now running at a $4-5 million per quarter revenue rate, with expansion into new geographies and technologies like CO2 decontamination.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Adjusted gross margin declined to 33.6% from 35.2% YoY, impacted by unfavorable product mix (~150 bps), NFPA certification costs (~80 bps), and freight cost release (~70 bps).
2. US Industrial and disposable business remains weak, with no meaningful recovery yet seen in oil and gas turnaround activity.
3. Geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East has temporarily slowed project timing and frozen certain regional budgets.
rows.key_quote: new product demand growth that has outpaced our prior manufacturing and stock capacity. As a result, our open order backlog has risen to historic levels.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Lift revenue declined only 5% despite a 15% drop in visitation, demonstrating the stability of the advance commitment pass model. 2. Strategic lift ticket initiatives drove outperformance, with US lift ticket visitation down 12% vs. an estimated 20% decline for the rest of the industry. 3. Achieved record guest experience scores despite poor conditions, with year-over-year increases at every resort in the Rockies.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Historically poor weather in the Rockies (worst snowfall on record) drove an industry-wide visitation decline of 24% in the region and pressured results. 2. Full-year guidance was lowered, with Resort EBITDA now expected at $735M-$755M, reflecting the impact of weak late-season visitation. 3. Spring pass sales for the next season were soft, with units down 10% and dollars down 5% year-over-year due to the challenging prior season.
rows.key_quote: Our results were significantly impacted by weather... our destination resorts in the Rockies experienced the worst season on record for snowfall.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Meals & Beverages division performing well, driven by strength in Rao's and Pacific brands and the resilient at-home cooking trend.
2. The core business of the Goldfish brand has been stabilized after focused strategic efforts.
3. Actively implementing cost savings (accelerating $100M SG&A plan) and revenue growth management (RGM) to offset significant inflationary pressures.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Projecting significant forward inflation of 5-6% for fiscal 2027, driven by high oil prices and geopolitical conflict, creating major cost headwinds.
2. Snacks division EBIT margin remains "not acceptable," down ~400 basis points year-over-year, due to volume pressure and operational challenges.
3. Lowered full-year EPS guidance to "$2.20 to below" and guided revenue to the low end of the range, citing cost pressures and higher share count.
rows.key_quote: If oil stays around $100 a barrel, we're looking at an additional 2% to 3% inflation on top of the core 3%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Volume and Category Growth: Avocado volumes sold increased 15% YoY, and the category attracted 1.6 million new U.S. households during the quarter.
2. Calavo Acquisition Closed: Completed the Calavo acquisition, projecting a minimum of $25 million in annualized cost synergies within 18 months and enhancing operational scale.
3. Robust Second-Half Outlook: Expects significant margin recovery and guides for consolidated second-half adjusted EBITDA of $84 million to $88 million, supported by a large Peruvian crop.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant Margin Pressure: Gross margin fell to 7.0% due to an oversupplied market and a mismatch in fruit sizing in April, forcing higher-cost spot market purchases.
2. Revenue and Profitability Collapse: Revenue declined 24% to $290.9M due to a 36% drop in per-unit pricing, and adjusted EPS fell to $0.01 from $0.12 in the prior year.
3. Challenging Market Conditions: The quarter was shaped by an unusually high supply from the largest Mexican crop in years, resulting in multi-year low avocado prices.
rows.key_quote: "...unfavorable step change in our per unit margins driven by a temporary imbalance of supply and demand of core fruit sizes."

rows.positive_highlights: Pipeline expanded over 250% to 4 gigawatts, with 89% driven by AI data center demand. Planned manufacturing capacity is being increased to 500 MW from 350 MW to meet demand. Balance sheet was strengthened with $441 million in cash following recent capital raises.
rows.negative_highlights: Revenue decreased 5% year-over-year to $35.6 million. Posted a $77.6 million net loss, driven by a $42.6 million non-cash impairment charge on the Groton project. Total backlog declined to $1.14 billion from $1.26 billion year-over-year.
rows.key_quote: Our pipeline expanded over 250% to 4 gigawatts, with potential data center customers making up about 89%, reflecting a step change in power demand.

rows.positive_highlights: Revenue grew 49.7% to $52.8 million, successfully lapping a nearly $10 million non-repeating Costco promotion from the prior year, demonstrating strong underlying business momentum. Successfully launched over 12 new branded items at major retailers, including new entries into Walmart, Target, and Food Lion, with strong initial results. Completed the enterprise-wide ERP system integration across all 3 facilities ahead of schedule, enabling enhanced operational leverage and data visibility.
rows.negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 23.6% from 26.1% year-over-year, impacted by startup costs for new product launches. Profitability was pressured by an estimated $500k to nearly $1M in labor and raw material inefficiencies related to new items. An intentional shift of ~$500k from SG&A to trade promotion (contra-revenue) was made to support the new launches, further impacting gross margin.
rows.key_quote: We grew revenue 50% to $52.8 million... while successfully lapping without repeat a nearly $10 million digital Costco MVM in the prior year.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record first-half new sales bookings of $1.2B, indicating strong demand. 2. Strong organic revenue growth of 6.1%, driven by Technical Solutions (+22%) and Aviation (+20%). 3. The WGNSTAR acquisition is fueling high double-digit organic revenue growth in the critical semiconductor market.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Consolidated segment operating margin decreased 60 basis points year-over-year due to contract mix and acquisition amortization. 2. The Business & Industry segment was flat and is expected to decelerate due to a large UK client exit and weakness in West Coast commercial real estate. 3. Aviation segment margin was pressured by weather-related costs, operational disruptions, and new contract ramp-up expenses.
rows.key_quote: During the second quarter, we secured tens of millions in new business and delivered high double-digit organic revenue growth across our semiconductor market.

rows.positive_highlights: Net sales increased 2.2% to $462M, driven by favorable pricing, tariffs and FX. Custom Solutions segment volume grew approximately 1% YoY, indicating market share gains in a soft market. Management is implementing targeted price increases in Q3 to recover margins and expects strong H2 cash flow for debt repayment.
rows.negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 350 basis points YoY due to a significant lag in passing through sharp increases in raw material and logistics costs. Adjusted EPS fell ~60% to $0.25 from $0.63 YoY, and Adjusted EBITDA dropped 30% to $44.2M. Full-year 2026 guidance was withdrawn due to increased inflationary pressures and geopolitical uncertainty reducing visibility.
rows.key_quote: Gross margins declined 350-basis-points year over year in Q2, primarily due to sharp increases in raw materials and logistics costs.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Gross Margin Expansion: Non-GAAP gross margin improved by 350 basis points to 45.7% due to full-price watching, a shift to owned brands, and strong inventory control. 2. Owned Brand Strength: The 'go-forward' portfolio grew high single-digits, highlighted by Donna Karan's ~40% growth and DKNY's e-commerce growth of over 40%. 3. Raised EPS Guidance: Full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance was increased to $2.15-$2.25 from $2.00-$2.10, driven by better-than-expected profitability.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Revenue Decline: Net sales fell 8% to $536 million, driven by the anticipated loss of revenue from the exited PVH brand licenses. 2. Swing to Net Loss: Reported a non-GAAP net loss of $0.21 per share, compared to a net income of $0.19 per share in the prior year, partly due to SG&A investments. 3. European Market Weakness: Management noted the European market remains soft due to ongoing pressure on consumer sentiment.
rows.key_quote: Gross margin benefited from pricing actions...as well as the mix shift to higher-margin owned brands from licenses.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. CooperSurgical revenue grew 6% organically, driven by a 10% organic rebound in the fertility business. 2. Non-GAAP EPS grew 26% due to strong operating leverage from cost efficiency programs, particularly within CooperSurgical. 3. The strategic review for CooperSurgical is advancing with 'significant interest' following the settlement of a major product recall litigation.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. CooperVision's Asia-Pacific revenue declined 6% due to market softness in Japan and China, leading to a full-year CVI revenue guidance reduction. 2. The company now expects CooperVision's APAC revenue to decline again in Q3, with market weakness and product rationalization continuing to be headwinds. 3. Forward-looking gross margins are guided to decline to ~66% in Q3 due to unfavorable FX, tariffs, and lower production volumes.
rows.key_quote: The difference... is softness in the market itself. That Asia Pac market... is softer than we anticipated it was going to be.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised full-year outlook for subscription ARR to $1.854B-$1.862B (27% growth), total revenue, and non-GAAP EPS, citing strong demand.
2. Subscription ARR grew 32% to $1.57B, adding a record Q1 net new ARR of $103M; subscription net retention rate remained strong at ~120%.
3. Identity business showed exceptional momentum, growing 38% sequentially to exceed $50M in subscription ARR, disrupting the identity protection market.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. FY27 reported revenue growth faces a 'meaningful headwind' from a substantial reduction in material rights revenue as the cloud transition nears completion.
2. Management acknowledged a competitive landscape for AI governance, with analysts naming large vendors like ServiceNow as potential rivals for the 'AI control plane'.
3. The growth trajectory for the new Rubrik Agent Cloud remains uncertain, with management stating they 'can't predict the future' regarding its scaling pace.
rows.key_quote: Our Identity business grew 38% sequentially quarter-over-quarter to reach over 50 million in subscription ARR in Q1.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record revenue of $291M (up 50% YoY), driven by the Power segment's ramp-up on newly awarded gas-fired projects.
2. Gross margin improved to 21% from 19% YoY, reflecting strong execution and early completion of key projects (Midwest solar and Trumbull).
3. Strong demand outlook for gas-fired plants due to data center growth and electrification, with a robust project pipeline and expectation of new awards in 10-18 months.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Project backlog slightly decreased to $2.8B from $2.9B sequentially as revenue was recognized from large ongoing projects.
2. Demand for renewable projects has "softened," shifting the company's focus more heavily towards natural gas facilities.
3. Management acknowledges a potential time gap between the completion of current jobs and the commencement of new ones, creating some uncertainty in the timing of backlog replenishment.
rows.key_quote: Significant revenue growth in our Power segment [was] driven by the continued ramp-up of construction activities on our most recently awarded projects.

rows.positive_highlights: China revenue grew 30% (23% in constant currency) and full-year growth is still guided at approximately 20%. Men's category revenue increased 7%, outpacing women's growth of 4%. Inventory units are down 4%, providing flexibility to chase stronger-performing styles.
rows.negative_highlights: North America revenue declined 3% with comparable sales down 6%, driven by a drop-off in traffic. Gross margin fell 410 basis points due to tariff impacts and higher markdowns. Full-year revenue guidance was cut to flat to -1%, and EPS guidance was lowered by over 15% at the midpoint.
rows.key_quote: Two key factors impacting our trend... First, spikes of negative commentary... and second, not all of our product launches have met our expectations.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Revenue grew 40% YoY to $1.57B, driven by a 70% surge in direct cloud customer revenue fueled by AI demand. 
2. Secured the industry's first multi-rail (RLS Hyper-Rail) order from a leading hyperscaler, validating a key new product cycle.
3. Raised full-year revenue growth guidance to 32% and operating margin to ~19%, reflecting strong execution and a record $7.7B backlog.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Navigating a significant supply chain imbalance, with demand outpacing supply, particularly for components like pump lasers and modems.
2. Raised full-year operating expense guidance to ~$1.61B due to higher variable compensation and investments in supply security.
3. Backlog growing to a record $7.7B indicates revenue is currently capped by supply capacity, as customers would accept faster delivery if possible.
rows.key_quote: Direct cloud customer revenue grew 70%, driven by strong demand for our RLS and Waveserver product lines, both up over 55% year-on-year.

rows.positive_highlights:
Brand Portfolio Strength: Organic sales grew 5.8%, with lead brands up 7% and Allen Edmonds up nearly 20%.
Significant Gross Margin Expansion: Consolidated gross margin increased 200 bps to 47.3%, driven by a 520 bps expansion in the Brand Portfolio segment to 49%.
Strategic Initiatives Successful: The new FLAIR store format at Famous Footwear provided a 7-point sales lift, and the newly integrated Stuart Weitzman brand exceeded internal sales and profit expectations.
rows.negative_highlights:
Famous Footwear Weakness: Sales declined 2.5% and comparable sales fell 2.3% amid a softer consumer backdrop.
Famous Footwear Margin Compression: Gross margin for the segment fell 150 bps due to higher markdowns and clearance activity.
Macroeconomic Headwinds: Management cited accelerated inflation as a key pressure on consumer traffic and sales, particularly impacting the Famous Footwear business in April.
rows.key_quote: Earnings per share exceeded our guidance, driven by strong sales and gross margin results in the Brand Portfolio segment.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Core comparable sales (excluding footwear) grew 1.2%, driven by strength in knit tops, bottoms, and the 'true' activewear line. 
2. The Opening Price Point (OPP) strategy drove double-digit conversion growth and represented ~30% of apparel sales at healthy margins. 
3. The sub-brand portfolio demonstrated strong momentum with 75% year-over-year growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Total company comparable sales declined 1.7%, primarily due to the planned restructuring of the footwear business. 
2. Gross margin contracted to 35.3% from 38.1% a year ago, reflecting the impact of tariffs and promotions. 
3. Net income fell sharply to $0.4 million ($0.00 EPS) from $5.9 million ($0.06 EPS) in the prior year.
rows.key_quote: Total company comparable sales declined 1.7% in Q1. Excluding footwear, Q1 comparable sales would have been +1.2%.

rows.positive_highlights: U.S. revenue growth of 15% in Concrete Pumping was driven by strong demand from large-scale data center and infrastructure projects. Data center and chip plant work now represent 10-12% of total revenue, up from 4-5% a year ago. Full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance were both significantly raised based on strong first-half results and continued U.S. momentum. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved 80 basis points to 24.7% due to higher revenue and improved operating leverage.
rows.negative_highlights: U.K. market conditions remain challenging with soft underlying commercial construction activity due to interest rates and economic uncertainty. Residential construction remains soft due to elevated mortgage rates and affordability pressures. Light commercial and office construction segments are subdued due to high financing costs.
rows.key_quote: ...between data centers and chip plant work, we're probably doing 10% to 12% of revenue on that type of work.

rows.positive_highlights:
Large customer momentum: ARR from $100k+ customers grew 37% YoY, accelerating for the third consecutive quarter.
Strong ARR and Revenue Growth: Net new ARR grew 30% YoY to $101M, and total revenue grew 31% YoY.
Emerging Product Traction: Emerging products contributed over 20% of net new ACV for the second straight quarter, highlighted by a large Connected Asset Maintenance deal with Hertz.
rows.negative_highlights:
Gross Margin Pressure: Gross margin declined 200 bps year-over-year due to investments in AI and cloud infrastructure.
Supply Chain Uncertainty: Management noted that visibility into the component supply chain (DRAM/NAND) 'isn't as good as it has been in the past'.
Potential Q2 Deceleration: The Q2 revenue growth guidance of 23-24% implies a sequential slowdown from Q1's 31% growth rate.
rows.key_quote: We now have over $1.2 billion in ARR from our customers spending $100,000 or more, growing 37% year-over-year and accelerating.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record revenue of $94 million grew 42% YoY, primarily driven by the Defense & Intelligence (D&I) sector which surged over 65% YoY.
2. Raised full-year revenue guidance to $425M-$441M based on strong performance and a record backlog of $906 million (up 72% YoY).
3. Signed a new 8-figure contract with an international D&I customer and launched Sweden's first sovereign reconnaissance satellite just four months after contract signing.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Non-GAAP gross margin decreased to 56% from 59% YoY due to investments in satellite services contracts and new launches.
2. Civil government revenue was flat year-over-year, impacted by a reduction in the company's contract with NASA.
3. Quarterly free cash flow was negative $2.5 million, though the company expects to be free cash flow positive for the full fiscal year.
rows.key_quote: First quarter D&I revenue grew over 65% year-on-year, driven by strong performance in our data subscription solutions and satellite services.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Professional segment sales grew 9.1%, led by low double-digit organic growth in the Underground and Specialty Construction business. 
2. Adjusted operating margins reached a 12-quarter high of 14.4% driven by the AMP productivity program, which is on track for $125M in run-rate savings.
3. Free cash flow conversion was 125%, leading to $361M returned to shareholders in the first half through share repurchases and dividends.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Management identified new headwinds from material and fuel inflation, estimated to impact EPS by approximately $0.16 for the full year. 
2. The company's tax rate is trending higher due to the geographic mix of earnings, creating an approximate $0.04 EPS headwind. 
3. Continued market softness was noted in Europe, particularly impacting residential segment results for the region.
rows.key_quote: We are particularly excited to have achieved low double digit organic sales growth in underground and specialty construction.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong D2C growth (+3% constant currency), driven by mid-single-digit e-commerce growth across all regions and both brands.
Key hero categories showed strong D2C performance: Calvin Klein underwear (mid-single-digit growth) and denim (double-digit growth); Tommy Hilfiger sweaters and outerwear (double-digit growth).
Full-year EPS guidance was reaffirmed at $11.80-$12.10, with the impact from EMEA headwinds being offset by an unexpected $100 million tariff refund.
rows.negative_highlights:
Lowered full-year revenue guidance (from slight increase to flat) due to the prolonged conflict in the Middle East negatively impacting the EMEA business.
EMEA region faces pressure from lower wholesale demand in the Middle East, negative knock-on effects in Turkey, and weaker consumer sentiment across Europe.
Q1 Wholesale revenue declined mid-single digits in constant currency, reflecting cautious partner positioning and shipment timing shifts.
rows.key_quote: ...we delivered mid-single-digit growth in global underwear and double-digit growth in denim in our direct-to-consumer business.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Revenue grew 77% to $438M, primarily driven by the accretive Kito Crosby acquisition. 2. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 130 basis points to 15.7%, demonstrating the profitability benefits of the acquisition and increased scale. 3. Management is highly confident in achieving its synergy target of $14M in FY27 and $70M over three years.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Adjusted gross margin declined to 32.7% due to unfavorable mix, tariffs, and disruptions from a recent divestiture. 2. Company recorded a large GAAP net loss of $238M due to a $200M non-cash goodwill impairment charge and acquisition costs. 3. Market conditions in EMEA are challenging, with geopolitical issues causing project delays and slowing order conversion.
rows.key_quote: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 130 bps, driven by the accretive Kito Crosby acquisition and benefits of scale from our newly combined company.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised full-year net new ARR growth guidance by over 500 basis points to 27-29% acceleration, driven by the AI security boom.
2. Record Q1 net new ARR of $256M (up 32% YoY) and ending ARR of $5.51B (accelerated to 24% growth).
3. New AIDR (AI Detection and Response) product ending ARR grew 250% sequentially with a Q2 pipeline already exceeding $50M.
rows.negative_highlights: No significant negative factors were discussed; the call was overwhelmingly positive with a focus on accelerating tailwinds.
rows.key_quote: The gap between AI adoption and AI protection is the widest asymmetry in security since the cloud transition. And it is moving faster.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) A major restructuring is complete, reducing headcount by ~35% and expected to save ~$135M in annual operating costs. 2) Founder/CEO Tom Siebel has returned to active management with a clear turnaround plan focused on fixing sales execution. 3) The company is well-capitalized with $673M in cash after a $69M insider purchase by the CEO, removing financing risk.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) CEO described sales performance as "unspeakably horrible" and having "fallen off the cliff," causing a severe drop in revenue. 2) Reported Q4 non-GAAP gross margin was extremely low at 37%, indicating poor unit economics. 3) FY27 revenue guidance is significantly below historical performance, signaling a long recovery period.
rows.key_quote: As I look at the sales performance I mean, it is just unspeakably horrible, and it is surreal. This is resulting in market multiples...that are candidly well earned.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. AI semiconductor revenue hit a record $10.8B (up 143% YoY) with bookings of over $30B, indicating massive demand.
2. Company issued robust Q3 revenue guidance of $29.4B (+84% YoY) and a full-year 2026 AI revenue target of $56B.
3. Non-AI semiconductor business showed a "full cyclical recovery," with bookings of $6B significantly exceeding revenue of $4.2B.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Consolidated gross margin for Q2 decreased 32 basis points YoY to 77.1% due to a mix shift towards semiconductors.
2. Q3 consolidated gross margin is forecast to decline further to approximately 74% as the proportion of AI revenue continues to grow significantly.
3. The wireless segment experienced a seasonal decline, which partially offset growth in other non-AI markets.
rows.key_quote: Demand for XPUs and networking is simply insatiable. During the quarter, bookings for AI semiconductors were over $30 billion against the $10.8 billion shipped.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Gross margin increased 80 basis points to 41.9%, beating expectations due to lower supply chain costs. 2. Adjusted EPS grew 21% to $0.91, leading to a raised full-year EPS outlook. 3. The Ollie's Army loyalty program grew 13% to 17.5 million members, who drive over 80% of sales.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Unseasonable weather and surging fuel prices pressured sales, particularly in weather-sensitive categories like lawn & garden in the South. 2. Q2 comp trends are running below the full-year target, leading to a slight reduction in the annual sales outlook. 3. The company saw divergent regional performance, with the South lagging plan by 100-300 basis points due to weather and throughput constraints at the Texas DC.
rows.key_quote: The combination of unseasonable weather and surging fuel prices put pressure on a few key categories such as lawn and garden and summer furniture.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Exceptional sales growth: Net sales grew nearly 33% with comparable sales up 23%, driven by a 19% increase in customer transactions.
2. Massive margin expansion: Adjusted operating margin increased 600 basis points to 12%, driven by a 340 basis point improvement in gross margin from strong sales leverage.
3. Raised full-year outlook: Raised full-year sales guidance to $5.4B-$5.48B and adjusted EPS to a midpoint of $8.85, reflecting strong momentum.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Cautious H2 macro outlook: Management remains cautious on the macro environment, consumer sentiment, and watching behaviors for the second half of the year.
2. Difficult H2 comparisons: The company faces challenging comparisons in the second half, where it will be cycling 15% comp growth from the prior year.
3. Identified cost pressures: Management noted rising fuel costs as a 20-25 basis point headwind (though offset) and increased marketing spend investment.
rows.key_quote: This end-to-end approach from detecting a burgeoning trend to amplifying it in social to creating an amazing in-store experience, that's our special sauce.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Enterprise comparable sales grew 3.0%, the strongest Q1 in four years, with positive comps at all nameplates: Macy's (+1.6%), Bloomingdale's (+10.2%), and Bluemercury (+6.4%). 2. The 'Bold New Chapter' strategy drove results, with the 200 'Reimagine' Macy's locations outperforming the nameplate with 2.4% comp growth. 3. Bloomingdale's delivered its highest Q1 sales volume in history, fueled by luxury brand additions and strength in ready-to-wear and fine jewelry.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Gross margin rate fell to 38.9% from 39.2% year-over-year, partly due to a 30-basis-point tariff impact. 2. Certain categories experienced softness, specifically big-ticket home goods like furniture and the plus-size apparel business. 3. Macy's Media Network revenue declined 5% year-over-year, attributed to the timing of advertising spend.
rows.key_quote: Macy's nameplate achieved positive 1.6% comparable sales with Reimagine locations growing 2.4%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Software revenue surged 26.5% YoY to $47.3 million, driving overall revenue growth.
2. Recurring revenue grew 10% YoY, propelled by stronger-than-expected adoption of subscription offerings, leading to an increased full-year outlook for this segment.
3. Profitability expanded significantly faster than revenue, with non-GAAP operating income up 41.5% and non-GAAP gross margin increasing 100 bps to 72.9%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Negative cash flow from operations of $4.7 million, attributed to subscription timing, FX headwinds, and inventory buildup.
2. Foreign exchange dynamics, particularly the weak USD versus the Israeli shekel, negatively impacted operating expenses and created a $2.2 million other expense.
3. Professional services revenue declined to $8.2 million from $13.5 million a year ago, though this was expected due to timing.
rows.key_quote: The growth was driven by the stronger-than-expected adoption of our subscription offerings, where we have seen an increased momentum recently.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Cardiac Ablation Solutions (CAS) grew 78% worldwide, driven by 145% growth in PFA, leading to an 8-point U.S. market share gain.
2. Achieved the strongest full-year organic revenue growth in 10 years at 5.8%.
3. Symplicity renal denervation system is now annualizing at $100 million in revenue, with weekly procedure volumes doubling since the NCD.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Structural Heart business was flat for the quarter, with U.S. performance being soft due to competitive low-risk TAVR data.
2. Gross margin was negatively impacted by 80 basis points from tariffs ($74 million) and 60 basis points from unfavorable product mix.
3. Certain segments faced headwinds, including continued pressure in bariatrics and market softness in sacral nerve modulation, which offset growth from new products.
rows.key_quote: CAS delivered another outstanding quarter, with 78% worldwide growth and gaining an additional 8 points of U.S. share.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Improved Renewals & RPO Growth: Achieved the highest renewal rate in over two years, driving total RPO past $1 billion for the first time (up 10% YoY).
2. Strong AI Adoption: ARR for AI-native SKUs grew 47% year-over-year, with over 180 AI client projects underway, demonstrating traction with copiloting and agentic offerings.
3. Record Enterprise Win: Signed the largest software deal in company history, a multiyear, multi-division platform agreement with a global consumer electronics company.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Weak Forward Guidance: Guided full-year FY27 total revenue growth to only 1% and lowered the full-year non-GAAP EPS outlook.
2. Geopolitical Headwinds: Experienced pressure in the Middle East, causing $3M to $4M in deal slippage during Q1 and creating uncertainty in the full-year outlook.
3. Margin Pressure: Experiencing higher data and hosting costs from AI product adoption and guided Q2 professional services gross margin to be negative 10%, impacting near-term profitability.
rows.key_quote: The outperformance in Q1 was driven by better linearity and improving renewals.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Major AI Push: Unveiled Veeva Falcon, an "agentic labor" platform to automate R&D tasks, and acquired Ostro for AI-driven commercial engagement, both viewed as significant, accretive growth drivers.
2. Strong Segment Performance: R&D Cloud had a strong start to the year, and the Crossix data business saw continued market share gains and strong growth.
3. Vault CRM Execution: Secured major new wins with Teva and Merck KGaA, maintains an over 80% win rate in the current year, and is confident in winning the majority of remaining Top-20 decisions.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Modest Guidance Increase: Despite a strong Q1 beat, full-year revenue guidance was raised by only $5 million, indicating conservatism or offsetting factors.
2. Gross Margin Pressure: Subscription gross margin saw a year-over-year dip due to tough comps, while services gross margin was impacted by increased investments.
3. Unchanged Macro Environment: Management stated the macro business environment is stable but has not improved since prior guidance, offering no additional tailwind.
rows.key_quote: Falcon specifically is at the agent layer and that's agentic labor. So fully replacing parts -- jobs that people used to do.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. High-margin segments drove growth: NRS recurring revenue grew 22%, net2phone subscription revenue grew 12%, and FinTech digital transactions grew 20%. 2. Profitability and margins hit records: Gross margin expanded 170 bps to a record 38.8%, and adjusted EBITDA grew 13% to $37.5 million. 3. Raised guidance: Full-year FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $150-$152M, citing strong operating leverage and momentum.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Increased competition in NRS: Management acknowledged increased competition is affecting new sign-ups for its POS terminal business. 2. Continued decline in traditional segment: The Traditional Communications segment continues its expected revenue decline, though profitability remains stable. 3. AI offerings are not yet accretive: New AI products are still in an investment phase and are not expected to be accretive growth drivers until fiscal year 2027.
rows.key_quote: IDT's year-over-year revenue and earnings growth was again powered by the continued expansion and operating leverage of our 3 higher-margin businesses.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Results: Record Q3 sales ($995M, +6%), adjusted operating margin (16.6%), and adjusted EPS ($1.06, +7%).
2. Mobile Solutions Strength: Sales up 8%, driven by an 8% increase in Aftermarket sales with double-digit growth in the independent channel, leading to a record segment margin of 20.2%.
3. Life Sciences Growth: Sales up 13%, driven by robust new equipment volume in Food and Beverage (+30%) and ongoing strength in Disk Drive.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Industrial Segment Margin Pressure: Gross margin was pressured by ~100 basis points from production shifts and optimization costs, causing segment pretax margin to fall to 13.4% from 18.1% YoY.
2. Aerospace & Defense Decline: Segment sales fell 14% due to supply chain constraints and project timing, despite a near-record backlog.
3. Lowered Op Margin Guidance: Full-year organic operating margin guidance was revised down to 15.8%-16.2% from 16.0%-16.4% previously due to the temporary industrial inefficiencies.
rows.key_quote: We grew double digits in our independent channel where our product availability, reliability, and consistency continue to drive share gains.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Overseas revenue grew 44% YoY to RMB 597 million, now 25% of total revenue. 
2. Non-GAAP gross margin improved to 38.8% from 37.9% YoY, driven by higher-margin overseas products. 
3. Two new overseas social apps achieved triple-digit YoY revenue growth and are rapidly approaching profitability.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Domestic revenue declined 15% YoY, driven by stricter tax enforcement on live-streaming agencies. 
2. Consolidated revenue declined 5% YoY, and Non-GAAP net income fell 28.7% YoY. 
3. Full-year domestic revenue guidance was downgraded to a mid-teens YoY decline, worsening from a previous 'low-teens' forecast.
rows.key_quote: The decrease was primarily due to heightened tax scrutiny on the agencies for Momo's Entertainment business, combined with softened consumer sentiment.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Meaningful improvement was seen in IL MAKIAGE's Customer Acquisition Cost (CPA) in May, which declined an estimated 28% from April, suggesting a potential recovery.
2. The new METHODIQ brand is off to a strong start, expected to deliver $25 million in revenue in its first year, in line with SpoiledChild's successful launch.
3. The company maintains a strong balance sheet with $667 million in cash and has been actively repurchasing shares, watching back $82 million in Q1.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. A major technical 'dislocation' with its largest advertising partner caused Customer Acquisition Costs (CPA) to spike to levels 2x higher than expected.
2. Q1 net revenue declined 26% year-over-year, driven by a ~50% decrease in first-time customer orders due to the advertising inefficiency.
3. Gross margin compressed by 520 basis points to 69.7%, leading to an adjusted EBITDA loss of $7 million and an adjusted EPS loss of $0.17.
rows.key_quote: We saw levels of CPA that, in some cases, were 2x higher than what we were expecting and what we see in other competitors.

rows.positive_highlights: Exceptional comparable store sales growth of 13.9%, marking the 21st consecutive month of growth and driven by both increased traffic and basket size. Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $13.9M from $6.4M last year, driven by gross margin expansion and 250bps of SG&A leverage. Performance was broad-based with strength across all product divisions, particularly Men's, Children's, and Footwear.
rows.negative_highlights: Gross margin was negatively impacted by higher freight expenses from rising fuel surcharges, a headwind expected to persist throughout the year. This led to a slight reduction in the full-year gross margin expansion guidance. Women's apparel was identified as an area needing repositioning, implying it is underperforming its potential relative to other categories. The store opening cadence for 2026 is irregular as the company ramps up its real estate program.
rows.key_quote: Our sales growth is being driven by refinements of trend, style and value of our core merchandising assortment.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong gross margin expansion: Increased 100 bps to 40.1%, driven by a significant, company-wide reduction in inventory shrink. 2. Robust sales growth: Net sales grew 11.1% and comparable sales increased 5.3%, led by high-teens growth in the fragrance category. 3. Raised profitability guidance: Full-year EPS guidance was increased to $28.36-$28.80, reflecting Q1 outperformance and an increased share buyback plan to $1.5 billion.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Implied back-half deceleration: Full-year revenue guidance was maintained despite the strong Q1, implying a slowdown to low single-digit comps for the remainder of the year. 2. Macroeconomic caution: Management cited that consumers are increasingly value-focused amid economic uncertainty, leading to a 'measured approach' on outlook. 3. Category-specific softness: Performance was mixed, with declines in hair tools and pressure in body care, while mass makeup was relatively flat.
rows.key_quote: Gross margin for the quarter increased 100 basis points to 40.1% of sales, primarily due to lower inventory shrink and higher merchandise margin.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong Revenue Growth: Total sales increased 15% and comp sales grew 13%, with double-digit growth across all core brands (VS, PINK, Beauty). 2. Significant Margin Expansion: Adjusted gross margin rate expanded 240 bps to 37.6% due to a successful 'promo detox' and higher regular-priced watching. 3. Robust Profitability: Adjusted EPS grew over 500% to $0.60, driven by sales leverage and improved merchandise margins.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Tariff Headwinds: Guidance assumes tariffs increase from 10% to 20% in the back half of the year, representing a gross headwind of about $75 million for the full year. 2. Shareholder Activism: Management acknowledged a shareholder campaign from BBRC, calling it a 'distraction' from the business momentum. 3. Rising SG&A Costs: Q2 SG&A rate is expected to increase due to investments in store labor, customer experience, and proxy contest-related expenses.
rows.key_quote: We are growing sales through customer count and higher average spend as we lead with emotion over promotion.

rows.positive_highlights:
Exceptional top-line growth: NGS ARR grew 60% to $8.13B, with organic growth accelerating to 28%. Total revenue grew 31% to $3.0B.
Strong Network Security Momentum: Next-generation firewall bookings rose nearly 40% YoY, the strongest hardware performance in a decade, driven by AI data center build-outs.
Rapid Product Scaling & Acquisition Success: Prisma AIRS reached 300 customers (tripling Q2), XSIAM hit $600M ARR (+100% YoY), and acquisitions CyberArk/Chronosphere are outperforming and integrating ahead of schedule.
rows.negative_highlights:
GAAP Net Loss: Reported a GAAP net loss per share of $0.22, primarily due to non-recurring transaction/integration costs and stock-based compensation from recent large acquisitions.
Near-term Cost Pressures: Monitoring rising component costs in memory/storage, which prompted a 10% hardware price increase. Stock-based compensation also increased to 17% of revenue due to acquisitions.
Cloud Portfolio Migration: Proactively transitioning Prisma Cloud customers to Cortex Cloud is ongoing, with management noting it was 'not contributing as well as some of the other products'.
rows.key_quote: Our Q3 results featured the strongest hardware performance in a decade, with next-generation firewall booking rising nearly 40% year-over-year.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Revenue grew 26.3% YoY to $155 million, driven by steady expansion of core operations. 2. Achieved a record net asset inflow of $2.9 billion, with over $2 billion from retail users for the first time, primarily from overseas markets. 3. Q2-to-date recovery has recouped all $4.9 billion of Q1's mark-to-market losses and trading activity has picked up significantly.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Incurred a one-time regulatory penalty of ~RMB 411 million, leading to a net loss of $26.9 million. 2. New regulations in China will restrict onshore trading for mainland clients, who account for 20-25% of total net revenue. 3. Total client assets declined 3.2% QoQ due to $4.9 billion in mark-to-market losses from market turbulence.
rows.key_quote: ...net asset inflow from retail users and the consolidated accounts exceeded USD 2 billion for the first time in our history.

rows.positive_highlights: Duo Agent Platform (DAP) contributed more net new ARR in its first quarter than Duo Pro and Duo Enterprise combined in any prior quarter, and attached to 4 of the top 10 deals. Revenue grew 23% to $264 million, beating guidance, with non-GAAP operating margin expanding 200 bps year-over-year to 14%.
