Customers with >$100k ARR grew 18% to 1,519, and new logo growth was 30% higher year-over-year.
rows.negative_highlights: Announced a major restructuring ('Act 2') impacting ~14% of the workforce (350 team members) and incurring $30M-$35M in charges. Experienced more seat contraction than anticipated due to customer layoffs and M&A activity, contributing to a dollar-based net retention of 117%. Full-year revenue growth guidance of 16-17% represents a deceleration, reflecting macro pressures and potential disruption from organizational changes.
rows.key_quote: Duo Agent platform contributed more net new ARR in its first quarter than Duo Pro and Duo Enterprise combined in any prior quarter.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Achieved profitable growth with revenue up 13.2% YoY to RMB 1.7B and non-GAAP net profit of RMB 41.4M.
2. Strong momentum in new initiatives, with non-academic tutoring gross billings up over 20% YoY, contributing over 35% of total billings.
3. Deferred revenue grew 24.1% YoY to RMB 1.8B, providing strong future revenue visibility.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Net operating cash outflow increased significantly by 73.6% year-over-year to RMB 828.4 million.
2. Watching expenses grew 19.0% YoY, outpacing revenue growth of 13.2%.
3. Gross margin slightly deteriorated to 69.5% as cost of revenue grew faster than net revenue.
rows.key_quote: In our new initiatives... nonacademic tutoring services, gross billings increased by over 20% year-over-year... contributing more than 35% of total gross billings.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Gross margin expanded 65 basis points to 31.6%, primarily driven by a 28 basis point reduction in shrink and improved inventory markups.
2. EPS increased 12.4% to $2.00, exceeding expectations and leading to a raise in full-year EPS guidance.
3. Same-store sales grew 2.0% on a 1.4% increase in customer traffic, with significant trade-in from higher-income customers (>$100k annually).
rows.negative_highlights:
1. The core customer remains financially constrained due to high fuel prices and reduced SNAP benefits.
2. SG&A as a percentage of sales increased by 25 basis points, with deleverage expected to continue for the full year.
3. Transportation costs increased, with fuel costs expected to remain elevated for the balance of the year.
rows.key_quote: Our shrink mitigation efforts once again contributed to strong gross margin expansion... we delivered a 28 basis points reduction in shrink versus prior year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Adjusted EPS grew over 30% to $1.56, driven by SG&A leverage from restructuring and cost discipline, leading to a 12% increase in adjusted operating income.
2. Achieved 1.8% comparable sales growth, with positive performance in every category and particular strength in higher price point sales (AUR up nearly 5%).
3. Raised the midpoint of full-year revenue and EPS guidance, citing strong Q1 results and continued momentum from Mother's Day into Q2.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Adjusted gross margin rate declined by approximately 100 basis points, with merchandise margin falling 70 basis points primarily due to higher gold costs.
2. The transition and sunsetting of the James Allen brand created a 1-point drag on comparable sales and resulted in a $32 million noncash inventory write-down.
3. Management anticipates continued modest unit declines, especially at lower price points, as a result of higher gold prices impacting affordability.
rows.key_quote: SG&A expenses were down 3%... from... restructuring and ongoing spend discipline to drive 12% growth in adjusted operating income.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record Margins: "Fiscal first quarter margin was a company record driven by strong program execution" and a $12M venture gain. 2. Raised EPS Guidance: "Our adjusted EPS guidance increases by approximately 4% to a range of $9.9 to $10.10." 3. Strong Execution: Performed better than expected with 0.5% organic growth on the year's toughest comparison.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Recompete Headwinds: The unsuccessful RITS recompete represents a ~$200M headwind for FY27, which is now expected to roll off in Q3. 2. Cautious Revenue Outlook: Maintained full-year revenue guidance of -4% to -2% despite the strong start, citing timing benefits and uncertainties. 3. Shrinking Pipeline: Qualified pipeline is down ~25% from last year to $85B as the company intentionally de-emphasizes commoditized enterprise IT opportunities.
rows.key_quote: We are... controlling our future as we build a premier portfolio... more aligned to budget priorities and more insulated against... commoditization.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Massive Growth: Reported record Q4 revenue of $437M (up 157% YoY) and FY26 revenue of $1.3B (up 206% YoY), driven by strong demand for AI connectivity solutions.
2. Bullish FY27 Guidance: Projects over 80% YoY revenue growth, fueled by an expected $600M+ contribution from its rapidly ramping optical portfolio (DSPs, SiPho PICs, ZeroFlap optics).
3. Strong Profitability & Leverage: Achieved a 68.3% non-GAAP gross margin in Q4 and guides for a non-GAAP net margin around 50% for FY27, showcasing significant operating leverage.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Supply Chain Constraints: Management acknowledged "significant tightness in the supply chain," requiring careful management to meet aggressive growth targets.
2. Back-Half Weighted Growth: FY27 growth is heavily reliant on a second-half inflection, with only "mid-single digit sequential growth" expected in the first half, concentrating execution risk.
3. Significant Opex Increase: Plans to increase non-GAAP operating expenses by approximately 50% YoY in FY27 to fund R&D and new product development.
rows.key_quote: As AI clusters scale from tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of GPUs, connectivity is no longer just about bandwidth.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record-breaking demand and backlog: "Orders more than doubled significantly outpacing revenue, resulting in a record company backlog."
2. Massive FY26 guidance raise: Raised non-GAAP EPS outlook by over 40% to $3.40 midpoint and free cash flow to at least $3.5 billion, achieving long-term targets two years early.
3. Strong server and AI momentum: "Traditional server orders increased triple digits... We booked $1.8 billion in new AI systems orders bringing Cumulative AI systems bookings to $16.4 billion."
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant supply constraints: "When it comes down to potential upside on the revenue... it really comes down to availability of supply." and "Supply chain is the name of the game in networking."
2. Component cost inflation: "...ongoing DRAM and NAND inflationary costs and supply constraints. We continue to work with our partners to secure long term agreements while executing the pricing actions..."
3. Lumpiness of large AI deals: "Service provider orders exceeded the combined total of its prior 4 quarters, underscoring the inherently lumpy nature of our large scale AI deals."
rows.key_quote: Traditional server orders increased triple digits as customers continue to modernize their compute infrastructure and invest in AI inferencing.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Market conditions are tightening in Brazil and the North Sea due to increased FPSO activity, leading to a stronger charter market.
2. Secured new charters and extensions for key vessels, increasing the fixed contract backlog to $858 million with an average duration of 2.4 years.
3. Increased the quarterly distribution and guided for "multiple gradual increases" supported by market strength and future accretive dropdown acquisitions.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Revenue declined sequentially due to scheduled vessel drydockings, which pushed overall fleet utilization down to 92%.
2. Changed vessel useful life estimate from 23 to 20 years, which will increase future non-cash depreciation expenses.
3. Faces significant near-term refinancing requirements, with a $220 million facility and a $65 million facility maturing in late 2026.
rows.key_quote: In both Brazil and the North Sea, we continue to see tightening markets driven by FPSO start ups, ramp ups, expansions, and new developments.

rows.positive_highlights:
Record Water Solutions Performance: The segment delivered adjusted EBITDA of $153M for Q4 and $603M for FY26, with produced water volumes up 10% YoY to 3 million barrels per day.
Strong FY27 Guidance: Projects adjusted EBITDA of $715M-$725M (~10% YoY growth), backed by contracted projects like the LEX II expansion, indicating high visibility.
Capital Structure Progress: Executed a $950M refinancing, redeemed 285,000 high-cost preferred units, and repurchased 8.7M common units, strengthening the balance sheet.
rows.negative_highlights:
Goodwill Impairment Charge: The company recognized an unspecified goodwill impairment charge during the quarter, which impacted GAAP income.
Absorbing Higher Capital Costs: Management stated they are absorbing increased pipeline costs for new projects and not passing them on to customers, which could pressure project returns.
Ongoing Asset Monetization: The company is still in the process of rightsizing its Liquids segment, indicating the strategic transition to a pure-play water company is not yet complete.
rows.key_quote: We achieved produced water volumes of approximately 3 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter, a 10% increase in physical volumes disposed.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Cloud Mining revenue grew 7.1% year-over-year to $57.5 million, providing a stable revenue stream.
2. Fleet efficiency significantly improved to 17.7 joules per terahash from 23.2 J/TH a year ago, structurally lowering production costs.
3. Maintained a strong balance sheet with $141.5 million in cash and digital assets and significant liquidity via a $100M revolver.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Total revenue declined 6.8% YoY, primarily due to a 35.2% decrease in self-mining revenue.
2. Gross margin declined significantly due to lower Bitcoin prices, higher network difficulty, and high-cost hashrate contracts from the prior quarter.
3. Reported a net loss of $35.0 million, driven by a $35.6 million fair value loss on Bitcoin holdings.
rows.key_quote: We deliberately reduced self-mining exposure to preserve liquidity and mitigate risk during significant price volatility.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Journeys' comps grew 5% driven by its transformation strategy, with new 4.0 stores delivering a >25% sales lift. 2. Johnston & Murphy comps accelerated to a 7% gain, benefiting from product innovation, the Peyton Manning campaign, and a trend towards refined dressing. 3. Full-year EPS guidance was raised to $2.00-$2.40, and a new $40-$50 million cost savings program was announced.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Schuh comps declined 9% due to an intentional pullback from promotions and a challenging UK consumer market. 2. Q2 outlook is weak, with total sales guided down 3-4% and operating loss expected to be in line with or worse than last year. 3. The overall consumer environment is described as "selective and intentional," leading to a "more conservative" view of the second half of the year.
rows.key_quote: The strength of our multi-branded multi-category elevated assortment drove stronger full-price watching and considerably higher average transaction size in the quarter.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Margin Expansion & Cost Control: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 46% from 42%, and gross margin hit 72% from 68%, driven by a ~90% reduction in fraud costs and significant AI-driven automation.
2. Strong Account & Asset Growth: Total HSA assets grew 19%, and total HSA account growth of 8% outpaced the market (6%), indicating market share gains. The enterprise sales pipeline is the largest in years.
3. Raised Guidance & Confidence: Raised full-year revenue and EPS guidance and increased the share repurchase authorization by $1 billion, signaling strong confidence in future cash flow.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Slower Interchange Growth: Interchange revenue growth of 5% was described as 'a little slower than it's been growing,' potentially indicating a slight deceleration in member spending.
2. Potential One-Time Service Cost Benefit: Approximately $2 million of service cost improvement came from unexpectedly low employee healthcare claims, a benefit management does not expect to recur.
3. Early Stage of Marketplace: While a key strategic initiative, the Marketplace is still nascent with over 10,000 members and is not yet a material contributor to revenue.
rows.key_quote: AI-enabled automation reduced manual efforts by more than 90% and accelerated processing times by up to 50%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Women's division sales grew 11%, driven by an 8% increase in denim sales where average price points rose to $92 from $84.85.
2. Overall net sales increased 6.1% and comparable store sales grew 5.1%, indicating strong customer demand for current assortments.
3. The Kid's business delivered a standout performance with sales up approximately 16%, representing a significant growth opportunity.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Gross margin decreased by 50 basis points to 46.2%, primarily due to a 40 bps impact from higher occupancy costs related to store projects.
2. The Men's denim business contracted by 1.5%, contributing to the division's underperformance relative to the rest of the company.
3. Inventory grew 13.5% year-over-year, outpacing the 6.1% sales growth, which could increase future markdown risk.
rows.key_quote: Women's denim category continued to be the leading contributor to revenue growth with denim sales up 8% year over year.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Advertising revenue grew 9% year-over-year to $369.8 million, driven by strong demand from internet services, local services, and automotive sectors. 2. Video consumption continues to grow, with total time spent on video playback pages achieving double-digit year-over-year growth. 3. Daily Active Users (DAUs) grew modestly quarter-over-quarter to 254 million, demonstrating core user resilience despite strategic channel budget reductions.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Non-GAAP operating margin decreased to 28% from 33% in the prior year due to increased investments in monetization initiatives. 2. Monthly Active Users (MAUs) declined to 562 million on both a YoY and QoQ basis due to a strategic rationalization of channel investment. 3. Value-added services revenue fell 11% year-over-year to $51.6 million, mainly because of a decline in game-related revenue.
rows.key_quote: The main growth contributors in the first quarter were verticals such as Internet services, Local services and Automobiles.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Sequential improvement in operating income, which rebounded from Q4 2025 levels, with operating margin rising to 12% from 1.4% in the previous quarter.
2. Maintained a strong balance sheet and liquidity position with ~RMB 2.4 billion in cash and an equity-to-asset ratio of ~57%.
3. Continued share repurchase program, watching back ~1.8 million ADS for ~$8.2 million, with ~$39.8 million remaining under the current authorization.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Loan origination volume collapsed, declining 58.4% year-over-year and 35.8% sequentially to RMB 14.63 billion.
2. Severe deterioration in credit quality, with the 91- to 180-day delinquency rate increasing to 9.95%, up from 2.73% a year ago.
3. Profitability plummeted, with net income falling to RMB 38 million from RMB 458 million in Q1 2025, a decrease of over 90%.
rows.key_quote: This pullback was deliberate as we place greater priority on portfolio integrity and long-term balance sheet stability over near-term origination volume.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. AI products drove 17% of net-new ARR in Q1, exceeding the 15% full-year target pace and boosting customer retention and expansion.
2. In-quarter NRR improved for the fourth consecutive quarter to 97%, and the tech vertical returned to positive YoY growth for the first time in 8 quarters.
3. Strategic acquisition of Stack.ai accelerates the AI and cross-system automation roadmap by over a year, strengthening the company's enterprise offering.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. The self-service (PLG) business remains a headwind, with guidance assuming a 2-point drag on ARR growth for the fiscal year.
2. Overall trailing four-quarter dollar-based net retention rate of 96% remains below 100%, indicating net contraction over the past year.
3. Stock-based compensation remains 'elevated,' expected to be in the low 20s as a percentage of revenue for the fiscal year.
rows.key_quote: AI product bookings now represent 17% of net-new ARR in Q1, ahead of the pace required to achieve our 15% full year target.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Adjusted EPS grew 38% to $1.74, significantly beating guidance due to strong operational execution.
2. Gross margin expanded 120 basis points, driven by operational improvements including favorable freight and a notable reduction in shrink.
3. The multi-price assortment strategy successfully drove a 4.5% increase in average ticket, contributing to a 3.5% overall comp sales increase.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Customer traffic declined 1.0% year-over-year, continuing a trend from the prior quarter, though it was in line with management's expectations.
2. Management expressed caution about the macro environment, specifically citing sustained higher fuel costs and pressure on lower-income consumers.
3. Full-year guidance assumes a reversion to higher tariff rates in the second half of the year, creating a potential headwind.
rows.key_quote: The biggest driver [of our outperformance] was shrink... a great performance. We said we would take action there, and we have.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Automotive revenue achieved an all-time record, driven by strong double-digit growth from AI adoption in the commercial vehicle telematics market. 2. Announced a major Long-Term Agreement (LTA) with Hanwha with potential revenue over $800 million across a 10+ year period. 3. Strong new product momentum with 15+ robotics design wins (>$100M lifetime revenue) and a steep production ramp for new 5-nanometer CV7x SoCs.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. The consumer IoT business suffered a double-digit sequential revenue decline, which weighed on overall results. 2. Inventory days rose sharply from 99 to 145, leading to significant cash usage. 3. The company reported a free cash outflow of $29.6 million for the quarter, primarily due to the large inventory build.
rows.key_quote: Our automotive revenue established an all-time revenue record with strong double-digit growth, led by the emergence of AI in commercial vehicle telematics.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised full-year revenue and operating income guidance after exceeding Q1 targets. 
2. Significant AI product momentum, with expansion deals including AI being 6x larger than those without. 
3. Achieved first-ever quarterly GAAP profitability and saw non-GAAP operating margin expand over 250 basis points YoY.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. ARR growth of 12% continues to trail revenue growth of 17%, a point of analyst inquiry. 
2. Management still characterizes the macroeconomic environment as "variable," necessitating a "prudent outlook." 
3. Customer attrition remains concentrated in the small business segment, though this aligns with the company's enterprise focus.
rows.key_quote: In the quarter, 16 of the top 20 deals included AI, and expansion deals that included AI were 6x larger than those that did not.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Beat expectations with 2% comparable sales growth, driven by gaming, computing (9th straight quarter of growth), and mobile phones (5th straight quarter).
2. Gross Margin expansion of 20 bps, fueled by growth in high-margin Best Watch Ads and Marketplace initiatives.
3. Strong outlook for key categories, with an exclusive year-long national retail launch of new RGB TV technology and improving trends in appliances.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Appliance category remained a weak spot, with sales declining in Q1 due to a pressured housing market and competition.
2. Inventory increased by 8% as the company pulled forward computing products to mitigate rising memory costs, increasing balance sheet risk.
3. Management anticipates rising memory costs will increase PC prices and cause some unit elasticity (lower unit sales).
rows.key_quote: The largest contributors to the comparable sales growth were gaming, computing, mobile phones and services, which were partially offset by a decline in appliances.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong sales & earnings beat: Total sales grew 14%, comps grew 6% (vs. 2-4% guidance), and EPS grew 26% (vs. flat guidance). 2. Margin outperformance: Operating margin expanded 20bps, beating guidance of a 60-100bps decline, driven by disciplined markdowns and supply chain productivity. 3. Successful seasonal execution: Upgraded allocation systems drove double-digit comps in warm weather categories, overcoming a historical weakness.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Rising inventory levels: Comparable store inventories increased 11% vs. Q1 2025, outpacing the 6% comp growth. 2. Acknowledged macro risks: Management is more "wary" than in March due to higher gas prices and potential inflation impact on consumers. 3. Freight cost pressure: Guidance includes modest deleverage in freight for the full year due to higher fuel costs.
rows.key_quote: Our upgraded allocation and localization capabilities enabled us to make faster, smarter and more precise allocation decisions.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) FPD revenue grew 13% year-over-year to $62 million, driven by strong demand for high-end AMOLED masks in China and Korea. 2) Strategic expansion projects in the U.S. and Korea remain on track, targeting advanced nodes (8-nanometer and below) with initial revenue expected late in fiscal 2026. 3) Company generated strong operating cash flow of $47 million, representing a healthy 22% of revenue.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) IC business revenue decreased 5% year-over-year as the post-Chinese New Year seasonal recovery did not occur as anticipated. 2) Management cited multiple near-term headwinds delaying design releases, including high fab utilization, memory supply constraints, and geopolitical uncertainty. 3) Q3 guidance is weak, with revenue guided flat and operating margins expected to compress, reflecting continued limited visibility.
rows.key_quote: Fabs have been unable to accommodate additional design releases from some of their customers because of this limited capacity.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Net New ARR of $44 million, a 55% year-over-year increase, marking a company record.
2. Non-endpoint solutions (AI, data, cloud) approached 50% of total ARR for the first time, with AI security ARR nearly doubling sequentially.
3. Operating margin improved by 550 basis points year-over-year, and the company raised its full-year operating income and EPS guidance.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Announced a strategic workforce reduction of approximately 8% to streamline the organization.
2. Maintained full-year revenue guidance despite a strong Q1 ARR beat, citing the back-end loaded timing of larger deals.
3. Net retention is still a focus area for improvement, though it did improve sequentially and YoY for larger customers.
rows.key_quote: Our AI security ARR nearly doubled again in Q1, driving our non-endpoint solutions to approach 50% of total ARR for the first time.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. **Margin Expansion & Raised Guidance**: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 46% from 42% YoY, and gross margin hit 72% from 68%. This led to raised full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance to $4.66-$4.73.
2. **Operational Efficiency via AI**: AI enabled automation reduced manual efforts in certain workflows by over 90% and contributed to a nearly 90% YoY reduction in fraud costs, directly boosting profitability.
3. **Strong Account/Asset Growth & Capital Allocation**: HSA assets grew 19% and total HSA account growth of 8% outpaced the market average of 6%. Management demonstrated confidence by increasing the share repurchase authorization by $1 billion.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. **Slower Interchange Revenue Growth**: Interchange revenue grew 5%, which the CFO noted was "a little slower" than in the past, potentially reflecting a broader slowdown in consumer healthcare spending.
2. **Uncertainty in Service Cost Savings**: A $2 million improvement in service costs was due to unexpectedly low employee medical claims, a benefit management does not assume will persist for the rest of the year.
3. **'Mark' Marketplace Still Nascent**: While a key strategic focus, management stated it's "still very early" and revenue is not yet material, with long-term member retention and cohort behavior still being analyzed.
rows.key_quote: AI enabled automation reduced manual efforts by more than 90% and accelerated processing times by up to 50%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record-breaking gas sales volumes driven by high consumer price sensitivity, which drove new members to use Costco's gas stations for the first time.
2. Strong top-line growth with net sales up 11.6%, adjusted comparable sales up 6.6%, and digitally-enabled comparable sales up 20.8% (FX adjusted).
3. Healthy membership metrics, with fee income up 10.7% and a 9.6% increase in higher-spending Executive memberships.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Reported gross margin declined 21 basis points to 11.04%, with core-on-core margins down 9 bps due to strategic price investments and mix shift.
2. Total paid membership growth slowed to 4.1% year-over-year, which management described as a more normalized but slower rate.
3. SG&A deleveraged by 3 basis points on a core basis (excluding gas inflation) due to higher healthcare costs, despite underlying productivity improvements.
rows.key_quote: The high consumer price sensitivity, which fueled these record volumes, also drove many members to use our gas stations for the very first time.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record Capital Markets performance: Net income was a record, with Corporate and Investment Banking revenue up 17% and Investment Banking revenue up 27% on strong M&A and origination. 2. Strong Wealth Management growth: Net income rose 28%, driven by market appreciation and $10 billion in net new assets in Canada and $5 billion in the U.S. 3. Significant Capital Return: Announced a 14% year-over-year dividend increase and a new normal course issuer bid to repurchase up to 45 million shares.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Rising Impaired Loans: Gross impaired loans increased by $623 million (4 bps) from last quarter, mainly in Capital Markets (real estate, forest products) and Wealth Management (City National). 2. Macro and Trade Uncertainty: Management repeatedly cited headwinds from CUSMA negotiations and geopolitical conflicts, leading to increased severity in downside economic scenarios. 3. Commercial Banking Headwinds: Loan growth was impacted by tariff-driven uncertainty in trade-exposed sectors and moderating demand in commercial real estate.
rows.key_quote: These results were underpinned by our diversified business model benefiting from both a constructive environment for our market-related businesses.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong AI-driven demand with ~500 AI customer wins in Q4, more than doubling the pace from the prior year. 2. Record All-Flash revenue, up 18% YoY in Q4, and Public Cloud revenue up 18% YoY for FY26 (ex-divestiture). 3. A multi-year agreement with Google Cloud for its Distributed Cloud platform was a key driver of the 14% YoY product revenue growth.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Rising memory and component costs are pressuring gross margins, with FY27 guidance of 68.5%-69.5% below the 71.3% achieved in FY26. 2. Management expects product gross margins to trough in Q1 of FY27 due to the full impact of higher component costs. 3. Acknowledged rising risk of accelerated customer purchasing (pull-ins) ahead of price increases, creating potential demand volatility.
rows.key_quote: Product revenue...up 14% year over year, driven by a multiyear agreement with Google Cloud to deliver secure, AI ready data infrastructure.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Gap Brand exceptional performance: Comparable sales increased 10% driven by cultural relevance (Young Miko campaign, Coachella), strength in denim/fleece, and reduced discounting for the 3rd consecutive quarter.
2. Raised EPS Guidance: Full-year adjusted EPS outlook was raised to $2.30-$2.40, reflecting financial discipline, share buybacks, and favorable interest/tax rates despite lower revenue.
3. Sustained Group Comps: Achieved 9th consecutive quarter of positive comparable sales (+2%) for the consolidated company, with 3 of 4 brands posting positive comp growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Old Navy Underperformance: Weakness in the women's dress business due to a poor product/value equation, leading to a moderated full-year outlook for the company's largest brand.
2. Athleta's Disappointing Rebuild: Sales decreased 12% and comps fell 11% as clearing legacy product is taking longer than expected, delaying the brand's turnaround.
3. Gross Margin Decline: Gross margin fell 130 basis points to 40.5%, primarily due to a 200 bps headwind from tariffs that overshadowed underlying merchandise margin expansion.
rows.key_quote: ...seasonal category that has just gotten off to a weaker start, particularly dresses where we just did not have the right fashion and value equation.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record revenue grew 25%, driven by very strong organic growth of 19% in the Flight Support Group and 17% in the Electronic Technologies Group.
2. Exceptional profitability improvement, with net income up 49% and operating margins expanding to 26.2% in FSG and 26.5% in ETG.
3. Cash flow from operations surged 43% to $292 million, highlighting strong cash generation.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. A pull-forward of $15-20 million in defense-related sales from future quarters boosted Q2 results but will moderate growth in the second half of the year.
2. The component repair business, while growing, is being held back by supply chain issues which are delaying the receipt of necessary parts to complete repairs.
3. A minor sales slowdown was noted in the Middle East due to regional conflict, though it was more than offset by strength in other geographies.
rows.key_quote: Business is very strong for us virtually across the board, including in our biggest markets, commercial aviation, defense and space.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. AI cloud gross billings surged 90.1% YoY to RMB 1.0 billion, accounting for 50.1% of public cloud revenue.
2. Public cloud revenue grew 47.5% YoY to RMB 2.0 billion, driving overall company growth.
3. Adjusted EBITDA increased 134.7% YoY, with the margin expanding 11.4 percentage points to 27.6%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Adjusted gross margin decreased to 13% from 17% in the previous quarter due to higher server costs and upfront investments.
2. Management identified supply chain capacity as the "primary limiting factor" for growth and capital spending.
3. Upstream costs for components and servers are rising, creating potential cost pressure.
rows.key_quote: AI cloud gross billings reached RMB 1.0 billion, a 90.1% YoY increase, accounting for over half of public cloud revenues for the first time.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong initial orders for the new Li L9 Livis model, with over 10,000 orders at a price over RMB 500,000.
2. Successful mass production of proprietary MAHE M100 AI chip, claimed to deliver 3x effective computing power at half the cost.
3. Guided for Q2 gross margin recovery to ~10% and delivery growth, driven by new product launches.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Q1 revenue declined 11.4% YoY to RMB 23 billion due to lower deliveries and unfavorable product mix.
2. Q1 gross margin collapsed to 7.9% from 20.5% YoY, with vehicle margin falling to just 6.1% from 19.8% YoY.
3. Reported a significant Q1 net loss of RMB 2.3 billion, reversing a net income of RMB 646.6 million in the prior-year period.
rows.key_quote: Our in-house M100 chip delivers triple the computing power of the previous generation platform at half the cost.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Atlas revenue grew 29.4% YoY, a fourth consecutive quarter above 29%, and added a record $117 million in YoY dollar growth.
2. Total revenue growth accelerated to 25% YoY, beating the high end of guidance.
3. Raised full-year revenue outlook by 200 bps and now expects 100-150 bps of operating margin expansion.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Expects Enterprise Advanced (EA) revenue to be approximately flat in the second half of the year due to tougher prior-year comparisons.
2. Subscription gross margin decreased by 60 bps year-over-year to 77.1%, driven by product mix and seasonality.
3. The go-to-market strategy for AI-native companies is described as a 'work in progress' to optimize engagement with high-growth self-serve customers.
rows.key_quote: Top line strength was driven by Atlas. Which grew 29.4% year over year including a record $117 million year over year dollar growth.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong top-line performance: Adjusted EPS grew 24% and revenue grew 14% year-over-year, with double-digit revenue growth in all business units.
Broad-based drivers: Growth was fueled by expanding net interest margins (up 17 bps YoY), balance sheet growth, and an 18% increase in market-related fees from constructive markets.
Robust capital position and return: CET1 ratio increased to 13.6% while repurchasing 6.5M shares, leading to the announcement of a new, larger 30M share buyback program.
rows.negative_highlights:
Rising credit provisions: Total provision for credit losses was $605 million, up from $568 million last quarter, with higher impairments in Canadian consumer portfolios due to economic pressures.
Specific margin pressure: U.S. segment Net Interest Margin decreased 11 basis points sequentially due to seasonally lower deposit balances and lower loan margins.
Announced transaction dilution: The strategic sale of CIBC Caribbean is expected to be dilutive to EPS by just over 1% upon closing, all else equal.
rows.key_quote: Revenues were up 14%, benefiting from balance sheet growth, improving net interest margins and higher fee income.

rows.positive_highlights:
Proprietary brands grew 6% on a comparable basis, successfully resonating with value-focused customers.
The core Kohl's Card customer cohort stabilized with flat comps, a 600 basis point improvement from Q4.
Digital sales showed strength, growing 4% due to increased traffic and strategic investments.
rows.negative_highlights:
The Sephora at Kohl's business underperformed, declining low-single digits due to weakness in makeup and skincare.
The overall physical store business lagged company performance, with sales down low-single digits on lower transactions.
Men's and footwear categories underperformed the company average, identified as areas needing improvement.
rows.key_quote: Proprietary brands were another bright spot in the quarter, running up 6% on a comparable sales basis.

rows.positive_highlights:
Broad-based growth: All three segments (Foodservice +7%, International +5%, Retail +1%) delivered organic net sales growth, marking the company's sixth consecutive quarter of overall growth.
Strong profit and margin expansion: Adjusted EPS grew 14% to $0.40, and gross margin expanded 70 bps to 17.4%, driven by pricing, favorable mix, and productivity gains.
Operational Excellence: Meaningful improvements in the vertically integrated turkey operations provided a significant profit tailwind for both the Retail and Foodservice segments.
rows.negative_highlights:
Q3 earnings expected to be flat: Management guided for Q3 adjusted earnings to be only 'in line with the prior year' due to multiple cost headwinds.
Cost pressures intensifying: The company faces a full quarter of higher fuel costs, continued logistics challenges, and commodity volatility, which will pressure near-term results.
Planned production slowdown: A targeted inventory rebalancing for certain ambient goods will result in lower plant utilization in Q3, creating a discrete drag on costs and margins.
rows.key_quote: ...we more than offset discrete cost pressures through top line growth, market based pricing actions, favorable mix, and ongoing productivity improvements.

rows.positive_highlights: Water Solutions segment achieved record performance, with Q4 produced water volumes up 10% to 3.0 million barrels per day. Management issued strong FY2027 guidance for adjusted EBITDA of $715-$725 million, representing ~10% growth driven by contracted projects. The company significantly improved its capital structure, redeeming 285,000 high-cost preferred units and repurchasing 8.7 million common units.
rows.negative_highlights: The company recorded an unspecified goodwill impairment charge during the period. Management disclosed it is absorbing increased pipeline costs for new projects rather than passing them on to customers. The Crude Oil Logistics segment's Grand Mesa Pipeline appears under-utilized, with management still working to contract more barrels.
rows.key_quote: There is an incredible amount of demand for additional capacity in the basin... It's continuing to increase and.. having a line out the door.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Total revenue grew robustly by 54.1% YoY to $98.6M, driven by the consumer-focused strategy. 2. Overseas live streaming revenue surged 89.3% YoY to $53.6M, confirming successful expansion into Southeast Asia and the Middle East. 3. Core profitability improved, with operating income turning to a $4.3M profit from a $1M loss, and non-GAAP net income growing from $0.9M to $4.1M.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Gross margin declined to 58.5% from 61.9% YoY due to a business mix shift toward lower-margin live streaming. 2. A large non-cash loss on an investment (Arashi Vision Inc.) resulted in a GAAP net loss from continuing operations of $192.4M. 3. Management cautioned that the rapid growth in the high-performing overseas live streaming business might see a "modest slowdown" in the future.
rows.key_quote: This exceptional growth validates our strategic focus on overseas markets, especially high-growth emerging regions such as Southeast Asia and the Middle East.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong revenue growth of 55% YoY to $28.2M. 2. Turned operating cash flow positive to $6.6M, a $17.3M improvement from a loss last year. 3. Raised full-year revenue guidance to $160M-$200M, up from a previous $137M-$160M.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Reported a significant operating loss of $41.1M. 2. The loss was driven by large non-operating items: a $20.9M stock-based compensation charge and a $18.9M foreign exchange loss. 3. Gross margin declined in the quarter due to a shift in mix towards hardware and aggressive pricing to secure a customer.
rows.key_quote: Q1 for me was the quarter where Gorilla moved from turnaround into scale. And scale is not always pretty in the first few innings.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record-breaking Performance: Achieved record Q1 revenue of $43.8B (up 88%) and record non-GAAP EPS of $4.86 (up 214%).

2. Explosive AI Growth: Booked $24.4B in AI orders, recognized $16.1B in AI server revenue, and exited with a record $51.3B AI backlog.

3. Broad-Based Strength and Share Gains: Revenue grew across all segments, with traditional servers up 92%, CSG up 17%, and storage up 8%, accompanied by market share gains.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant Supply Constraints: Management repeatedly stated that demand is significantly outpacing supply, with memory (DRAM/NAND) and CPUs being the primary constraints limiting growth.

2. Gross Margin Rate Compression: The consolidated gross margin rate fell to 18.1% as revenue from lower-margin AI servers grew nearly 9x and became a larger part of the mix.

3. Inflationary Component Costs: The company is operating in a highly inflationary environment for key components like DRAM, NAND, and CPUs, requiring frequent repricing for customers.
rows.key_quote: Demand was stronger than we anticipated... with customers moving to secure supply across a broad range of IT needs.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong Q2 delivery guidance of 100,000-106,000 units, representing >60% QoQ growth. 2. Successful launch of the flagship GX SUV, with over 80% of initial orders for the premium RMB 350,000+ trim. 3. Accelerating international expansion, with Q2 overseas revenue expected to exceed 20% of total revenue and a Q4 goal of 10,000+ monthly overseas deliveries.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Q1 revenue decreased 17.6% YoY and 41.4% QoQ due to lower deliveries amid market volatility. 2. Vehicle margin declined to 12.1% from 13.0% in Q4 2025 due to increased component costs. 3. Net loss widened to RMB 1.78 billion for Q1 2026, compared to a loss of RMB 0.66 billion in Q1 2025.
rows.key_quote: we are entering a period of strong growth driven by 4 new models, increasing production capacity and expanding international business.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong cash generation: Generated nearly $600M in full-year free cash flow ($177M excluding a one-time payment) and has been FCF positive for 5 consecutive quarters.
2. Strong DAT Segment Growth: DAT revenue grew 12% in Q4, driven by Infosec and Cyber products, and secured a key follow-on award for the PTSG program.
3. Significant deleveraging: Reduced net leverage ratio to 3.1x by paying down $743M of debt during the fiscal year.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Communication Services Decline: The segment's revenue fell 2%, driven by a 24% decline in fixed residential services which offset growth in aviation.
2. Moderating Aviation Growth Outlook: Management guided that increased competition will reduce the rate of growth in aviation services in FY27.
3. Weak Maritime Performance: Maritime revenue declined 1%, and management pushed back the expected inflection to growth until later in FY27.
rows.key_quote: Viasat has recently seen double-digit revenue earnings growth in aviation, offset by declines in fixed residential services and maritime.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Commitment growth acceleration: CRPO grew 20% and RPO grew 28%, driven by large, multi-year customer deals for AI transformations, signaling future revenue acceleration.
2. Strong AI-driven demand: Over 600 customers with >$100k ACV now use Elastic's AI capabilities, which are driving platform consolidation wins, particularly in security.
3. Significant margin expansion outlook: Guided FY27 non-GAAP operating margin to ~19% (from 16.4% in FY26) and raised the medium-term FY29 target from >20% to ~25%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Cloud mix shift impacted Q4 revenue: A higher mix of new cloud commitments (vs. self-managed) deferred revenue recognition, impacting the reported quarter's growth rate.
2. Weak monthly cloud/SMB segment: The self-serve monthly cloud business grew only 3% and is considered a 'flattish business,' indicating weakness at the low end of the market.
3. Initial FY27 growth deceleration: Guided Q1 FY27 total revenue growth of ~13.1% is a sequential deceleration from the 16% reported in Q4 FY26, though management projects acceleration through the year.
rows.key_quote: CRPO growth accelerating to 20%... Organizations are increasingly choosing Elastic for their long term AI transformations and making larger multi year commitments...

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Aerie brand's exceptional growth: Revenue surged 34% with a 25% comp, led by a 45% comp in apparel, surpassing $2B in trailing 12-month revenue.
2. Strong consolidated results: Total revenue grew 10% to $1.2B, with comps up 8% and operating income of $28M beating expectations.
3. Significant gross margin expansion: Gross margin increased 860 basis points to 38.2%, driven by lapping prior year inventory write-downs (710 bps) and expense leverage.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. American Eagle brand weakness: Brand revenue declined 2%, primarily due to underperformance in women's bottoms and soft demand for seasonal categories.
2. Q2 margin headwinds: Guidance includes a $20M incremental tariff headwind and SG&A growth in the mid-teens due to planned advertising investments.
3. Elevated inventory cost: Inventory cost grew 27% versus a 5% unit increase, reflecting tariff impacts and lapping last year's write-down, posing a potential risk.
rows.key_quote: Aerie saw broad based strength across key categories led by a 45% comp in Aerie apparel, a key driver of the success.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong Earnings & ROE Growth: EPS increased 21% year-over-year, and ROE rose over 200 basis points to 14.4%. 2. Record Segment Performance: Wholesale Banking, Wealth & Insurance, and Canadian P&C all delivered record results, showcasing broad-based strength. 3. Ahead on Strategic Goals: Already achieved full-year structural cost reduction target of $900 million and tracking well ahead of pace on AI value generation.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Ongoing AML Remediation: U.S. AML remediation remains the top priority, with associated costs guided at ~$500 million for the year. 2. Macroeconomic Uncertainty: A performing reserve build was taken due to an updated macroeconomic outlook, reflecting concerns about trade, tariffs, and geopolitical conflict. 3. Elevated U.S. Expenses: U.S. Banking expenses rose 10% year-over-year, driven by investments in governance, control, and business growth initiatives.
rows.key_quote: Strong revenue performance this quarter was driven by momentum in our markets-driven businesses, margin expansion and volume growth in Canadian Personal and Commercial Banking.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong commercial momentum with net bookings of $2.9 billion, a 19% year-over-year increase, and a net book-to-bill of 1.36x. 2. Biotech win rates experienced a 5-point sequential uptick, a key strategic focus area. 3. RFP flow increased by a low double-digit percentage, indicating strengthening demand.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. An internal investigation found improper revenue recognition and material weaknesses in financial controls, requiring restatements. 2. Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin collapsed to 15.5% primarily due to a >$50 million negative impact from revised cost-to-complete estimates. 3. Full-year 2026 guidance implies organic revenue decline and an adjusted EPS range ($10-$11) significantly below 2025's result ($12.53).
rows.key_quote: Changes made to cost to complete estimates in our full-service business impacted earnings by over $50 million in the quarter.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Exceeded Q1 guidance: Revenue grew 18%, and EPS came in above the high end of the guidance range. 2. Raised full-year outlook: Increased guidance for revenue (to $8.155B-$8.215B), non-GAAP operating margin (to approx. 39%), and free cash flow. 3. Strategic acquisition: Announced acquisition of MaintenX, a high-growth leader (50%+ growth, >$135M ARR) in asset operations, to expand into a $40B TAM and bolster AI data strategy.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Sales reorganization impact: Acknowledged go-to-market changes caused expected weakness in new subscription growth during Q1. 2. Slower RPO growth: RPO growth was 9%, impacted by a strategic shift to shorter-duration annual contracts as multi-year discounts were reduced. 3. Acquisition dilution: The MaintenX acquisition will be dilutive to margins in the near term, though management plans to absorb it within long-term goals.
rows.key_quote: Underlying business momentum was a bit better than assumptions, with strength coming from AECO, particularly in construction and emerging markets.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record pipeline generation for new AI products, described as "bigger than anything we have ever seen." 2. Strong go-to-market execution, including increased sales productivity, strong pipeline build, and low AE attrition. 3. New products, especially Identity Governance, drove 25% of Q1 bookings and deliver a 40% ACV uplift in deals.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. New AI agent products are still in early days and did not materially contribute to Q1 revenue. 2. Full-year revenue growth guidance includes a 1-point headwind from a strategic shift of professional services business to partners. 3. Full-year free cash flow margin guidance includes a 1-point headwind from lower interest income due to stock buybacks and debt settlement.
rows.key_quote: Our new product portfolio represented approximately 25% of Q1 bookings, a meaningful increase from Q1 last year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record total trading volume of HKD 4.15 trillion (+29% YoY), driven by the AI investment theme and Hong Kong market volatility.
2. Strong international client acquisition, adding 225,000 net new funding accounts, with Malaysia leading all markets in growth.
3. Underlying profitability remains robust, with adjusted net income (excluding the regulatory fine) increasing 36% YoY to HKD 2.9 billion.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. A massive one-time administrative penalty of RMB 1.85 billion from the CSRC caused reported net income to decrease 61% YoY.
2. New regulatory restrictions will impact Mainland Chinese clients, who represent 13% of funded accounts and contribute approximately 20% of total revenue.
3. Interest income declined 13% sequentially, attributed to lower income from security borrowing & lending and bank deposits.
rows.key_quote: Total trading volume reached a record HKD 4.15 trillion, up 29% year-over-year, as client interest shifted towards AI infrastructure beneficiaries.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Profitability: Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 25% from 20% YoY, and the company achieved its fourth consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability.
2. Usage-Based Model Traction: ARR for the new Operations Cloud pricing model nearly doubled from Q4 to Q1, and these usage-based offerings now represent nearly 10% of total ARR.
3. New Customer Acquisition: Acquired over 600 new customers for the fifth consecutive quarter, demonstrating continued demand and a strong product-led growth motion.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Stagnant Top-Line Growth: Revenue grew only 1% YoY to $121M, and Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) was flat compared to the prior year.
2. Declining Net Retention: Dollar-based net retention (DBNR) fell to 97%, indicating that customer churn and contraction are outpacing expansion revenue.
3. Flat Full-Year Guidance: The company reiterated its full-year revenue guidance to be "essentially flat year over year," signaling no near-term growth re-acceleration.
rows.key_quote: The ARR of customers on this [Operations Cloud] model nearly doubled from Q4 to Q1, which gives us confidence in the business model transformation.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Commercial and international franchise segments grew a combined 34.1%, driven by new store openings in markets like Germany, The Philippines, and Italy.
2. Gross margin increased 700 bps to 63.8% (or 140 bps excluding a tariff refund) due to higher average unit retail.
3. Dollars per transaction increased, driven by improvements in both units per transaction and price increases, indicating strong engagement from visiting customers.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Q1 revenue fell 2.4% to $125.3M, missing expectations, driven by declines in the direct-to-consumer segment.
2. Domestic store traffic declined 7% and e-commerce demand fell 26.1%, attributed to macro pressures and ongoing challenges with AI search changes.
3. A pronounced drop-off in store visits from the teen and adult ('cadult') demographic, which was a key growth driver in the prior year.
rows.key_quote: This year...we have seen a more pronounced drop in store visits from this demographic [teens and adults], impacting overall results.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. User base growth: Average mobile DAUs reached a record 80.73 million in March, up 4.9% YoY. 2. Strong shareholder returns: Announced RMB 500 million interim dividend and has already executed ~$62.3M of its $200M share buyback. 3. Strategic expansion: Launched overseas platform 'YesAuto' in Thailand and piloted a new online car purchasing feature for its new retail business.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Significant EPS plunge: Non-GAAP diluted EPS fell ~56% YoY from RMB 3.52 to RMB 1.54. 2. Historic auto market downturn: Management stated Q1 was the "first quarter in history where NEV sales recorded a year-over-year decline" of 21% in China. 3. Gross margin erosion: Gross margin contracted to 75.5% from 78.3% in the prior-year period.
rows.key_quote: Retail sales of passenger vehicles declined 17% year-over-year, while NEV sales declined 21% year-over-year... the first time in history.

rows.positive_highlights:
Q4 net sales grew 20.6% and diluted EPS from continuing operations increased 53%.
Strong demand driven by customer AI journeys led to a record backlog and 25% growth in the product segment.
Demonstrated significant operating leverage, with full-year adjusted EBITDA up 49.5% on 22.1% revenue growth while keeping headcount flat.
rows.negative_highlights:
Consolidated gross margin declined to 24.6% from 26.5% year-over-year, primarily due to a sales mix shift towards lower-margin large enterprise customers.
Issued conservative FY27 guidance for mid-single-digit growth, a major deceleration from FY26's performance.
Management cited a 'worldwide memory chip shortage and geopolitical issues' as potential headwinds impacting future results and guidance.
rows.key_quote: Leading to increased demand for infrastructure modernization across the breadth of our focused product categories.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record quarterly revenue of $86.4M, up 30% YoY, driven by 33% growth in the Grid business.
2. Record order bookings of nearly $100M, fueled by traditional energy, utilities, and a notable 10% from the data center sector.
3. 12-month backlog grew 40% YoY to a record of over $280M, providing strong visibility for fiscal 2026.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Q1 FY26 EPS guidance is sequentially lower, as the reported Q4 non-GAAP EPS of $0.31 included a large one-time tax benefit not expected to repeat.
2. Gross margin of 27.3% was negatively impacted by 170 basis points due to non-cash purchase accounting from the Comtrafo acquisition.
3. Operating expenses increased year-over-year to $18.8M from $15.6M, driven by costs from the Comtrafo acquisition.
rows.key_quote: Fourth quarter orders reached nearly $100 million driven by strong utility and traditional-energy demand.

rows.positive_highlights:
AI Cloud Dominance: AI cloud gross billings surged 90.1% YoY to RMB 1.0 billion, surpassing 50% of public cloud revenue for the first time, driven by strong AI agent and coding demand.
Robust Revenue Growth: Total revenue increased 37.2% YoY to RMB 2.7 billion, propelled by a 47.5% YoY growth in the Public Cloud segment.
Strong Ecosystem Momentum: Revenue from the Xiaomi and Kingsoft Ecosystem partners grew 68.9% YoY, leading the company to revise future annual transaction caps upwards.
rows.negative_highlights:
Gross Margin Compression: Adjusted gross margin fell to 13% from 17% in the prior quarter, pressured by higher AI-related server costs and upfront investments for customer activities.
Supply Chain as a Bottleneck: Management identified supply chain capacity for computing resources as the "primary limiting factor" for growth, constraining their ability to meet surging customer demand.
Massive Capital Investment: The company plans a full-year CapEx of RMB 15-20 billion, highlighting the high capital intensity required to compete and capture market share in the AI cloud space.
rows.key_quote: AI cloud gross billings reached RMB 1.0 billion, up 90.1% YoY, accounting for over half of public cloud revenues for the first time.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. AI-driven demand fueled strong performance, especially in hardware-assisted verification solutions for hyperscalers. 2. Raised full-year guidance for revenue, non-GAAP op margin (to 41%), non-GAAP EPS, and free cash flow (to $2B). 3. Design IP segment bottomed in Q1 and is recovering, with a 90%+ win rate for PCIe 7.0 IP and over 150 total UCIE wins.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Design IP segment revenue declined approximately 6% year-over-year, indicating the recovery is still in its early stages. 2. Design start activity in analog, industrial, and automotive end-markets remains 'fairly muted'. 3. The pending divestiture of the processor IP solutions business will reduce revenue by approximately $40 million for the remainder of the fiscal year.
rows.key_quote: Hardware assisted verification remained a key growth driver, with particular demand from hyperscalers and leading semiconductor customers, who are scaling emulation and prototyping.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised full-year revenue and operating margin guidance, reflecting strong Q3 results and higher TCV bookings expectations (Q3 TCV bookings grew over 20%).
2. Significant traction with its external storage support initiative, winning large deals where customers retained existing storage hardware, simplifying migration and avoiding hardware costs.
3. Increased uptake of the NC2 public cloud solution, as customers leveraged it to bypass long lead times and high prices for on-prem server hardware.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Persistent server hardware supply chain challenges are causing higher prices and long lead times, delaying revenue recognition and are expected to continue into FY27.
2. Management is taking a 'prudent approach' to Q4 guidance due to challenges conducting new business in the Middle East because of geopolitical instability.
3. Q4 revenue guidance was perceived as slightly cautious, reflecting the combination of supply chain constraints and regional uncertainty.
rows.key_quote: Our support of external storage platforms is simplifying migrations to Nutanix… without requiring significant hardware changes.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. AI-driven efficiency in Professional Services compressed engagement hours by over 40%, boosting the segment's gross margin to 10% (up 1,100 bps YoY).
2. Strong AI adoption with 'Banking Advisor' usage up >38x since October and the first customers consuming their entire 'Intelligence Unit' bundles, proving the consumption model.
3. Achieved the 'Rule of 40' with 12% subscription revenue growth and a 28% non-GAAP operating margin, which itself grew 79% YoY.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. U.S. Mortgage business faces tough comps, with guidance forecasting a -2% YoY subscription revenue decline for the segment in Q2 due to elevated mortgage rates.
2. A portion of the Q1 operating income beat ($1.7 million) resulted from delayed timing of marketing expenses, not solely core operational outperformance.
3. Management is not flowing through the entire Q1 operating income outperformance to full-year guidance, choosing to retain some for 'operating flexibility'.
rows.key_quote: AI tooling and methodologies are already compressing professional services hours per engagement by >40%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Personal Systems Growth: Revenue grew 13% YoY driven by both commercial (up 14%) and consumer (up 10%), with AI PCs now comprising 44% of shipments.
2. Effective Cost Mitigation: Successfully executed a plan to manage rising memory/storage costs, resulting in better-than-expected Personal Systems operating margins (5.2%) and a consolidated EPS beat.
3. Raised EPS Guidance: Company raised its full-year EPS guidance to $2.90-$3.10, reflecting strong confidence in its ability to manage future cost headwinds.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant Input Cost Headwinds: Management expects memory and storage costs to continue increasing in Q3 and Q4, putting pressure on gross and operating margins.
2. Anticipated Margin Compression: Personal Systems operating margins are expected to fall below the long-term range for the rest of the year, with Q4 being a "low point".
3. Weak PC Market Outlook: The company aligns with forecasts for the PC unit TAM to decline in the high-teens for the second half of the calendar year.
rows.key_quote: We continue to grow in high value categories, and accelerate our mitigation strategy to manage commodity cost pressures which allowed us to deliver EPS above our guidance.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Total revenue grew 11% YoY to RMB 106.2 billion, driven by a 20% increase in transaction services revenue.
2. Announced a major strategic pivot to a first-party brand model, backed by a RMB 100 billion long-term investment plan to upgrade its supply chain.
3. Expanded logistics support to remote regions, reducing shipping costs for merchants by up to 80% and driving order growth of over 30% to Western provinces for some.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. GAAP diluted EPS fell 14.7% to RMB 8.48 from RMB 9.94 in the prior year, reflecting increased investments.
2. Gross margin deteriorated as Cost of Revenues grew by 15% YoY, outpacing the 11% revenue growth.
3. Management highlighted challenges of "homogeneous competition" and a slowdown in online marketing services growth, necessitating a major organizational restructuring and heavy investment phase.
rows.key_quote: our priority is long-term value creation through sustained investments in the ecosystem and the supply chain rather than short-term results.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Revenue grew 55% YoY to $28.2M, and operating cash flow turned positive to $6.6M, a $17.3M improvement. 2. Raised full-year revenue guidance to $160M-$200M based on strong contracted project timelines. 3. Major progress in strategic AI infrastructure build-out with key projects in India (Yotta) and Thailand (200MW campus) advancing.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Reported a large operating loss of $41.1M, driven by a $20.9M stock compensation charge and an $18.9M foreign exchange loss. 2. Gross margin for the quarter was lower than desired due to a hardware-heavy sales mix and aggressive pricing to win a deal. 3. Acknowledged potential supply chain risks for project completion, citing market shortages in memory and CPUs.
rows.key_quote: Q1 for me was the quarter where Gorilla moved from turnaround into scale. And scale is not always pretty in the first few innings.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Massive Revenue Outlook Raise: FY27 revenue forecast increased to ~40% YoY growth (nearly $11.5B), and FY28 introduced at ~45% YoY growth ($16.5B), driven by accelerating data center demand.
2. Accelerating Interconnect Growth: The interconnect business growth forecast for FY27 was raised to over 70% YoY from a prior 50%, fueled by strong demand for 800G/1.6T PAM, DCI, and emerging scale-up optics.
3. Strong Custom Silicon Momentum: Custom silicon business is projected to more than double in FY28, driven by existing XPU programs and over a dozen XPU-attach programs, tracking towards a $10B+ target in FY29.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Communications & Other Segment Decline: The communications and other end market is guided to decline mid-single digits sequentially in Q2, though it is expected to grow YoY.
2. Increased Prepayments for Capacity: The company is making ~$1 billion in prepayments to secure future supply, highlighting a very tight supply chain to meet massive demand.
3. Slight Sequential Gross Margin Dip Guided: The Q2 non-GAAP gross margin guidance midpoint of 58.75% is slightly below the 58.9% reported in Q1, reflecting product mix dynamics.
rows.key_quote: Notably, we expect our interconnect business to grow more than 70% year over year, well above our prior expectation of 50% growth.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Agentic AI Momentum: Agentforce ARR surpassed $1 billion and the platform processed 28.6 trillion tokens, up 152% QoQ. Top AI users increased spend 1.5x in the last year.
2. Strong Slack Performance: Slack drove nearly half of million-plus dollar wins, up 80% YoY, with Slack Agentic Work Units (AWUs) growing nearly 350% QoQ.
3. Record Large Deals: Secured a record 98 Q1 deals over $1 million in new ACV, and bookings for premium AI SKUs (A1E & A4x) grew nearly 60% YoY.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Specific Product Weakness: Guidance reflects ongoing weakness in Marketing and Commerce clouds, and increased softness in Tableau bookings and renewals.
2. Lowered Cash Flow Guidance: FY27 Operating and Free Cash Flow growth guidance was updated to 4-5% from a higher level, due to a 5-point headwind from debt issuance for the ASR.
3. Softness in Tableau: Tableau was specifically and repeatedly mentioned as a source of softness in both bookings and renewals, acting as a drag on results.
rows.key_quote: Our top 10 customers by Q1 AWU usage have increased their total Salesforce spend by 1.5x in the last year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Risk metrics improved significantly: C2M2 ratio fell 17% sequentially to 0.8% and new loan FPD 7 declined 20% from Q4.
2. Funding costs were reduced by 10 bps sequentially due to an increased proportion of ABS in the funding mix.
3. The tech solutions business grew strongly, with empowered loan volumes up sevenfold year-over-year to RMB 9.96 billion.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Profitability declined sharply: Non-GAAP net income fell approximately 51% year-over-year to RMB 946 million.
2. Loan volume contracted: Total loan origination volume declined 7.5% sequentially to RMB 65 billion as the company prioritized risk over scale.
3. Weak Q2 guidance: Management projects a 47%-51% year-over-year decline in non-GAAP net income for the upcoming quarter.
rows.key_quote: Rather than pursuing scale, we proactively optimized our user and asset mix to strengthen overall health and long-term resilience of our business.

rows.positive_highlights: New moisturizing hand soap formulas drove double-digit increases in AUR and SKU productivity. The White Barn Neutral candle collection grew approximately 20% and attracted a younger demographic. The new Amazon sales channel shows strong week-over-week growth and is acquiring younger, more affluent customers.
rows.negative_highlights: The core Body Care category significantly underperformed, declining mid-teens due to missteps in the 'everyday luxury' assortment. Overall net sales fell 3.2% as 'underlying business trends remain pressured.' Adjusted gross margin declined 270 basis points to 42.7% due to tariffs, inflation, and negative category mix.
rows.key_quote: Body Care underperformed...this reflected...actions within our everyday luxury franchise, where we pulled back too substantially on the assortment.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Gross margin expanded 90 bps to 33.9% Y/Y, driven by lower technician labor costs as a percentage of sales.
2. Strategic initiatives are showing progress, with the ConfiDrive inspection tool effectively driving higher-margin service sales.
3. Despite a weak Q4, the company achieved positive comparable store sales for the full fiscal year 2026 for the first time in three years.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Comparable store sales fell 2.4% in Q4, primarily driven by a 5% decline in tire units.
2. Consumers are deferring high-ticket purchases and trading down to lower-cost tires, with Tier 4 mix growing from 25% to 30% of sales.
3. The near-term outlook is weak, with May month-to-date comps down approximately 3% due to consumer 'pocketbook pressure'.
rows.key_quote: The primary driver of our comp store sales decline was a 5% decline in tire units as consumers defer spending on high-ticket categories.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong Q1 performance with revenue up 8.1% to $142.4M and adjusted EPS increasing to $0.32 from $0.08, driven by strong retailer replenishment and robust direct-to-consumer growth (movado.com +12.8%, company stores +10.2%).
Gross margin expanded to 57.3% from 54.1%, driven by favorable channel/product mix and a temporary benefit from the elimination of the IEPA tariff.
Management signaled confidence with a 5% ($0.05) increase in the quarterly dividend to $0.40 per share, citing a strong balance sheet with $225M in cash and no debt.
rows.negative_highlights:
The Middle East region was 'extremely challenging' due to ongoing conflict, significantly dampening overall international sales growth.
The company declined to provide a full-year fiscal 2027 outlook, citing 'economic and geopolitical uncertainty,' including the Middle East conflict.
Management expects sales growth to moderate in Q2 following strong Q1 retailer replenishment and is experiencing inventory shortages in key Movado brand styles.
rows.key_quote: Sales growth was driven by retailer replenishment, and continued consumer response to our Bangle collection, Museum Valeura, and the new Mini Bold Evolution tank.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Data Center sales grew 158% year-over-year to over $400 million in Q4, driving overall company revenue growth of 47%.
2. Announced a landmark $4 billion long-term agreement with a key customer for data center cooling products for calendar years 2027-2029.
3. Issued very strong FY27 guidance with revenue growth of 20-35% and adjusted EBITDA growth over 40%, led by a 60-80% forecast for the Data Center segment.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Gross margin declined due to severe weather causing production disruptions (20 shifts lost in data centers) and costs related to recent acquisitions.
2. Facing short-term supply chain challenges with key component shortages, which will temporarily impact Q1 production schedules and efficiency.
3. The Performance Technologies segment saw its adjusted EBITDA decline 15% from the prior year due to lower sales volume and higher material/tariff costs.
rows.key_quote: The main driver was data centers, which grew $246 million or 158%.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Revenue grew 35% year-over-year, exceeding guidance, driven by broad-based strength and market share gains. 2. Operating profit increased over 90% year-over-year, demonstrating strong leverage and operational discipline. 3. Evergreen//1 storage-as-a-service (SaaS) sales grew 73% year-over-year, indicating strong adoption.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Unprecedented supply chain crisis is causing component shortages and rapid cost escalations, especially for NAND. 2. A significant portion of revenue growth (estimated at one-third) is from price increases and customer pull-ins, creating uncertainty about future demand sustainability. 3. Product gross margins are at the low end of the target range (65.5%) due to rising costs, with only a gradual recovery expected.
rows.key_quote: We estimate price increases and customer pull ins represented nearly a third of our Q1 year on year revenue growth.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Payment Solutions revenue grew 40% YoY, primarily driven by the contribution from the Access One acquisition. 2. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 23%, with adjusted EBITDA growing to $30.5M from $20.8M YoY, demonstrating strong operating leverage. 3. The Access One securitization facility was increased by $100M to $300M and expanded to non-investment grade clients, increasing the cross-watch opportunity into Phreesia's base.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Network Solutions clients are committing lower spend for the second half of fiscal 2027, creating more forecasting variability and pressure on growth. 2. Subscription revenue saw a 6% sequential decline, part of a deliberate strategy but signaling a continuing mix shift away from this recurring revenue line. 3. The company implemented a restructuring plan post-quarter end to reduce operating expenses, indicating a proactive need to align costs with current business priorities and a more challenging outlook.
rows.key_quote: deliberately moderating subscription pricing to keep retention strong, drive the downstream economics in Payments and Network Solutions.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. The core DICK'S business delivered a very strong 6% comparable sales growth, demonstrating broad-based strength across all categories. 
2. The Foot Locker turnaround is showing early success, with a 6.4% comp in the U.S. Foot Locker banner and its first overall positive comp since Q4 2024. 
3. The 'Fast Break' store remodel program for Foot Locker is proving highly effective, delivering double-digit comps and meaningful margin improvement in remodeled locations.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Consolidated non-GAAP gross margin declined 328 basis points to 33.42%, primarily due to the inclusion of the lower-margin Foot Locker business. 
2. Full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance was maintained, not raised, as strong operational results were offset by a projected $0.25 unfavorable impact from a higher consolidated tax rate. 
3. The Foot Locker business in Europe is lagging the U.S. turnaround and is expected to trail the U.S. business through the end of the year.
rows.key_quote: Our Fast Break stores delivered double-digit comps in Q1 and meaningful merchandise margin improvement.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Partner Vericel awarded a new 10-year BARDA contract for NexoBrid, valued at up to $197 million, with MediWound to share in procurement and development revenues starting H2 2026.
2. Reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $24M to $26M despite a weak Q1, based on expected second-half ramp in government contract revenues.
3. Market dynamics for EscharEx improved significantly due to Medicare reimbursement changes expected to reduce sales of competing CTP products by ~90%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Q1 revenue declined 62.5% to $1.5 million from $4.0 million year-over-year, due to timing of BARDA revenue and postponed shipments.
2. The EscharEx Phase III VALUE study timeline was delayed, with enrollment completion pushed back to the end of Q1 2027 due to slower recruitment.
3. Operating loss increased to $8.0 million from $5.2 million YoY, and net loss per share worsened to $0.23 from $0.07 YoY.
rows.key_quote: The decrease was primarily attributable to timing of BARDA-related revenue as well as postponed shipment related to regional conflict.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Significant margin expansion: Operating margin improved 130 bps YoY to 26.4%, driven by the 'Ignite' operating system which delivered ~200 bps of strategic pricing. 2) Strong End-Market Growth: Diagnostics & Clinical grew 11%, Chemicals & Advanced Materials grew 8% (fueled by semiconductor demand), and Pharma grew 6%. 3) Instrument Momentum: High single-digit instrument growth, with LC/LCMS and GC growing low-double-digits, driven by a strong replacement cycle and market share gains.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) China Weakness: Revenue in China declined 9% YoY, which was more than expected, due to Lunar New Year timing and softness, though H1 was flat. 2) Food Market Decline: The Food end market declined 3% due to delayed government spending and funding in China and India. 3) Academia & Government Softness: The A&G market declined 5%, in line with expectations, reflecting tight government funding.
rows.key_quote: The operational and P&L benefits from our Ignite operating system are increasingly becoming structurally embedded in the business.

rows.positive_highlights:
Product revenue growth accelerated to 34% YoY, up from 30% last quarter, marking the strongest sequential dollar growth in company history.
Raised FY'27 product revenue growth guidance significantly from 27% to 31%, driven by rapid adoption of new AI product Cortex Code (CoCo) and core business strength.
Raised FY'27 non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 13.5% from 12.5%, demonstrating disciplined execution and operating leverage despite investments.
rows.negative_highlights:
New AI products like Cortex Code carry a lower gross margin than the core platform, requiring cost offsets to maintain the 75% product gross margin target.
Management acknowledged the potential for customers to 'govern or throttle' the use of consumption-based AI tools to contain costs, a potential future headwind.
Co-Founder and Chief Architect Benoit Dageville is stepping away from day-to-day operations, representing a significant transition in the company's technical leadership.
rows.key_quote: AI is accelerating consumption across our core platform and our native AI products, Snowflake Intelligence and Cortex Code are scaling rapidly, already contributing meaningfully to revenue.

rows.positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS surged 40% to $3.67 and ROE increased 370 bps to 13.5%, driven by record fee income and 16% pre-provision pretax earnings growth. The U.S. Banking segment reached an "inflection point," delivering 4% sequential commercial loan growth after completing its optimization program. Capital Markets and Wealth Management delivered record performance, with Capital Markets PPPT at $900M (up 31%) and Wealth Management net income up 39% on strong markets and AUM growth of 30%.
rows.negative_highlights: Canadian consumer credit is showing pressure, with rising delinquencies and provisions in the unsecured portfolio reflecting macro weakness and high insolvencies. Consolidated Net Interest Margin (NIM) declined 4 basis points sequentially, partly due to holding higher levels of low-yielding liquid assets for prudent liquidity management. The outlook for the Canadian economy remains "mixed with modest near-term growth," creating a potential headwind for Canadian-focused segments.
rows.key_quote: Record net income of $2.7 billion, driven by robust fee revenue across Capital Markets, Wealth Management and Treasury and Payment Solutions.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Revenue grew 30% YoY to $211M, the fourth straight quarter of acceleration. 2) Robust bookings driven by competitive takeaways, with customers >$500K growing 33% YoY. 3) Dollar-based net retention improved 100 bps to 110% (111% for large customers).
rows.negative_highlights: 1) Non-GAAP gross margin declined to 67.4% from 69.3% YoY, due to messaging mix and new headcount. 2) Announced the departure of CFO Isabelle Winkles after six years. 3) Faced supply constraints for Decisioning Studio implementations, though hiring is now accelerating to address this.
rows.key_quote: Q1 bookings were robust, driven by competitive takeaways particularly in the enterprise.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Revenue grew 56% YoY (25% organic) to $1.965B, driven by fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) work which grew 33% sequentially.
2. Raised full-year revenue guidance significantly, with Building Systems segment margins now expected in the high teens.
3. Achieved record backlog of $11.9B (+25% sequentially) and improved DSOs by 15 days YoY to 96.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Rising fuel costs were noted as a headwind being managed across the business.
2. Announced acquisition will increase pro forma net leverage to below 2.5x adjusted EBITDA.
3. Significant continued investment is required to support rapid growth and integrate acquisitions.
rows.key_quote: our fiber to the home works grew 33% in 1 quarter's time.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Profitability & Capital Return: Adjusted PTPP earnings grew 16% YoY and ROE rose to 13.2%; the bank raised its dividend by $0.04 and repurchased 6.4 million shares.
2. Broad-based Segment Strength: Canadian Banking PTPP grew 13% on margin expansion, International Banking earnings grew on strength in Mexico (+25% earnings), and Global Wealth saw record net sales of $4.7B.
3. Robust Revenue & Margin Growth: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY, while All-Bank NIM expanded 24 bps YoY and 6 bps QoQ, driven by higher-margin assets and lower funding costs.
rows.negative_highlights:
