1. Elevated Credit Losses & Revised Guidance: PCLs rose to $1.2B (66 bps), leading management to revise impaired PCL guidance for the rest of 2026 to the mid-50 bps range, higher than before.
2. Large Single Impairment: A single corporate loan in Brazil accounted for ~7 basis points of the bank-wide impaired PCLs, prompting analyst questions about concentration risk.
3. Strain in Canadian Retail: While savings deposits grew, overall Canadian deposits fell 3% YoY due to term deposit outflows. Management noted that prolonged inflation could further strain vulnerable consumers.
rows.key_quote: The return on equity was 13.2%, up 270 basis points year-over-year, driven by strong revenue growth of 13%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong regional performance in Americas and APAC: Americas sales grew 3% and APAC sales grew 24%, showing strength in key markets. 
2. Full-Year Guidance Maintained: Despite new headwinds, the company reaffirmed its full-year outlook for 3-5% sales growth and 12-12.5% operating margin. 
3. Successful ERP Implementation: A multiyear merchandising ERP upgrade was completed, strengthening the company's operational foundation for future growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant Weakness in EMEA: Sales declined 10% in EMEA due to regional conflict in the Middle East, negatively impacting total company Q1 sales by over 50 basis points. 
2. Q2 Margin Pressure: Q2 operating margin is guided to ~10%, a significant year-over-year decline, driven by a 120 bps unfavorable tariff impact and increased marketing spend. 
3. Hollister Brand Flatness: Hollister's net sales were flat, underperforming the Abercrombie brand, primarily due to its higher exposure to the weak EMEA market.
rows.key_quote: Continued growth in the U.K. was more than offset by declines in the Middle East...driving EMEA sales down 10% for the quarter.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Gross margin expanded 490 basis points to 64.8%, including a $40M tariff refund and driven by higher AURs and full-price watch-throughs.
2. Michael Kors full-price comparable store sales turned positive across all regions, demonstrating traction for new products and brand storytelling.
3. Jimmy Choo revenue grew 5.3%, exceeding expectations with double-digit growth in the Americas and growing momentum in accessories.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Total company revenue declined 3.7% to $796 million, impacted by strategic reductions in promotional and off-price sales at Michael Kors.
2. Michael Kors brand revenue decreased 5.5%, with the Americas region declining 14% due to the ongoing 'quality of sale' initiatives.
3. The Michael Kors outlet channel remains a drag on performance, with sales down mid-single digits and acting as a headwind into H1 FY2027.
rows.key_quote: Actions taken to improve quality of sale... reduced fiscal 2026 revenue by over $150 million, with this headwind expected to moderate.

rows.positive_highlights:
Record Q4 revenue of $309M (up 34%) and record adjusted EBITDA of $83M (up 39%), driven by acquisition contributions and 2.8% consolidated organic growth. 
Pro forma organic revenue for Contractor Solutions grew 5.5%, with the Aspen acquisition outperforming the market by delivering 10.4% growth in the quarter. 
Management increased the run-rate synergy target for the Mars acquisition from $10M to 'in excess of $12 million,' reflecting strong integration progress.
rows.negative_highlights:
Adjusted gross margin declined 70 basis points year-over-year to 43.5%, pressured by acquisition-related dilution, cost inflation, and tariffs. 
Free cash flow was a negative $6.8 million, a sharp decrease from a positive $22.8 million in the prior-year quarter, due to working capital for growth, acquisition costs, and higher interest expense. 
The company took a $15.6 million impairment charge related to the strategic exit of its non-core GRD business line.
rows.key_quote: This outperformance was driven by acquisitions that are outperforming our acquisition models and are also helping to support organic growth.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Significant risk improvement: FPD7 (new loan risk indicator) declined by ~20% sequentially, and C2M2 delinquency ratio fell ~17% to 0.8%. 2. Cost optimization success: Overall acquisition costs fell ~17% sequentially, and funding costs were reduced by ~10 basis points. 3. Strategic shift to quality: Spending on high-quality users increased ~40% sequentially, improving the user mix and asset portfolio health.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Financials declined: Loan volume dropped 7.5% sequentially, and non-GAAP net income fell 11.6% sequentially to RMB950 million. 2. Weak macro environment: Management cited soft consumer credit demand, broad-based asset quality pressure, and a fifth consecutive quarterly decline in industry loan balances. 3. Cautious guidance: Projected a 47-51% year-over-year decline in Q2 non-GAAP net income, signaling continued headwinds.
rows.key_quote: Our FPD7, a leading risk indicator for new loans, declined by approximately 20% in Q1 compared with Q4 last year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Revenue grew 11% YoY, the first quarter of double-digit growth in over 12 quarters, driven by strong AI product adoption.
2. The 'Enterprise Advanced' suite is driving momentum with a 30-40% price premium and a net retention rate higher than the company's overall 105%.
3. Operating margin expanded 240 bps to 27.7%, and the company raised its full-year revenue and EPS guidance, signaling sustained strength.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Foreign exchange rates created a significant headwind, reducing reported billings growth to 5% from 13% in constant currency.
2. FX headwinds are expected to continue, impacting the full-year revenue outlook by ~90 bps and the EPS outlook by ~$0.08.
3. CEO noted that advanced AI agent use cases are still 'relatively early in the journey', indicating much of the expected AI-driven growth is still prospective.
rows.key_quote: This outperformance was driven primarily by strong Q1 bookings fueled by continued momentum from customers upgrading to Enterprise Advanced.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Wholesale revenue surged 58.1% YoY to RMB 1.06 billion, driven by strong AI demand and customer move-ins, becoming the largest revenue contributor.
2. Secured massive new orders totaling 519 megawatts year-to-date, demonstrating strong market demand and a high pre-commitment rate of 85.8% on capacity under construction.
3. Margins expanded, with adjusted EBITDA margin rising to 33.1% from 30.4% YoY and adjusted cash gross margin improving to 45.0% from 43.1% YoY.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. High capital expenditure guidance of RMB 10-12 billion for the full year requires significant financing through asset recycling (REITs) and other channels.
2. Delivery of capacity is heavily back-loaded to the second half of 2026, which introduces execution risk for the full-year plan.
3. Increased reliance on very large wholesale contracts, including 400 MW and 110 MW orders from a single customer, increases future customer concentration risk.
rows.key_quote: Wholesale revenues, our key revenue growth driver, increased significantly by 58.1% to RMB 1.06 billion for the first quarter.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Data Center revenue hit a record $71.6M (+39% YoY) with guidance for 35% sequential growth in Q2. 2. LoRa revenue grew to $44.5M (+14% YoY) with guidance for >15% sequential growth in Q2. 3. Strong Q2 guidance with revenue up 13% sequentially to $328M and adjusted EPS up 20% sequentially to $0.61, with expected acceleration in the second half of the year.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. GaN chip demand currently exceeds supply by approximately 3x, potentially limiting upside until capacity expansion is completed. 2. Signal Integrity segment gross margin declined sequentially to 62.7% from 67.4% due to the ramp-up costs of a newly acquired facility. 3. The planned divestiture of the cellular module business, while progressing, has not yet been successfully closed.
rows.key_quote: Data center sales... a record $71.6 million... the result of sustainably increased customer engagement, portfolio alignment, and supply assurance.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. AI products gaining traction: 'AI Protect' solution bookings crossed $100 million in the past 12 months, signaling a strong new growth vector.
2. Strong platform expansion: 'Zero Trust Branch' ARR tripled year-over-year and 'Data Security' ARR grew over 30% YoY to cross $500 million.
3. Record profitability: Non-GAAP operating margin reached an all-time high of 23%, demonstrating strong operating leverage and disciplined investment.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Sales leadership turmoil: The departure of two sales leaders prompted a 'prudent approach' to guidance, creating significant uncertainty around near-term execution.
2. Major growth deceleration guided: Preliminary FY27 guidance calls for 16-17% growth, a sharp slowdown from the current 25% run-rate.
3. Weak new logo outlook: Management stated it took a 'tempered view of new logos' for the FY27 outlook, indicating a key growth engine is underperforming expectations.
rows.key_quote: At the end of the third quarter, 2 sales leaders departed... we are taking a prudent approach to our guidance during this transition.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Revenue grew 13.5% YoY to $37.7M, exceeding guidance, with Q2 guidance implying acceleration to 13.7%-16.6% growth.
2. GAAP net income more than doubled YoY to $1.1M, marking the 6th consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability.
3. New conversational AI product usage shows strong early momentum, growing over 150% sequentially each quarter since its launch.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Gross margin decreased to 63.4% from 68.0% YoY, due to the initial negative margin of the new subscale conversational AI business.
2. Dollar-based net retention rate was 99%, indicating a slight revenue decline from the existing customer cohort year-over-year.
3. Operating cash flow was negative $4.3 million, a significant decrease from a positive $17.6 million in the prior year's quarter.
rows.key_quote: Results reflected continued expansion of usage growth of our real time engagement services in sectors such as US live shopping, social and entertainment.

rows.positive_highlights:
App Growth Platform (AGP) revenue grew 57% YoY in Q4, driven by its brand business (+58%) and DTX/SSP business (+60%).
Adjusted EBITDA grew 53% YoY in Q4 with margin expanding nearly 500 bps to 22%, demonstrating significant operating leverage.
International On-Device Solutions (ODS) saw over 40% YoY growth in revenue per device (RPD) due to strong advertiser demand.
rows.negative_highlights:
CFO Stephen A. Lasher is stepping down, creating a leadership transition in a key role.
The company reported a GAAP net loss of $7.3 million for the quarter.
Total debt remains significant at $361 million, though the company is actively deleveraging.
rows.key_quote: Our rates were up 40% year-over-year in our HEP business, a direct result of better targeting AI capabilities.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong AirDial momentum: AirDial services revenue grew 80% YoY, new lines installed more than doubled, and bookings increased over 75%, driving the overall beat.
2. Raised full-year guidance: Both revenue and EPS guidance were increased, reflecting confidence from the strong Q1 results and future outlook.
3. Residential stabilization and innovation: The residential user base grew for the first time in many quarters, aided by the launch of the new 'MyPhone' product which is gaining retail traction.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Worsening product margins: Product gross margin was -31% and is expected to decline to approximately -40% for the full year due to higher component costs and new product launch expenses.
2. Dependency on external factors for POTS growth: A key growth driver's pace depends on actions by carriers like Verizon, which management noted has not yet begun sunsetting many lines.
3. Uncertainty in new product revenue: Management expressed conservatism in forecasts for new 'MyPhone' and 'Ooma AI' products, as customer adoption and financial impact are still unknown.
rows.key_quote: The biggest driver of the upside was from AirDial... we are happy with the outcome of it. Obviously, exceeded by a good amount.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Achieved record annual home sales of 26,622 since going public in 2018.
2. Q4 revenue grew 4.6% to $621.3M, outperforming the broader HUD market which declined 9%.
3. Announced strategic acquisition of Homes Direct, adding 11 retail locations and ~$70M in annualized revenue, and refreshed share repurchase program to $150M.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Guided Q1 adjusted gross margin to 24.5%-25.5%, a decline from 25.7% in Q4, due to input cost inflation lagging pricing actions.
2. Forecasted flat year-over-year revenue for Q1, signaling a deceleration from 4.6% growth in Q4 due to consumer affordability challenges.
3. Management highlighted accelerating inflation on key inputs like forest products, steel, and petroleum, creating near-term cost pressure.
rows.key_quote: The largest portion of our gross margin headwind is the input cost inflation, as actions that we're taking to offset it will lag a bit.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. easyJet Holidays grew passengers by 22% and profitability (PBT) by 39% to GBP 61 million.
2. Aircraft utilization increased 20% vs 2023, returning to pre-COVID levels, and a GBP 250 million cost benefit from fleet upgauging was quantified for FY27-28.
3. Maintained a strong balance sheet with a GBP 434 million net cash position and 72% of summer fuel hedged at a favorable $726/mt.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Performance was hit by market oversupply on key beach routes (e.g., London-Spain) due to competitors redeploying capacity away from Tel Aviv.
2. Faced significant cost inflation, with CASK ex-fuel up 8% in H1, driven by airport fee hikes (Schiphol +35%) and other investments.
3. Consumer uncertainty led to a shortened booking window, with Q4 bookings currently lagging 7% behind last year, creating risk for summer yields.
rows.key_quote: Performance was impacted by market oversupply on thick beach routes, as most airlines pulled out of Tel Aviv and redeployed them on longer-leisure flows.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Profit: Achieved all-time high adjusted consolidated profit of JPY 535.2 billion (up JPY 211.8B YoY), surpassing the FY2030 target.
2. P&C Profitability: Domestic P&C profit increased by JPY 95.9B, driven by a JPY 70B improvement in the base profitability of Fire & Casualty insurance.
3. Shareholder Returns: Announced a 33% increase in the FY2026 dividend to JPY 200 per share, marking the 13th consecutive year of dividend growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Buybacks Paused for M&A: Management is holding back on share buybacks to secure capital for a potential large M&A, creating uncertainty around returns beyond dividends.
2. Market Softening Overseas: Management acknowledged that insurance rates are "softening in all lines of business, excluding casualty," potentially slowing overseas top-line growth.
3. Complex ROE Calculation: The unadjusted FY2026 ROE forecast is ~11%, below the 13% target, requiring complex adjustments and explanations from management about performance.
rows.key_quote: The main contributors were a plus JPY 70 billion in improved base profitability of Fire & Casualty and JPY 15 billion increase in investment income.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Lucky Star Foods operating profit increased by over 40% to ZAR 324 million, driven by strong margins from low-cost inventory and reduced promotional spend.
2. Wild Caught Seafood operating profit surged from ZAR 74 million to ZAR 204 million, benefiting from record prices, efficient operations, and a ZAR 43 million fuel hedge gain.
3. The balance sheet significantly de-risked, with the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio improving from 2.2x to 1.1x due to debt repayments and lower working capital.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. The SA Fishmeal & Oil division suffered a ZAR 139 million operating loss (vs. a ZAR 5 million loss prior year) due to a near-total failure of anchovy and red-eye landings.
2. Consolidated group revenue declined by 6%, reflecting the collapse in the SA fishmeal segment and lower global prices impacting the US business.
3. The flagship Lucky Star brand is facing raw material shortages, forcing the company into 'allocation mode' and constraining sales volumes for the upcoming quarter.
rows.key_quote: ...where we've had challenges, other businesses have stepped up and replace the earnings that we've seen a drop off.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record FY2025 Profits: Group adjusted profit reached a record JPY 1,000.9 billion, up JPY 269.1 billion YoY.
2. Strong International Growth: Overseas subsidiaries' profit increased by JPY 77.4 billion, driven by revenue growth in Europe/Americas and lower natural catastrophe losses.
3. Robust Shareholder Returns: FY26 dividend guided to increase to JPY 170/share, with a total of JPY 270 billion in share repurchases planned for the fiscal year.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Lower FY2026 Profit Guidance: Adjusted profit is forecast to fall to JPY 800 billion from JPY 918.9 billion (IFRS) in FY25, primarily due to assuming normalized, higher natural catastrophe losses.
2. Significant Merger Costs: The FY26 forecast includes a substantial JPY 111 billion in pre-tax merger-related expenses, a sharp increase from JPY 42.5 billion in FY25.
3. Domestic Life Insurance Loss: The domestic life insurance business profit decreased by JPY 74.9 billion in FY25, driven by a JPY 51.9 billion loss at one subsidiary from the sale of securities.
rows.key_quote: This growth was mainly driven by higher premium income, a decrease in natural catastrophe losses and increased dividend and interest income.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Applied Electronics segment operating profit grew 41% due to strong execution of a healthy order book and favorable currency hedging. 
2. Announced a strategic, capital-efficient European defense JV with CSG, backed by a binding 3-year launch order, to manufacture fuses in Slovakia. 
3. Circuit breaker business showed strong export growth to the U.S., partially offsetting weakness in the power cables division.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Electrical Engineering segment operating profit declined 40%, driven by double-digit volume declines in the cables business due to weak infrastructure demand in SA and Zambia. 
2. Group HEPS fell by 22%, impacted by the poor cables performance and a ZAR 52 million negative swing from non-trading share-based payment charges. 
3. Overall profitability severely impacted by challenging macro conditions, including record-high copper prices (up 17% in rand terms) and South Africa's gross fixed capital formation falling to a 25-year low.
rows.key_quote: The negative volume growth in the cable business primarily drove a 40% decline in profitability.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Overseas business matured into a second profitable engine, contributing 30% of group revenue with 35% YoY revenue growth and 88% YoY operating profit growth.
2. Improved risk metrics in China, with vintage delinquency easing 30 basis points and Day-1 delinquency improving, allowing for cautious re-engagement in growth.
3. Strong shareholder returns, including a new US$150 million share buyback program and a 10.5% year-over-year dividend increase.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Ongoing regulatory uncertainty in China, particularly new rules for online marketing of financial products, creating a 'regulatory fog'.
2. Flat sequential transaction volume for the group (RMB 42.6B), as well as for the individual China (RMB 38.5B) and Overseas (RMB 4.1B) segments.
3. Significant foreign exchange fluctuations offset 13% sequential operating profit growth, resulting in only 1% sequential net income growth.
rows.key_quote: Overseas markets again deliver 30% of group revenue... It has matured into a second profitable engine.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Profitability Acceleration and Margin Expansion: Underlying profit before tax (PBT) grew 16% with the PBT margin expanding to 51%, driven by successful cost control initiatives alongside strong revenue growth.
2. Record Inflows and Market Share Gains: The Transact platform achieved record gross inflows of over £6 billion and net inflows of £2.4 billion (+14% YoY), capturing 25% of the market's net inflows.
3. Confident Outlook and Shareholder Returns: Management reaffirmed cost growth guidance of 3% for FY26 and FY27 and increased the interim dividend by 15%, signaling confidence in sustained performance.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Platform Revenue Margin Moderation: The platform revenue margin declined by 1 basis point due to clients progressing through the tiered pricing structure and prior-year fee reductions for family portfolios.
2. Increased Regulatory Capital Requirements: Regulatory capital needs rose significantly during the period due to formulaic changes for its investment firm and actuarial valuations, absorbing some liquidity.
3. Reduced Wrapper Fee Income: This revenue stream decreased compared to the prior year, reflecting the full impact of a reduction in charges for family-linked portfolios implemented in H2 of the previous fiscal year.
rows.key_quote: This record revenue, combined with the slowing growth in the cost base, has driven group underlying profit before tax up 16%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Achieved GBP 73 million in ODI outperformance, driven by a 33% reduction in pollutions, 41% reduction in spills, and an 8% improvement in leakage.
2. Upgraded FY'28 EPS guidance to 'at least 250p' due to strong ODI delivery and a new GBP 150 million operating cost efficiency commitment.
3. Proposed GBP 600 million of additional investment ('reopener') focused on long-term asset health, supported by customer research.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Incurred a GBP 28 million penalty for weak performance on the C-Mex customer experience metric.
2. Confirmed ongoing investigations by regulators Ofwat and the Environment Agency, with no clear timeline for resolution or potential outcomes.
3. Acknowledged that tougher ODI targets create a GBP 20 million headwind for next year's performance just to 'stand still'.
rows.key_quote: We've reduced pollutions by 1/3, we've reduced spills by 41%, and we've improved leakage by 8% year-on-year, which is absolutely fantastic.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Diversified ecosystem (offline, fintech, e-commerce) GMV grew 42% sequentially, now accounting for nearly 50% of total GMV. 2. Asset quality improved, with day-1 delinquency ratio decreasing by ~7% Q/Q and FPD30 for new loans expected to fall ~6%. 3. New active users surged 63.3% Q/Q to 1.44 million.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Core online consumer finance business is contracting, with credit facilitation service income declining ~10% Q/Q. 2. Net profit declined 5.9% Q/Q to RMB 201 million. 3. Operating expenses rose 13.8% sequentially due to investments in the new ecosystem businesses.
rows.key_quote: Our diversified ecosystem businesses accounted for nearly 50% of our total loan volume, becoming the company's new growth drivers.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strategic progress: Completed the Ninety One transaction and increased ownership in Indian insurance businesses to over 50%, strengthening future dividend capacity.
2. Strong new business volumes: Achieved overall strong growth in new business volumes and net client cash flows, with particular strength in capital-light market-linked sales.
3. Robust capital position: Discretionary capital is at the upper end of the long-term target range, providing a strong buffer against volatility.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Weather-related claims: Suffered large reductions in underwriting profit at Santam and SanlamAllianz due to significant weather-related claims, pushing SanlamAllianz below its target margin.
2. VNB Margin decline: Reported a lower Group VNB margin, primarily driven by an unfavorable product mix shift toward lower-margin products and negative margins in the Indian life business.
3. Lower investment returns: Investment returns on shareholder funds were depressed by higher bond yields and equity market weakness in Morocco, resulting in a -7% decline in Q1 operating profit excluding investment variances.
rows.key_quote: This quarter saw volatility from investment variances and large underwriting profit reductions from large weather-related claims.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Jewellery Maisons Strength: Sales surged 14% at constant rates with double-digit growth across all regions, acting as the primary driver for the group. 2. Americas Momentum: The region grew 17% at constant rates, marking the ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. 3. Robust Financial Position: Ended the year with a net cash position of EUR 8.5 billion, generating EUR 4.9 billion in cash from operations.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Gross Margin Compression: Gross margin declined by 250 basis points to 64.4%, impacted by higher gold costs, US duties, and negative FX. 2. Specialist Watchmakers Weakness: Sales fell 4% at actual rates, and operating margin contracted sharply to 3.4% due to multiple headwinds. 3. Significant FX Headwinds: Constant currency operating profit growth of 23% was reduced to just 1% at actual rates, highlighting the severe impact of currency movements.
rows.key_quote: Jewellery Maisons sales increased 14% at constant rates with double-digit growth across all regions, underpinned by both jewelry and watch sales.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Green energy segment EBITDA grew 73% year-on-year to PLN 99 million, driven by the full contribution from the Drzezewo wind farm.
2. B2C ARPU growth accelerated to 5.8% year-on-year, reaching PLN 82.2, thanks to the successful multiplay strategy.
3. Consolidated net profit increased by over 54% to PLN 134 million, reflecting revenue growth and disciplined cost control.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Net debt to EBITDA ratio increased to 3.68x from 3.59x due to a one-off PLN 590 million payment for a spectrum license renewal.
2. Media advertising revenue grew 1.2%, underperforming the broader market's 2% growth due to a high prior-year base and competitor sports broadcasting.
3. The real estate segment showed lower revenue and EBITDA due to a high year-ago comparable from a large handover of apartments.
rows.key_quote: The main growth driver in Q1 was clearly the green energy segment. It contributed PLN 136 million to revenue and PLN 42 million to EBITDA.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. National Security portfolio grew 1.6% in Q4, driven by strong demand for Intel work, and is guided to grow mid-single digits in FY27.
2. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps to 11.1% in Q4 despite revenue declines, demonstrating strong cost discipline and contract execution.
3. Strategic shift to outcome-based work is gaining traction, with a ~50% increase in Other Transaction Authority (OTA) awards year-over-year.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Consolidated revenue declined 6.4% in Q4, with the Civil business contracting 23% due to contract cuts and smaller recompetes.
2. Civil portfolio is expected to decline by high-single-digits in FY27, creating a significant headwind for overall growth, especially in the first half.
3. FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance of $6.00-$6.35 represents a year-over-year decline from the $6.51 achieved in FY2026.
rows.key_quote: Our national security portfolio grew 1.6% year-over-year...driven by strong demand for our Intel work...As expected, our Civil business declined 23% year-over-year.

rows.positive_highlights: Q1 performance was the most profitable quarter since 2004, with VLCC TCE rates at $103,500/day.###Exceptional forward guidance for Q2, with 82% of VLCC days booked at an even higher rate of $181,700/day.###Market dynamics are surprisingly robust; rerouting of trade routes (ton-mile effect) has offset lost volumes from the Hormuz closure, keeping utilization and rates high.
rows.negative_highlights: Extreme market volatility is driven by the 'opaque and volatile political narrative' surrounding the Strait of Hormuz closure.###The vessel order book is growing and delivery windows are stretching into 2030, though management currently views it as manageable.###The company's high spot market exposure presents significant downside risk if geopolitical tensions resolve abruptly and normalize trade flows.
rows.key_quote: The long-haul trade has kind of outgrown the loss of the relatively short-haul trade from the Middle East Gulf to Far East.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Market Disruption Driving Rates: Red Sea rerouting has absorbed ~10% of effective shipping capacity, increasing demand and charter rates for GSL's vessels.
2. Strong Financial Position: Achieved a near net-zero debt position with net leverage at 0.3x and a cash position of $655 million.
3. High Contract Coverage: Secured $2.1 billion in contracted revenue with 100% charter coverage for 2026 and 86% for 2027, providing strong revenue visibility.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Global Instability Risk: While currently a tailwind, extreme geopolitical uncertainty in the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz presents underlying long-term volatility and risk.
2. Rising Operating Costs: Management acknowledged absorbing inflationary increases in vessel OpEx, specifically citing 'rising crewing costs.'
3. High Industry-Wide Orderbook: The overall orderbook-to-fleet ratio stands at a high 37%, which could lead to oversupply pressure if market demand normalizes, although it is concentrated in larger vessel classes.
rows.key_quote: Ships rerouting from the Red Sea around the Cape of Good Hope has absorbed about 10% of effective shipping capacity in the process.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Delivered bottom-line results ahead of expectations, driven by effective cost management.
2. Saw positive performance trends in premium bread and cake categories, which helped offset weakness in traditional bread.
3. Executed a major nationwide relaunch of the core Nature's Own brand, with a significant marketing push aimed at stabilizing the key traditional loaf business.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Underperformed in the traditional loaf category, which represents ~38% of branded retail, due to soft top-line trends.
2. Wider-than-desired pricing gaps with competitors following earlier price hikes negatively affected sales volumes.
3. Facing new cost headwinds from rising oil prices impacting resin and distribution, estimated at a $0.02-$0.03 per share headwind in the second half of the year.
rows.key_quote: We did take pricing late last year, and the pricing gaps have remained a bit wider than we would like in the short term.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Membership Growth: Membership fee income grew 10% to a record $132M, driven by acquisition, retention, and higher-tier penetration.
2. Successful Club Expansion: New Texas clubs are performing 33% ahead of plan on membership. Clubs opened in the last 5 years are comping +6%, over 4x the chain average.
3. Strong Gas Business Performance: Comp gallon growth reached over 10% in March/April, significantly outperforming the market and driving traffic.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Margin Pressure: Merchandise gross margin declined 10 bps (60 bps excluding tariff benefits) due to strategic price investments to return tariff refunds to members.
2. Pressured Consumer Segment: The vast majority of comp sales growth was driven by higher-income members as lower-income households face elevated costs.
3. Modest Core Merchandise Growth: Merchandise comps were a modest 1.5%, with perishables comps dampened by egg deflation and reliance on consumer electronics for GM strength.
rows.key_quote: The vast majority of our comparable sales growth was driven by our higher income members, who remain engaged and continue to shop with us consistently.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Defense Performance: Defense segment revenues grew 9% for the fiscal year, with Q4 adjusted segment operating income margin expanding to 10.2% amidst a strong demand environment.
2. Clear Transformation Plan: Management detailed a plan to generate $125-$150 million in annual run-rate savings by FY2030, including divesting 8% of revenue and rationalizing 10% of the civil simulator network.
3. Improved Free Cash Flow: Achieved a 123% free cash flow conversion rate in FY2026 under a new, stricter definition, and targets 100% cumulative conversion by FY2030, signaling strong capital discipline.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Weak Civil Segment Performance: The Civil segment was described as 'soft' with performance 'tempered' by market weakness and specific Q4 challenges from the Middle East conflict, negatively impacting utilization.
2. Guarded FY2027 'Reset Year' Outlook: Guidance for FY2027 is for low single-digit revenue growth and a 'temporary step back in margins and earnings' due to transformation costs and market headwinds.
3. Civil Network Disruption and Light Backlog: Rationalizing the training network will create 'stranded cost and attrition', while the company entered FY2027 with a 'lighter order backlog of civil full-flight simulators'.
rows.key_quote: Overall, strong Defense revenue and profit was tempered by a soft Civil market. In particular, events in the Middle East were challenging in Q4.

rows.positive_highlights: Funds under Management (FUM) grew 15.4% (10.5% in neutral currency) benefiting from strong net inflows. Non-interest income grew strongly by 13.6%, which more than offset NII decline and drove total revenue growth of 4.2%. Adjusted EPS increased by 4.8%, the dividend was raised by 5.5%, and a GBP 110 million share buyback was completed.
rows.negative_highlights: Net interest income (NII) declined by 1.6% due to the impact of lower average interest rates on the bank's endowment capital. The near-term outlook for the U.K. business is uncertain due to the political situation, leading to flat ROE guidance of 13-14% for next year. Short-term profitability is being intentionally suppressed by a heightened investment cycle, with most of the GBP 282 million program being expensed rather than capitalized.
rows.key_quote: Noninterest income grew strongly by 13.6% from increased client activity, offsetting lower net interest income caused by a drop in interest rates.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Q1 production of 23,200 Boe/d came in 10% higher than internal projections due to outperformance from new gas wells and accelerated well completions.
2. Raised full-year 2023 production guidance by 500 Boe/d to a range of 21,000-23,000 Boe/d, reflecting strong asset performance.
3. Maintained a robust deal pipeline, spending $17M on opportunity capture (89% in the Delaware) and closing an $18M PDP acquisition.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Q1 D&C CapEx was $40M higher than expected, with 75% of the variance from accelerated activity and the rest from cost inflation.
2. Full-year D&C CapEx guidance was increased by $25M at the midpoint due to cost inflation and unforecasted activity.
3. Revenue decreased 3% YoY to $91.3M despite a 46% production increase, as the growth was "more than offset by lower commodity pricing."
rows.key_quote: Our actual first quarter '23 production results came in about 10% higher than projections due to outperformance on newer gas wells.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record order intake of GBP 3.6 billion and a record backlog of GBP 4.8 billion (up over 40%), providing strong multi-year revenue visibility.
2. Significantly stronger cash generation with free cash flow of GBP 159 million (up over 40%), leading to enhanced shareholder returns via a new dividend policy and GBP 200M buyback extension.
3. Strong performance in the core UK business with 7% revenue growth, which offset challenges in the US and drove improved group profitability.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Challenging US defense services market with budgetary pressures and a shift away from services, which impacted performance and necessitated restructuring.
2. Flat group revenue (1.3% organic growth) impacted by portfolio actions, including the disposal of the US Fed IT business and exiting lower-return contracts.
3. Cautious full-year revenue guidance (3-5% growth), with the higher end dependent on gaining more clarity on customer budgets in core markets.
rows.key_quote: We've delivered strong performance in the U.K. with 7% growth offsetting stabilized performance in the U.S.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Established a new two-banner strategic direction, ending the costly rebannering program and clarifying long-term focus. 2) Maintained a strong balance sheet with $129M in cash, no debt, and continued shareholder returns via dividends and buybacks. 3) Initiated concrete corrective actions to realign product assortments with target customers, expected to drive improvement starting in the back-to-school season.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) Core performance driver was flawed product positioning, with Shoe Carnival assortments becoming too expensive and Shoe Station assortments failing to align with local demographics. 2) Q1 gross margin compressed by 120 basis points to 33.3% due to increased promotional activity and higher costs, with a much larger decline expected in Q2. 3) Management cited a deteriorating macro environment, leading to 'unusually consistent softness across all' footwear categories as consumer pressures mount.
rows.key_quote: More fundamentally, the underlying issue in the first quarter was our product positioning at both banners.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Games segment revenue grew 7% YoY to RMB 25.7 billion, driven by strength of both overseas titles like 'Where Winds Meet' and domestic franchises. 2. Consolidated gross margin dramatically increased to 69.4% from 54.1% YoY, led by margin expansion in the games business to 74.8%. 3. Key domestic titles showed enduring appeal, with 'Fantasy Westward Journey' PC hitting a new peak active user high of $3.9 million.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. NetEase Cloud Music revenue decreased 7% YoY to RMB 2.0 billion. 2. Innovative business and others revenue declined 5% YoY to RMB 1.5 billion. 3. Youdao's gross margin fell to 44.7% from 47.3% YoY, primarily due to margin decline in its Smart Devices business.
rows.key_quote: Our performance...was underpinned by continued strength of our game portfolio, both internationally and domestically.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Raised full-year operating profit margin guidance to 'slightly above 20%' due to cost control and operational savings. 2) Aerospace division delivered strong growth, benefiting from solid execution and positive pricing on recent contract renewals. 3) John Crane division maintained a positive book-to-bill ratio, indicating a strengthening order book despite regional disruptions.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) Full-year revenue growth guidance was lowered from 3-4% to ~2% due to the Middle East conflict. 2) The John Crane division experienced a £10 million negative revenue impact in Q3 due to conflict-related disruptions. 3) The Flex-Tek division declined, reflecting ongoing weakness in the U.S. construction market and tough prior-year comparators.
rows.key_quote: Reflecting the disruption we've now seen in Q3... we now expect full year growth for Smiths of around 2%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Delivered strong shareholder returns with a $0.50/share dividend and $37.9M in share repurchases.
2. Generated robust cash flow with adjusted EBITDA of $114.3 million and daily cash margin of $12,073 per vessel.
3. Management is "very positive for the next 18 months" on market outlook, citing strong ton-mile growth (up 5.1% in first 5 months) and supply constraints.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Acknowledged macroeconomic risk that very high oil prices (e.g. >$150) could "damage the world economy" and trade.
2. Noted potential China weakness, as record iron ore stockpiles create "downside risk for the second half of the year" despite strong imports.
3. Fleet faces 1,236 off-hire days and $42 million in CapEx for scheduled dry-docking in the remainder of 2026.
rows.key_quote: Ton-miles expanded at a faster pace, driven by strong Atlantic exports and longer Pacific trading distances.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Evergreen platform AUM grew 64% YoY to $17.5B, with over $1B in net inflows for the quarter despite industry headwinds.
2. Strong fundraising for Direct Equity Fund VI, which reached $2.8B, over 35% larger than the prior vintage.
3. Robust financial growth with full-year fee-related revenue up 20%, FRE up 25%, FRE margin expanding to 50%, and an 11% dividend increase.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Evergreen net flows turned slightly negative in March (-$17M) and were slower in April (+$265M), indicating sensitivity to market narrative.
2. Customized Separate Account fee-earning AUM was flat quarter-over-quarter due to distributions and fee step-downs.
3. Increased G&A expenses driven by third-party commissions and platform fees related to growing Evergreen products.
rows.key_quote: Our Evergreen platform finished the quarter with net positive inflows in aggregate...and not having to impose gates in any of our evergreen funds.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record leasing of GBP 70.9 million, 10.3% ahead of ERV, driven by strong demand for prime space and a market supply drought.
2. Successful capital recycling strategy, with GBP 490 million of sales at a premium to book value and acquisitions at a ~60% discount to replacement cost.
3. Strong value growth reflected in a 6.1% increase in EPRA NTA per share, a 4.3% portfolio valuation uplift, and a 63% increase in EPRA EPS.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Ongoing macroeconomic uncertainties, including political risk and a less accommodative interest rate environment, which could dampen investment market activity.
2. Weaker performance in the retail portfolio (13% of total), which lagged the strong growth seen in the core office assets.
3. Persistent construction cost inflation, which tempers development economics compared to previous cycles despite being actively managed.
rows.key_quote: Our excellent operational performance, delivering record leasing well ahead of target... into a Central London market starved of such quality.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. **P&C Underlying Profitability:** The attritional current year loss ratio improved by over 1 full percentage point, demonstrating strong underlying performance despite high natural catastrophe losses. 2. **Strong Life Inflows & Value Growth:** The Life segment achieved €4.3 billion in net inflows and a 19% increase in new business value, showcasing high-quality, profitable growth. 3. **Excellent P&C Revenue Growth:** P&C gross insurance revenue grew almost 7% year-on-year, with increasing positive contributions from volume growth (motor +1.8%).
rows.negative_highlights: 1. **High Natural Catastrophe Losses:** The quarter was impacted by significant Nat Cat events, primarily storms in Portugal, which exceeded the company's preventive insurance protection layer. 2. **Adverse Market Variances:** Financial market volatility in Q1 led to a negative impact of ~€900 million on the CSM and ~5 percentage points on the Solvency II ratio. 3. **One-off Tax Expense:** A new French surtax law required the recognition of a one-off tax component of approximately €50 million in the quarter.
rows.key_quote: Our underlying performance was very healthy, with a more than 1 full percentage point improvement in the attritional current year loss ratio.

rows.positive_highlights:
Green Energy segment EBITDA grew 73% to PLN 99 million, driven by full-period production from the Drzezewo wind farm.
B2C ARPU growth accelerated to 5.8% YoY, reaching PLN 82.2, driven by successful execution of the multiplay strategy.
Consolidated net profit increased by over 54% to PLN 134 million, reflecting revenue growth and effective cost control measures.
rows.negative_highlights:
Media segment's advertising revenue growth of 1.2% was slightly below the market's 2% growth, impacted by competitor Olympic broadcasts and a high base.
Leverage increased, with net debt to EBITDA rising to 3.68x from 3.59x, due to a PLN 590 million payment for a spectrum concession renewal.
The pay TV base continues to be under structural pressure, although this is partially offset by a shift to IPTV and OTT solutions.
rows.key_quote: The main growth driver in Q1 was clearly the green energy segment. It contributed PLN 136 million to revenue and PLN 42 million to EBITDA.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Revenue grew 11%, with accelerating growth in key regions like North America (14%) and strong performance from Sage Business Cloud (up 15%).
2. Operating margin expanded 80 basis points to 23.9%, driven by operating leverage and disciplined cost management, leading to 16% EPS growth.
3. Renewal rate by value increased to 102% (from 101%), reflecting price increases, strong retention, and successful cross-watching of add-ons, including new AI features.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Management noted they will face 'tougher comparators in the second half of the year,' which tempers the outlook slightly.
2. Leverage ratio stands at ~2x, which is at the 'upper end of our target range of 1 to 2x.'
3. Net finance costs were higher year-over-year following recent debt issuance, providing a slight drag on net profit.
rows.key_quote: Revenue grew by 11%. This reflects strong demand from existing customers alongside continued momentum in new customer acquisition.

rows.positive_highlights: Comparable sales grew 3.5%, the strongest in 5 years, driven by mid-single-digit growth in the Pro channel. Adjusted operating margin expanded by 410 basis points to 3.8%, fueled by merchandising initiatives. Strategic focus on 'Main Street Pro' customers is yielding over 200 basis points of outperformance in comparable sales relative to the overall Pro comp.
rows.negative_highlights: Full-year guidance was only reaffirmed despite a strong Q1 beat, citing potential consumer demand variability from rising gas prices. The strategic optimization of large national accounts created a significant headwind in the Pro channel. Adjusted gross margin was partially offset by a $17 million year-over-year LIFO expense headwind.
rows.key_quote: In our Pro business, the expanded assortment in brakes and undercar is driving above-average comps and helping us capture more Main Street business.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. AI-driven business grew from 5% to 15% of total revenue YoY, reaching £27 million, with higher margins. 2. Secured a major new partnership with Tyl by NatWest to modernize its payments acceptance platform. 3. Expanded collaboration with Google, joining its exclusive AI Agent partner program, leading to new client wins.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Revenue declined 8.4% YoY, missing guidance due to slower pipeline conversion, Middle East conflict delays, and slower execution of large deals. 2. Recorded a massive non-cash goodwill impairment of £364.6 million, reflecting the diminished outlook. 3. Adjusted PBT margin collapsed to 1.8% from 12.6% YoY, and both Q4 and full-year guidance for revenue and EPS were significantly lowered.
rows.key_quote: The primary driver of the quarter's miss and the lowered Q4 [guidance] was a slower-than-expected pipeline conversion.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Best Q1 new ACV growth in 5 years, with new ACV from agentic AI products growing over 200% year-over-year.
2. Raised FY27 non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 30.5% due to operational discipline and AI-driven productivity gains.
3. Strong AI product adoption, with over 4,000 customers using an organic agent (doubled QoQ) and approaching $500M in ARR from all agentic AI solutions.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Full-year revenue guidance was reiterated, not raised, despite a strong Q1, suggesting the outperformance was needed to remain on track.
2. Seat growth (FTEs) was described as "flattish," with declines in the tech sector being offset by other industries, indicating a sector-specific headwind.
3. RPO growth of 11% lagged CRPO growth of 15.5%, which management attributed to a mix shift towards renewals that typically have shorter durations.
rows.key_quote: In Q1, our new ACV from agentic AI products it grew more than 200% year-over-year. And we are also approaching $500 million in ARR.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Online Marketing Services revenue grew 20.9% YoY to RMB 611.1M, driven by AI-powered advertising, with over 50% growth in emerging sectors like AI apps. 2. AI-driven subscription services within the Learning segment surged over 70% YoY, with Youdao Lingshi gross billings growing by over 20%. 3. Achieved seventh consecutive quarter of operating profitability (RMB 57.5M), while narrowing net operating cash outflow by 63.6% YoY.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Smart Devices segment revenue plummeted 42.6% YoY, a result of declining demand and a strategic shift away from volume growth. 2. Consolidated operating profit fell 44.7% YoY, heavily impacted by proactive investments in AI and a high comparison base. 3. Consolidated gross margin slightly declined due to the business mix shifting towards the lower-margin, high-growth Online Marketing segment.
rows.key_quote: The rapid rise of our advertising business is, at its core, driven by our AI revolution, becoming our primary growth engine.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong asset growth: Funds under management (FUM) grew 15.4% and core loans grew 9.6%.
2. Robust non-interest revenue: Non-interest income (NIR) increased by 13.6%, offsetting NII weakness and driving overall results.
3. Resilient profitability: Adjusted EPS grew 4.8% despite a challenging macro environment and significant investment spend.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Pressure on interest income: Net interest income (NII) declined by 1.6% due to the impact of lower average interest rates on endowment capital.
2. Cautious short-term outlook: Guidance for FY2027 ROE is 13-14%, largely flat with the current year, amid market uncertainty.
3. Increased operating costs: Costs rose 4.7% driven by a major multi-year investment program (£282M) that is being expensed in the income statement.
rows.key_quote: Noninterest income grew strongly by 13.6%, supported across the business by increased activity with our clients.

rows.positive_highlights: Time charter equivalent (TCE) earnings increased to $32,300 per day from $21,100 in Q1 2025, driving a significant turnaround to a $5 million net profit from a $6.4 million net loss last year. Capesize ton-mile demand grew 4.3% YoY in Q1, driven by a 23% increase in bauxite volumes from Guinea. The company continued its dividend policy, declaring a cash distribution of $0.18 for the quarter.
rows.negative_highlights: Average vessel OpEx per day increased to $6,800 from $6,400 in Q1 2025 due to higher costs for crew, spares, and insurance. Interest expense remains a significant cost at $12.4 million for the quarter. The market's forward FFA curve implies lower future rates than management's optimistic outlook, suggesting potential investor skepticism.
rows.key_quote: Tonne-mile in Q1 for Capesize increased 4.3% year-over-year. We can yet again thank the increased bauxite volumes from Guinea.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. **easyJet Holidays Growth**: Grew passengers by 22% and profitability by 39% in H1, generating GBP 61 million PBT. 
2. **Upgauging Cost Savings**: Accelerating A319 retirements is projected to deliver GBP 250 million in P&L efficiencies by FY28. 
3. **Strong Balance Sheet**: Maintained a net cash position of GBP 434 million and GBP 4.7 billion in liquidity, providing strength to navigate volatility.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. **Demand Uncertainty**: Shorter booking windows due to consumer caution, with Q4 bookings currently tracking behind last year and August bookings down 7% YoY. 
2. **Fuel Cost Impact**: Volatile fuel pricing in March resulted in a GBP 25 million additional cost headwind. 
3. **Market Oversupply & Cost Inflation**: Faced overcapacity on beach routes due to competitor redeployments and significant airport fee hikes (e.g., Schiphol up 35%).
rows.key_quote: Market oversupply happened because most airlines pulled out of routes into Tel Aviv and redeployed them on longer-leisure beach flows.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Fundraising significantly beat expectations at $17 billion for the year, driven by a record $5.5 billion for real assets.
2. Fee-Related Earnings (FRE) grew 23% to £350 million, with the FRE margin (ex-catch up) expanding to 47%.
3. Record operating cash flow of £861 million enabled a substantial reduction in net debt to £113 million from £629 million a year prior.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. The macro investment environment remains challenging and uncertain, leading management to maintain a cautious and selective deployment strategy.
2. The balance sheet's debt portfolio generated a negative 2% return, driven by mark-to-market movements in the CLO portfolio.
3. Fundraising in FY'27 is expected to be lower than the record FY'26 level due to the natural timing of the fund cycle.
rows.key_quote: Fundraising in the year outperformed our expectations at $17 billion and fee-earning AUM grew 11% during the year.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong Strategic Execution: Closed the Ninety One transaction, increased ownership in Indian insurance businesses to over 50%, and advanced new banking services. 2. Robust New Business Volume Growth: Achieved strong growth in overall sales and net client cash flows, particularly in capital-light market-linked products. 3. Strong Capital Position: Discretionary capital is at the upper end of the target range, positioning the group well to handle future volatility.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. High Weather-Related Claims: Suffered large reductions in underwriting profit at both Santam and SanlamAllianz due to significant weather-related claims. 2. Lower VNB Margin: The value of new business (VNB) margin declined due to an unfavorable product mix shift and negative margins in the Indian business. 3. Negative Operating Profit Growth: Reported a 7% decline in operating profit (excluding investment variances) due to lower investment returns and higher claims.
rows.key_quote: ...large reductions in underwriting profit for both Santam and SanlamAllianz as a result of large weather-related claims.

rows.positive_highlights:
1) FY26 EPS grew 8% and is guided to grow "at least high single-digit" in FY27, driven by an accelerated share buyback program of ~£500M.
2) Dominant market position strengthened, with share of time spent increasing to 11x the nearest competitor group and 6x all main competitors combined.
3) Average Revenue Per Retailer (ARPR) grew 5% in FY26 to £2,995 per month, driven by price (+£117) and product (+£72) levers.
rows.negative_highlights:
1) Retailer profitability pressure led to higher cancellation levels, resulting in a net loss of 460 paying retailers in H2 FY26 and a tough run rate into FY27.
2) Weak FY27 guidance includes an expected 1-2% decline in average retailer forecourts and a negative stock lever impact of £30-£40 on ARPA.
3) Employee engagement plummeted from 91% to 72%, attributed to tougher trading, cost controls, reorganizations, and negative retailer feedback.
rows.key_quote: We have seen higher cancellation levels than in previous years, which has impacted both FY '26 and the run rate into FY '27.

rows.positive_highlights: West Elm delivered an 8.5% comp driven by new products and collaborations; B2B division grew 13.7% with contract business up 22%; Supply chain efficiencies delivered 50 bps of gross margin benefit, offsetting higher domestic shipping costs from fuel prices.
rows.negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 30 bps to 44.0% year-over-year; Merchandise margins fell 100 bps due to higher tariff costs; Management did not raise full-year guidance despite the Q1 beat, citing significant external uncertainty.
rows.key_quote: Our 4.8% comp was driven by strong performance at all of our brands, growth from our B2B division, and continued outperformance of emerging brands.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record Q2 sales ($741M, +7% organic) with all 3 segments contributing to growth. 2. Backlog surged 18% organically year-over-year, driven by accelerating order entry. 3. Full-year sales and EPS guidance were raised due to strong demand momentum, particularly in semiconductor end markets.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Medical and Fluid Solutions (MFS) margins were slightly compressed due to a near-term product start-up headwind. 2. Consolidated incremental EBITDA margins of 31% were on the low end of the company's target range. 3. Management noted operating in an inflationary environment, including tariffs, which is creating cost pressures.
rows.key_quote: Order entry momentum continued... driving up backlog 18% organically compared to the prior year.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Construction & Forestry (C&F) showed exceptional strength with sales up 29% and full-year sales guidance raised to +20%, driven by infrastructure spending. 2. Small Ag & Turf (SAT) delivered a strong quarter with sales up 16% and a 20.6% operating margin, offsetting weakness elsewhere. 3. Full-year net income guidance was maintained at $4.5B-$5.0B, demonstrating resilience through business diversification and strong execution.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. The Large Ag (Production & Precision Ag) segment remains weak, with sales down 14% due to lower shipment volumes amid muted customer sentiment. 2. The South American ag industry outlook was significantly worsened, with the forecast cut to a 15% decline from a 5% decline due to economic pressures in Brazil. 3. Ongoing tariff costs remain a significant headwind, with a run rate of $1.2 billion for the year, equivalent to a ~3% margin headwind.
rows.key_quote: While large ag is operating below trough levels, small agriculture and turf is progressing towards mid-cycle and Construction & Forestry is slightly above mid-cycle.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Accelerated top-line growth with GMV up 12.9% YoY, driven by an 11% increase in transacting customers to 66,000.
2. Achieved first-ever Q1 non-GAAP adjusted net profit of RMB 1.7 million, a significant turnaround from a RMB 50.2 million loss YoY, driven by operating leverage.
3. Strong growth in key segments: SME customer GMV grew over 20%, key industry accounts (new energy, electronics) grew over 20%, and overseas business revenue increased sixfold.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Gross margin declined to 16.7% from 17.2% YoY, attributed to a product mix shift towards lower-margin categories like diesel and transformer oil.
2. The company remains unprofitable on a GAAP basis with an operating loss of RMB 22.5 million.
3. R&D expenses were reduced by 25.9% YoY, a potential concern despite the company's focus on AI development.
rows.key_quote: Our prior investments in warehouse network optimization and automation drove a 36% year-over-year improvement in warehouse utilization efficiency.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Gross Margin Expansion: "Gross margin increased to 24.4% from 23.2% in the prior year period" due to favorable category mix and operational discipline.
2. Strong SVIP Growth: "Our SVIP members who grew by 9% year-over-year. Their paid members accounting for... 55% of our online spending."
3. Shanshan Outlet Strength: "Shenzhen Outlet business is quite strong in the first quarter, and the GMV growth around 30% year-over-year."
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Negative Q2 Revenue Guidance: "we expect our total net revenues to be between RMB 24.5 billion and RMB 25.8 billion, representing a year-over-year decrease of approximately 5% to... 0%."
2. Worsening Sales Trend: "following the holiday period, we saw a very apparent moderation of sales in March and as we enter the second quarter, the April data does not turn out very well... into May to date, still very challenging."
3. Core Online Category Weakness: "online, we have seen a very notable decline... the real weakness is actually going into a discretionary -- more discretionary apparel categories like women's and men's wear."
rows.key_quote: Our first quarter performance reflected a significant calendar-driven shift caused by the later Chinese New Year... resulting in the soft March.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong eCommerce growth (26% enterprise) driven by faster delivery and a nearly 50% increase in U.S. Marketplace sales. 2. Improving profit mix, with higher-margin Advertising (+37%) and Membership (+17%) businesses now comprising roughly one-third of operating income. 3. Favorable merchandise mix contributed to U.S. gross margin expansion (+29 bps) for the first time in 18 quarters, led by strength in General Merchandise.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Significant fuel cost pressure, which negatively impacted operating income by $175 million or ~250 basis points of growth. 2. Noted signs of stress among lower-income consumers due to budget pressures. 3. Pharmacy sales faced a 100 basis point comp headwind from maximum fair pricing legislation.
rows.key_quote: Q1 marked the first time in 18 quarters that merchandise mix contributed favorably to Walmart U.S. gross margin expansion.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record Q1 deliveries of 83,465 vehicles (+98.3% YoY), driving revenue up 112.2% to RMB 25.5 billion. 2. Gross margin expanded significantly to 19.0% (vs. 7.6% YoY), with vehicle margin reaching 18.8% due to a favorable mix of high-margin models like the ES8. 3. Achieved positive non-GAAP operating profit and positive operating cash flow, boosting cash reserves to RMB 48.2 billion.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Expects significant cost pressure of over RMB 10,000 per vehicle starting in Q2 from rising material and memory chip costs. 2. Guided Q2 vehicle margin to decrease to 17-18% from 18.8% in Q1 due to cost headwinds. 3. The ONVO brand continues to face challenges with lower brand awareness, requiring increased marketing efforts and time to build.
rows.key_quote: The vehicle margin increase was mainly due to the higher contribution by higher-margin models, especially the ES8 which has over 20% vehicle margin.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong International Performance: Revenue grew 14.1% (7.9% ex-FX) with units up 5.9%, driven by strength in the U.K., Germany, and Canada.
Record U.S. ASPs and Gross Margin Expansion: U.S. insurance ASPs increased 4.1% to a record high, and global gross margin expanded by 71 basis points to 46.3%.
Growth in Ancillary Businesses: The Purple Wave industrial auction platform saw Gross Transaction Value (GTV) grow over 25% LTM, and the non-insurance "whole car" segment is successfully attracting "crossover buyers."
rows.negative_highlights:
Declining U.S. Insurance Volume: U.S. insurance unit volume fell 4.2% due to softer claims activity from consumer pullback on insurance coverage.
Overall Unit Decline: Global unit volume declined 2.4%, with insurance units down 2.7% and U.S. total units down 4.2%.
Consumer Retrenchment: ISS Fast Track data shows earned car years declined 4% YoY while vehicles in operation grew, indicating consumers are dropping insurance coverage.
rows.key_quote: We continued to see expansion in average watching prices, which rose 4.6% and more than offset a modest decline in unit volumes of 2.4%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Achieved $50 million in CP Kelco cost synergies one year ahead of schedule.
2. Delivered $53 million in productivity savings, progressing toward an increased $200 million 5-year target.
3. Asia Pacific delivered robust performance with EBITDA up 9% despite tariff pressures.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Pro forma revenue declined 3% due to muted market demand and volume decreases.
2. A $20 million profit benefit from bio-gums capacity consolidation is delayed from FY2027 to FY2028, creating an earnings headwind.
3. Specific weaknesses in European bulk sweeteners and Latin American sweetener volumes drove approximately 50% of the total revenue decline.
rows.key_quote: Specific challenges affected us in Europe... impacted by lower bulk sweetener revenue and in Latin America, where we saw lower sweetener volumes.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Stormwater revenue increased 12%, driven by a 43% growth in Allied Products sales which included a $49 million contribution from the NDS acquisition. 2. Full-year free cash flow was $569 million, up significantly from $369 million in the prior year, driven by profitability and working capital management. 3. The integration of NDS is proceeding ahead of plan, with management increasingly excited about cross-watching opportunities beyond the initial $25 million cost synergy target.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. FY2027 guidance assumes significant inflationary pressure on material and transportation costs, which pricing actions will only offset on a dollar-for-dollar basis. 2. Core pipe revenue decreased 2% in the quarter, reflecting continued softness in the residential and infrastructure markets. 3. Management warned of a potential "air pocket" in summer sales due to customer pre-watching ahead of price increases, creating choppy demand.
rows.key_quote: Stormwater revenue increased 12%, driven by a 43% increase in Allied Products sales, including the $49 million contribution from the NDS acquisition.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Achieved record quarterly adjusted EPS of $3.19 (+7% YoY) and record full-year adjusted EPS, driven by favorable price/mix and OpEx discipline. 2. Recorded highest book-to-bill ratio in nearly 4 years at 1.1x, with orders outpacing revenue across all business lines, signaling a potential demand recovery. 3. Energy Systems segment revenue grew 7% with operating margin up 130 bps, bolstered by strong demand in data centers and broadband.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Consolidated organic volume declined 6% YoY due to softness in electric forklift and transportation markets. 2. Adjusted gross margin decreased 170 basis points to 29.5% due to a net $20 million year-over-year impact from higher freight and tariff costs. 3. Motive Power segment revenue fell 6% and operating margin contracted 280 basis points due to lower volumes and lost operating leverage.
rows.key_quote: Net sales came in at $988 million, up 1%... driven by a 4% benefit from price/mix... partially offset by a 6% decrease in organic volume.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. **Growth Engine Acceleration:** Revenue in core 'growth engines' grew 24%, with customer locations growing 11%, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of location growth acceleration.
2. **Profitability and Margin Expansion:** Full-year adjusted free cash flow turned positive ($18M). Transaction-based gross margin rose to 31% from 29%, and normalized software gross margin improved to ~82% from 81% last year.
3. **AI-driven Efficiency & Product:** AI is now resolving over 80% of support tickets, significantly reducing costs, while new AI-powered product features are increasing adoption and platform value.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. **Slowing Software Revenue Growth:** Consolidated software revenue growth moderated to 6% Y/Y (from 9% in growth engines) due to lapping prior price increases and a strategic shift to annual contracts with upfront discounts.
2. **Negative Hardware Gross Margins:** Hardware margins remained deeply negative due to discounting and incentives used as a loss-leader strategy to acquire new customers and attach payments.
3. **Quarterly Cash Flow Timing:** The company posted negative adjusted free cash flow of $13 million in Q4, which management attributed almost entirely to the timing of working capital.
rows.key_quote: Our performance was bolstered by the strength of our growth engines, where we saw total revenue up 24%, GTV up 19% and locations up 11%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. HOKA achieved its largest quarter ever with revenue up 15% to $671M, driven by new products and robust global DTC growth. Full-year revenue grew 16% to $2.6B.
2. UGG grew 8% for the full year to $2.7B, with over half of the growth coming from newer sneaker and sandal collections, successfully diversifying beyond seasonal boots.
3. Profitability remained strong with Q4 gross margin increasing 90 bps to 57.6% and a full-year operating margin over 23%, fueled by high levels of full-price watching.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. FY27 gross margin is guided down to 56.5% from 57.7% in FY26, attributed to higher freight costs from shipping disruptions and increased input costs.
2. FY27 operating margin is projected to decline to ~21.5% from 23.1% in FY26, as the company intentionally increases SG&A investments in marketing, personnel, and technology.
3. EPS for the reported quarter (Q4) declined to $0.96 from $1.00 in the prior year, partially due to a strategic shift of expenses into the quarter.
rows.key_quote: HOKA delivered its largest quarter ever, driven by new products in road and trail, and robust global DTC growth.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Q4 revenue grew 12%, beating expectations, driven by a 17% increase in retail comps and 28% growth in Asia (including +50% in China). 2. Average Unit Retail (AUR) increased 16%, fueled by stronger full-price watching and favorable mix, contributing to a 40 bps gross margin expansion to 69%. 3. High-potential categories (women's apparel, outerwear, handbags) grew over 20%, outpacing overall company growth and validating the product expansion strategy.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. FY27 guidance for Europe is cautious (low-to-mid single digits) due to macro pressures, energy costs, and potential disruption to Middle East tourism. 2. Management signaled a normalization of wholesale growth in FY27, following a period of stronger performance and reorders in FY26. 3. The outlook assumes a sequential increase in tariff headwinds in the second half of FY27, which could pressure margins if relief is not extended.
rows.key_quote: Gross margin expansion was driven by stronger than expected AUR growth and favorable channel mix, more than offsetting the planned step up in U.S. Tariffs.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record-breaking comparable store sales growth of 17%, the highest in company history, driven primarily by transaction growth. 2. Double-digit growth in customer count across all demographics, including younger shoppers, fueled by marketing initiatives. 3. Operating margin expanded 120bps to 13.4% on lower COGS and sales leverage, contributing to a 37% increase in EPS to $2.02.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. SG&A deleveraged 25 basis points, despite a 17% comp, due to higher incentive compensation costs. 2. Management expects elevated fuel prices to pressure both ocean and domestic freight costs for the rest of the year. 3. Packaway inventory, a key source of value, decreased as a percentage of total inventory to 36% from 41% last year.
rows.key_quote: The comp increase was primarily driven by a growth in transactions, and we saw healthy increases in customer count on a comp store basis.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Fulfilled order growth accelerated to 14.3% YoY, driven by successful platform governance initiatives that improved freight quality. 2) High-margin transaction service revenue surged over 33% YoY, as commission penetration rate increased by 9 percentage points to over 94%. 3) Platform fulfillment rate hit a new record of 44.1%, and average shipper MAUs grew 13% YoY to 3.11 million, indicating a healthier ecosystem.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) Total net revenue growth was slow at 5.5% YoY, intentionally suppressed by the strategic shift away from the high-revenue, low-margin self-operated freight brokerage business. 2) Management noted that oil price volatility could cause some near-term softening in long-haul freight demand for low-value goods. 3) The transition of the freight brokerage service to an aggregator model (1-2% fee) from a self-operated one (~10% take rate) will continue to be a drag on reported total revenue growth.
rows.key_quote: The structural improvements from our governance initiatives are increasingly translating into tangible business momentum and reaccelerating order growth across our platform.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Enterprise Acceleration & Platform Wins: Enterprise revenue grew 7.2% YoY, with 15 of top 20 deals being multi-product wins, often displacing competitors like Teams and Cisco.
2. AI-Driven CX Growth: Zoom Customer Experience (ZCX) saw 'high double-digit' growth, with paid AI included in 9 of the top 10 ZCX deals.
3. Raised Guidance & Buyback: Raised full-year revenue and EPS guidance and announced a new $1 billion share repurchase authorization, signaling strong confidence.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Increased Online Churn: Average monthly churn in the online business increased to 3.0% from 2.8% in the prior-year quarter.
2. Sub-100% Net Dollar Expansion: Enterprise net dollar expansion rate was 99%, indicating slight net churn among existing customers, though it was an improvement sequentially.
3. Implied Back-Half Deceleration: Full-year guidance of 4.4% growth implies a slowdown from the 5.5% growth in Q1, particularly in the online segment.
rows.key_quote: Zoom customer experience continued to accelerate in Q1 with high double-digit growth driven by paid AI in 9 of the top 10 ZCX deals.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record double-digit growth: Achieved an eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth with revenue up 15.3%, adjusted EBITDA up 16.7%, and adjusted EPS up 18.3%.
2. Strong diversified performance: Volume-related revenue grew 17.7% due to high volatility, while non-volume-related revenue grew 13.4%, driven by acquisitions (Admincontrol, Euronext Athens) and custody services.
3. Strategic execution success: Successfully launched Nordic Power Futures, capturing ~90% market share, and made significant progress on CSD expansion with major custodians onboarded for September 2026 launch.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Higher operating costs: Underlying expenses increased by 12.7% (5.2% excluding acquisitions) due to strategic investments in technology and talent, though revenue growth was higher.
2. Net Treasury Income decline: NTI decreased by 11.6% due to client margin efficiencies following the migration of Italian markets to a new clearing framework.
3. Slight fixed income softness: MTS cash volumes experienced a slight reduction due to a temporary widening of bid-offer spreads linked to a conflict in Iran.
rows.key_quote: Volume-related revenue increased 17.7%, driven by elevated market volatility, resilient revenue capture, and strong market share management.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Massive FY27 Guidance & GTA VI Launch Date: Initial FY27 net bookings guidance of $8.0B-$8.2B (~20% growth), driven by the confirmed November 19 launch of Grand Theft Auto VI.
2. Strong Q4 & FY26 Beat: Q4 net bookings of $1.58B beat the high-end of guidance, driven by outperformance from the Grand Theft Auto series, Red Dead Redemption, and mobile titles.
3. Broad-based Divisional Strength: NBA 2K delivered record FY26 bookings, Zynga had its best year since acquisition (Toon Blast +25% YoY), and GTA series recurrent consumer spending grew 5% in Q4.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Cautious FY27 Mobile Outlook: Guidance assumes the mobile segment will be down year-over-year as trends on several mature titles are expected to moderate.
2. Softer NBA 2K Q4 Trends: Recurrent consumer spending was 'softer than anticipated' in Q4 as spending moderated from extreme growth seen earlier in the fiscal year.
3. Weaker Q1 FY27 Guidance: Net bookings for the upcoming first quarter are projected to decline to $1.32B-$1.37B, compared to $1.42B in the prior year.
rows.key_quote: Our initial financial outlook for fiscal 27 includes record net bookings of $8 to $8.2 billion... led by the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Online sales grew 15.5% due to enhanced user experience and fulfillment. 2. Pro segment maintained momentum, benefiting from loyalty programs and strong in-stocks. 3. Delivered positive comp sales for the fourth consecutive quarter (+0.6%) despite a challenging market and weak DIY demand.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Gross margin declined 70 bps to 32.7%, primarily from the dilutive impact of FBM and ADG acquisitions. 2. DIY demand remains under pressure, contributing to a 0.9% decline in comparable transactions. 3. Q2 adjusted EPS is expected to decline approximately 2% year-over-year due to margin pressures from acquisitions and investments.
rows.key_quote: While DIY demand remains under pressure, we're continuing to grow market share in a challenging housing environment.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Wild Caught Seafood turnaround: Operating profit surged from ZAR 74M to ZAR 204M, driven by record market prices, improved catch rates, and a ZAR 40M fuel hedge gain.
2. Lucky Star margin expansion: Operating profit grew over 40% on flat volumes due to improved margins from lower inventory/procurement costs and reduced promotions.
3. Strong outlook for US Fishmeal (Daybrook): A looming global supply shortage due to El Niño in Peru is expected to drive fishmeal and oil prices 'substantially' higher, strongly benefiting the division.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. SA Fishmeal & Oil collapse: The division recorded a ZAR 139M operating loss (vs ZAR 5M loss prior year) due to a near-total lack of anchovy and red-eye landings, leading to high unrecovered fixed costs.
2. Lucky Star supply constraints: faces raw material shortages, forcing it into 'allocation mode,' limiting promotional activity and creating a constrained outlook for Q3 sales.
3. Disappointing Squid performance: The squid business had a 'very poor year' due to a cyclical trough in the species, despite recent investments in new vessels and rights.
rows.key_quote: Strong performances by Lucky Star and Wild caught seafood helped offset lower results from fishmeal, reflecting the benefits of the group's diversified business model.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Raised full-year guidance for revenue and all non-GAAP metrics. 2. Strategic growth engines (assisted tax, money, mid-market) all grew over 30%. 3. TurboTax Live revenue grew 36%, now representing over half of total TurboTax revenue.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Disappointing performance in the price-sensitive DIY tax segment, where the company "lost on price". 2. Announced a 17% reduction in workforce as part of a major restructuring. 3. Mailchimp revenue was down slightly and requires "rightsizing".
rows.key_quote: I am constructively dissatisfied with our performance... We face pressure among the most price sensitive DIY filers... We lost on price.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Data Center revenue of $75B (+92% YoY) driven by the rapid ramp of the Blackwell architecture and strong inference demand.
2. Announced new 'Vera' CPU for agentic AI, opening a new $200B TAM with visibility to nearly $20B in revenue this year.
3. Strong Q2 guidance of $91B and long-term visibility into $1 trillion in revenue from Blackwell and Rubin platforms through 2027.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Continued exclusion of China Data Center compute revenue from the outlook due to regulatory uncertainty on imports.
2. Full-year OpEx growth forecast was increased to the 'upper forties' percent range year-over-year.
3. Consumer demand in the Edge Computing segment fell modestly due to higher memory and system prices.
rows.key_quote: Demand has gone parabolic. The reason is simple. Agentic AI has arrived.

rows.positive_highlights: 1.
