rows.positive_highlights: 1. Regulatory Milestone: Submitted a Construction Permit Application (CPA) to the U.S. NRC for its KRONOS reactor, one of the first Gen 4 developers to do so. 2. Commercial Progress: Completed a 1-gigawatt power feasibility study for BaRupOn's AI data center campus and signed key MOUs with Supermicro and EHC Investment. 3. Strong Liquidity: Ended the quarter with $569 million in cash, deemed sufficient to fund its prototype through construction and commissioning.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Increasing Net Loss: Net loss grew by $3 million quarter-over-quarter to $9.2 million, driven by higher development and headcount expenses. 2. Rising Future Expenses: Management expects expenses to continue increasing as the company scales up and begins procuring long-lead items. 3. Pre-Revenue Stage: The company has no revenue and commercialization remains years away, pending successful construction and licensing of its prototype post-2027.
rows.key_quote: The recent CPA submission to the U.S. NRC for our prototype at the University of Illinois represented a substantial milestone, validating our design maturity.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised Guidance: Full-year revenue guidance was increased to $2.56B-$2.58B and Adjusted EBITDA to $328M-$332M due to strong Q1 performance. 
2. Successful Preferred Payer Strategy: Signed 4 new PDS agreements (reaching 60% of MCO volume) and 4 new Home Health agreements, driving double-digit volume growth in those segments.
3. Strong Segment Growth: All divisions grew year-over-year, with Home Health & Hospice revenue up 17.4%, Private Duty Services up 16.4%, and Medical Solutions up 7.4%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Negative Free Cash Flow: Free cash flow was negative $3.8 million, as Q1 is the company's typical seasonal low point for cash generation.
2. Weather Impact: January weather events negatively impacted revenue by approximately $5.5-$6 million and EBITDA by about $1.5 million.
3. Moderating Government Rate Wins: Management noted a shift away from significant government rate wins, increasing reliance on commercial preferred payer negotiations for future rate enhancements.
rows.key_quote: It is clear that aligning caregiver capacity with preferred payers who value our partnership is the right path forward at Aveanna.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Performance & Accretive Acquisition: Achieved record revenue of $187M (~3x YoY) and positive adjusted EBITDA, driven by the immediately accretive Lanteris acquisition which expanded production scale and margins.
2. Major Contract Wins & Backlog Growth: Secured over $400M in new bookings, including a spot on the $6.24B Andromeda IDIQ and the SDA Tranche 3 award, growing total backlog to a record $1.1B.
3. Strategic Expansion: Announced the acquisition of Goonhilly Earth Station to build out a global ground network, strengthening the company's end-to-end space infrastructure services for commercial and government clients.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. High Cash Burn: Reported negative free cash flow of $64.6M, driven by onetime acquisition costs of ~$20M for Lanteris, R&D investments, and inventory pre-buys.
2. Increased Operating Loss: Operating loss widened to $39.2M from $10.1M YoY, primarily due to non-recurring acquisition-related expenses and amortization.
3. Elevated SG&A: SG&A expenses were $50.7M, inflated by $20M in transaction/integration costs and $6.3M in share-based compensation tied to the Lanteris deal.
rows.key_quote: Lanteris expanded our production scale and margin profile. Second, national security demand accelerated with SDA and Andromeda wins.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record revenue of $63M, up 36.7% YoY, driven entirely by volume growth in flagship Kefir and farmer cheese.
2. Gross margin expanded 360 basis points to 27.5% due to higher volume, manufacturing efficiencies, and favorable milk pricing.
3. Successfully capitalizing on consumer trends including gut health, GLP-1 user demand, and new USDA guidance.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Management noted it is beginning to lap significant distribution gains from 2025, creating more challenging year-over-year comparisons.
2. No other material negative factors were discussed.
3. No other material negative factors were discussed.
rows.key_quote: This record breaking achievement...represents entirely volume led expansion, fueled by our flagship Lifeway Kefir and high protein LifeWay farmer cheese.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Revenue and Profitability: Achieved record $5 billion in revenue and $871 million in net income, up 41% YoY on an FX-neutral basis.
2. Strong Customer Growth and International Progress: Reached 135 million total customers, with Mexico surpassing 15 million customers and achieving its first quarter of IFRS profitability.
3. Operating Leverage: Delivered a record-low efficiency ratio of 17.6%, driven by scalable technology and AI-driven productivity gains, with engineering throughput up over 50% YoY.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Increased Credit Provisions: Credit Loss Allowance (CLA) increased 33% QoQ to $1.79 billion, driven by growth, seasonality and mix, not credit quality deterioration.
2. Risk-Adjusted Margin Compression: Risk-adjusted Net Interest Margin (NIM) declined 100 bps sequentially to 9.5% as a direct result of higher provisioning.
3. Mexico Deposit Outflow: Experienced a deposit outflow in Mexico, attributed to a reversal of seasonal year-end inflows and a deliberate strategy to optimize funding costs.
rows.key_quote: Portfolio growth alone contributed $423 million, more than half of the total [ECL allowance] build, which simply reflects the upfront lifetime loss provisioning we book.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong residential leasing performance with new free market leases up over 7% and renewals up 5%, driving record rents and 99% overall occupancy.
2. Successful initial lease-up of the new Prospect House development, which is now fully leased at strong market rents of approximately $78 per foot.
3. Ongoing stabilized residential properties showed a 9% revenue increase and an 18% AFFO increase year-over-year.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Termination of the NYC lease at 250 Livingston Street caused a $4.2 million revenue decrease and a $5.8 million decrease in AFFO.
2. Company ceased debt payments on the 250 Livingston Street property, effectively defaulting on the loan and creating uncertainty around its resolution.
3. Consolidated AFFO plummeted by 71% to $2.3 million from $8.0 million a year ago, primarily due to the Livingston lease termination.
rows.key_quote: A $5.8 million AFFO decrease reflects... a $5.8 million decrease from the 250 Livingston Street property, resulting from the New York City lease termination.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Broad-Based Demand Strength: Demand was strong across all served regions, enabling a 14% capacity increase while improving load factor to 87.2% and passenger yield by 1.6%.
2. Record Profitability and Margin Expansion: Achieved record net profit of $212M (EPS up 20.5% YoY) and an industry-leading operating margin of 24.6%, up 0.8 percentage points YoY.
3. Disciplined Cost Control: Unit costs excluding fuel (CASM-ex) declined 1% year-over-year to $0.058, demonstrating effective cost management amid significant growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Major Jet Fuel Price Shock: Management projects an 80-90% year-over-year increase in all-in jet fuel prices for Q2, creating a significant cost headwind.
2. Lag in Cost Pass-Through: The company expects to recover only ~50% of the Q2 fuel cost spike via revenue due to tickets booked in advance, leading to sharply lower Q2 margin guidance (8-12%).
3. Temporary Guidance Uncertainty: Management is holding off on updating full-year operating margin guidance until the volatile fuel and pricing environment becomes clearer, indicating a lack of near-term visibility.
rows.key_quote: I would say that we see strength across the network and not necessarily one region is stronger than other...every region we serve is performing very well.

rows.positive_highlights:
Reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $130 million, citing strong customer demand and visibility.
Expanded NeoTensr contract to a total potential value of $70 million, with an $11M+ delivery expected in Q2.
Announced Blaize AI Services, a new recurring revenue stream, and secured new strategic partnerships with Winmate ($15M first year intent) and Datacomm.
rows.negative_highlights:
Q1 revenue of $2.7 million was negatively impacted by a global HBM shortage, which delayed an $11M+ order to Q2.
Supply chain constraints for HBM-intensive servers persist, though the company is mitigating this with its own DDR-based hybrid server designs.
Revenue is heavily back-half weighted for 2026, increasing execution risk to meet the full-year $130M guidance.
rows.key_quote: Q1 revenue... reflects a global memory shortage that limited server availability from one of our trusted suppliers and delayed orders.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong underlying growth: Revenue up 21% to €1.6B and underlying EBIT grew 36% to €76M. 2. Massive near-term awards expected: Forecasting €4B to €8B in new contracts in the next 45 days. 3. Solid cash generation: Generated €112M, boosting net cash to €360M.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Major project disruption: A €45M provision was booked to cover impacts from the Middle East conflict. 2. Execution uncertainty: Four key projects representing €1.5B in backlog are significantly impacted by logistical and site disruptions. 3. Guidance risk: Revenue guidance of €6.5B is now considered 'very tight' and the provision is contingent on the conflict not escalating.
rows.key_quote: The eruptions and impact that we have estimated in EUR 45 million, for which we have decided to make a provision in our accounts.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. China revenue rebound: $47.4M driven by EVO+ launch and normalized end-market demand after clearing excess inventory. 2. Profitability restoration: Achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of $24.4M, a swing from a $26.3M loss YoY, and net income of $0.10/share. 3. Gross margin expansion: Margin increased to 73.6% from 65.8% YoY due to reduced Swiss manufacturing ramp-up costs and lower inventory provisions.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Refusal to provide guidance: Management repeatedly declined to give a financial forecast, citing macro uncertainty, despite a very strong quarter. 2. Headwinds in smaller markets: Geopolitical and trade disruptions impacted sales in the Middle East by less than $2 million, with macro volatility also affecting India. 3. Sluggish macro market conditions: U.S. laser vision correction market was down 7% in Q1, indicating STAAR's growth is dependent on market share gains.
rows.key_quote: In China, our first quarter performance reflected continued share gains in premium lens-based refractive surgery.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Revenue Growth in Core Brands: Revenue driven by Merrell (up 9% CC) and Saucony (up 15% CC), which both exceeded expectations.
2. EPS Guidance Raised: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $1.43-$1.58 from $1.35-$1.50, driven by a better gross margin outlook due to lower tariffs.
3. Profitability Improvement: Adjusted operating margin expanded 140 basis points to 7.7%, and adjusted EPS grew 32% year-over-year, demonstrating significant leverage.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Sweaty Betty U.S. Contraction: Brand revenue declined 4% due to an intentional strategic reset of the U.S. business to a more premium model, causing a near-term headwind.
2. Macroeconomic Caution: Management cited a 'dynamic operating environment', higher freight costs from oil prices, and consumer pressure as reasons for prudently not raising revenue guidance despite the Q1 beat.
3. Wolverine Brand still declining: The namesake Wolverine brand's revenue declined 3%, though this was an improvement and in-line with expectations, indicating the turnaround is still in progress.
rows.key_quote: The growth was driven by our 2 biggest brands. Merrell grew revenue high single digits, while Saucony was up mid-teens.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Major SafePointe Bookings: Secured a 3-year, $3.2M deal ($1M+ ARR) with a major hospital chain and another $1M+ hospital deal, validating the healthcare vertical strategy.
2. Key Competitive Win: Retained the Cleveland contract despite competitive pressure, with the Mayor crediting ShotSpotter for an 80% homicide solve rate.
3. Cost Savings & Guidance Reaffirmation: Reaffirmed full-year guidance with confidence, supported by a $4M annualized cost savings plan and a clear path to second-half revenue acceleration.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant Profitability Decline: Adjusted EBITDA swung from a $4.5M profit in Q1 2025 to a $100k loss in Q1 2026, driven by investments and weaker revenue.
2. Heavy Investment Drag: The SafePointe product is generating over $8 million in annualized losses, heavily weighing on consolidated profitability.
3. Revenue and Margin Contraction: Revenue declined 14.5% year-over-year, and gross margin fell from 59% to 47%, primarily due to a non-recurring $3.5M catch-up revenue in the prior-year quarter.
rows.key_quote: SafePointe... is currently generating over $8 million of annualized losses as we invest ahead of expected revenue.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Wholesale channel grew 19%, its strongest quarter in over 3 years, driven by robust double-digit watch-through in the U.S. consumer market.
2. Drinkware sales grew 5%, marking a return to growth in the U.S. and validating the platform's durability and innovation strategy.
3. Coolers & Equipment sales increased 11%, led by strong performance in soft coolers and bags, with demand outpacing supply.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Adjusted gross margin for Q1 decreased by 200 basis points to 55.3% year-over-year, primarily due to a 280 basis point headwind from higher tariff costs.
2. Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) sales were flat, pulled down by a decline in the corporate sales channel due to order timing and a cautious corporate environment.
3. Adjusted EPS declined 16.1% to $0.26 from $0.31, reflecting the impact of lower gross margins and investments in growth.
rows.key_quote: Global wholesale grew 19% year-over-year, our strongest quarter in more than 3 years, driven by consumer pull and notable weakness-through trends.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong portfolio credit quality with non-accruals decreasing to 1.1% from 1.7% and robust interest coverage of 3.5x.
Significant unrealized equity appreciation of $37.8 million ($0.62/share) with clear expectations to realize gains in fiscal 2027.
Robust capital position with over $625 million raised in new debt and accretive equity during the year, and $394 million in available liquidity.
rows.negative_highlights:
Total investment income decreased quarter-over-quarter to $57.8M from $61.4M, primarily driven by a 35 basis point drop in SOFR.
NAV per share declined to $16.69 from $16.75, impacted by a specific asset write-down and market multiple compression.
Deal close rate moderated from 2.0% to 1.5% as the company maintained discipline amid a more competitive market with tighter leverage and pricing.
rows.key_quote: We had one portfolio company that was added to our watch list that had a write-down, and then the rest... multiples were down.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. TPV growth accelerated to a record $14.1 billion, up 73% YoY, driven by broad-based growth across markets and verticals.
2. Strong recovery in Argentina with normalized funding costs and strong volume growth, contributing significantly to a record $119 million gross profit.
3. Africa and Asia division grew gross profit by 16% QoQ, now representing 29% of the total, demonstrating successful geographic diversification.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Reported net income was impacted by a $9.7 million one-off prior period tax adjustment, which also hit operating expenses.
2. Operating expenses (excluding the tax adjustment) grew 58% YoY due to the carryover from the 2025 investment cycle, pressuring margins in H1.
3. Brazil experienced a sequential gross profit decline due to seasonality and a mix shift towards lower-monetization Pix payments after a strong Q4.
rows.key_quote: Compared to international acquiring... we're able to deliver up to 20 percentage points conversion uplift in certain markets.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Raised full-year revenue guidance to $325M-$345M and adjusted EBITDA to $115M-$135M due to strong Q1 execution. 2. DefenCath sales drove a Q1 revenue beat ($127.4M total), with DefenCath full-year guidance also increased to $175M-$195M. 3. The ReSPECT Phase III study for REZZAYO met its primary endpoint, paving the way for an sNDA submission and potential 2027 launch.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Expects DefenCath price erosion and sales variability in H2 2026 due to the expiration of TDAPA reimbursement. 2. The Phase III TPN study for DefenCath is delayed into 2028 due to slow enrollment and lower-than-expected infection rates. 3. A significant Q2 shelf stock adjustment for DefenCath is expected in June, effectively creating a '2-month quarter' for the product.
rows.key_quote: Our primary objective for Q3 and Q4 is to maintain or grow existing patient utilization heading into 2027.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. **Massive AI Opportunity**: The new Genesis AI product saw unexpectedly high early interest (500+ users) and is expected to open a $12.5B market, with management seeing an opportunity to double the business.
2. **U.S. Federal Business Rebound**: The U.S. Federal segment is "rebounding quickly" with a 35% YoY increase in its pipeline, supported by the recent FedRAMP High authorization, which opens new government cloud opportunities.
3. **Strengthened Product Portfolio**: Launched several key offerings including a market-leading device unlock solution and the GA of Guardian Investigate, creating a more comprehensive end-to-end platform.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. **Modest Q1 Net New ARR**: Net new ARR of $12.2 million was described as modest and was flat year-over-year, attributed to seasonality, a small pool of contract expirations, and deal pushes.
2. **FX Headwinds**: The Q2 outlook includes an estimated two-point headwind to adjusted EBITDA margin from unfavorable foreign exchange rates.
3. **Flat Services Revenue**: Non-recurring revenue from training, hardware, and professional services is expected to be flat, indicating it is not a growth driver for the company.
rows.key_quote: Within 15 minutes, Genesis identified 16 additional victims... a manual review would have required approximately 2 weeks of investigator man hours.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Achieved a 23% average rent escalation on re-leased hangars over the last 12 months, an acceleration from 22% in the prior quarter, demonstrating strong pricing power. 2. Successfully opened Miami Phase 2 with 68% pre-occupancy, validating the new pre-leasing strategy and on-time, on-budget delivery through the Ascend construction program. 3. Secured $368M in liquidity, fully funding a development pipeline that doubles the company's size, with a strategic shift towards higher-value Tier 1 markets (48% of new sq. ft.).
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Allowed the ground lease for a planned Seattle campus (Boeing Field) to lapse due to unfavorable long-term lease terms offered. 2. Operating expenses increased due to new campus openings and non-revenue generating ground leases, pressuring near-term margins. 3. The Denver (APA) campus is experiencing a slower lease-up than other locations, currently standing at only 44% leased.
rows.key_quote: The average escalation between one lease and the next is 23%. By the way, that's up from 22% in the last quarter.

rows.positive_highlights:
1) Extremely strong forward bookings provides high visibility: 2026 is 92% booked with advanced bookings up 13% YoY, while 2027 is already 38% booked with advanced bookings up 31% YoY. 
2) Robust Q1 top-line and profitability growth: Q1 revenue grew 17.5% YoY to over $1B, and Adjusted EBITDA grew 43.9% YoY to $105M. 
3) Strong pricing and yield improvement: Consolidated net yield rose 9.5% YoY, driven by strong pricing and a strategic shift to higher-yielding itineraries like Egypt and Vietnam.
rows.negative_highlights:
1) Temporary booking softness: Management acknowledged a short-term softening in bookings for the 2026 season due to geopolitical events, although demand has since fully rebounded. 
2) Increased operating costs: Vessel expenses excluding fuel per capacity day increased 10.6% in the quarter, driven by the timing of repair and maintenance work across the fleet. 
3) Anticipated fuel cost pressure: Management expects higher fuel prices to affect results as the year progresses, particularly for the ocean segment which has greater sensitivity to market movements.
rows.key_quote: This shift towards higher-yielding itineraries combined with continued pricing strength drove a materially favorable increase in net yield.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. AI-Driven Demand Surge: Raised outlook for semiconductor equipment business to >30% growth in calendar 2026, fueled by the accelerating build-out of AI infrastructure. 2. Record Financials & Margin Expansion: Achieved record Q2 revenue ($7.91B, +11% YoY), record EPS ($2.86, +20% YoY), and the highest gross margin in 25 years at 50% (+80 bps YoY). 3. Strength in Key Growth Segments: Expects packaging revenue to grow >50% in 2026, with leading-edge logic, DRAM, and packaging accounting for over 80% of WFE spending growth.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Supply Chain Constraints: The primary bottleneck limiting even faster growth is the broader supply chain's ability to respond to surging demand. 2. ICAPS Business Digestion: The ICAPS business is expected to be flat to slightly higher as the market digests significant capacity added in prior years. 3. China Business Risk: While factored into guidance, questions about Huawei restrictions highlight ongoing regulatory uncertainty as a potential headwind.
rows.key_quote: AI adoption is accelerating and diversifying, fueling broad and durable demand for semiconductors and semiconductor equipment.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Announced two major acquisitions (Breathe Right, LaCorium) expected to add over $165M in revenue and be accretive to growth. 2. Generated strong free cash flow of $246.4M in FY26, enabling strategic investments and capital returns. 3. Strong performance in GI franchise (Dramamine, Fleet, Hydralyte) and double-digit growth in e-commerce, which now represents 18% of the business.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Q4 revenue missed expectations, declining 5% (6.4% organic) due to supply issues and shipping disruptions. 2. Severe supply constraints in the core Clear Eyes brand, resulting from production shutdowns and shipment delays, significantly impacted Q4 and are expected to weigh on H1 FY27. 3. Full-year FY26 revenue declined ~4% and adjusted EPS fell to $4.38 from $4.52 in the prior year, primarily due to the Eye Care supply issues.
rows.key_quote: In Q4, Clear Eyes sales were below expectations due to delayed shipments and production shutdowns ahead of line updates.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Positive VIKTORIA-1 Mutant Cohort Data: Gedatolisib triplet showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in Progression-Free Survival (PFS) versus the standard of care. 2. VIKTORIA-2 Trial Expansion: Expanded Phase III study to include the larger first-line endocrine-sensitive patient population, targeting an additional ~60,000 U.S. patients annually. 3. Commercial Launch Readiness: Hired and onboarded an entire experienced oncology sales force (average 16 years experience) in preparation for a potential Q3 launch.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Widening Net Loss: Q1 net loss increased to $52.8 million from $37.0 million year-over-year due to pre-launch spending. 2. Increased Cash Burn: Cash used in operations rose to $55.1 million from $35.9 million, driven by an $8.7 million increase in commercial headcount and launch activities. 3. Long Clinical Timelines: Data for the newly expanded VIKTORIA-2 studies are not expected until the end of 2028 and 2030, indicating a long-term investment horizon.
rows.key_quote: The gedatolisib triplet demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival compared to alpelisib and fulvestrant.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Improving Sales Trend: Quarter-to-date Q3 same-store sales are "approaching flat" after a -3.8% decline in Q2, driven by a better balanced barbell strategy. 
2. Digital Channel Optimization: Improved offer lineup on first and third-party digital channels is now driving higher and more profitable checks. 
3. Operational Green Shoots: Seeing improvements in customer satisfaction, accuracy, and friendliness, with low-cost mini refreshes delivering a low single-digit sales lift.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant Sales Decline: Q2 same-store sales decreased 3.8% due to a decline in transactions. 
2. Severe Margin Compression: Restaurant level margin fell to 16.4% from 19.6% due to commodity inflation (especially beef at double-digits), wage pressure, and sales deleverage. 
3. Lowered Full-Year Guidance: Lowered same-store sales guidance to a "low single digits" decline and adjusted EBITDA to $225M-$235M.
rows.key_quote: Second quarter same-store sales decreased 3.8%,... resulted primarily from a decline in transactions, partially offset by menu price increases.

rows.positive_highlights: Distributable earnings of $0.35/share significantly covered the $0.30 dividend, boosted by one-time fees. Generated $1.6 million in non-recurring income from a $1.2M prepayment fee (Boheme loan) and a $400k fee (Silver Mountain loan). All loans in the portfolio are current and performing, with a weighted average yield of 12.4%.
rows.negative_highlights: A loan on the Thompson San Antonio hotel was foreclosed on, becoming a non-income-producing REO asset during the quarter. Q1 distributable earnings were significantly inflated by one-time fees, suggesting a lower run-rate going forward. No income is expected from the San Antonio hotel for the next couple of quarters until it is sold.
rows.key_quote: The quarter included onetime fees from 2 investments: a $400,000 fee on a short-term loan and a $1.2 million prepayment fee.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. User engagement soared, with workflow active prescribers growing 30% year-over-year to 800,000, a significant acceleration. 2. Rapid adoption of the clinical AI suite, with 140 health systems now as customers, including 7 of the top 20 U.S. hospitals. 3. Generated a record $107 million in free cash flow during the quarter, ending the fiscal year with a strong $749 million cash position.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Weak forward guidance, with full-year FY27 revenue growth projected at only 4%, a steep drop from 13% in FY26. 2. Significant margin compression expected, with FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guided to 49%, down from 55%, due to heavy AI investments. 3. Softening core market, with management citing weak demand in the HCP digital pharma ad market, macro uncertainty, and clients shifting to shorter-term contracts.
rows.key_quote: Our benchmark workflow engagement reached over 800,000 unique quarterly active prescribers in Q4, up roughly 30% year-on-year, a significant acceleration.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Total revenue surged 19% in Q4, driven by the opening of 25 new stores (a record 80 for the year) and a strong 6.1% consolidated same-store sales growth. 2. The work boots category showed significant strength, achieving its fourth consecutive quarter of accelerating comp sales growth and starting Q1'27 with high single-digit comps. 3. Exclusive brand penetration for the full year grew by 220 basis points to 40.8%, outperforming expectations and helping to expand full-year merchandise margin by 80 basis points.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Q4 gross profit margin declined by 80 basis points year-over-year to 36.3%, primarily due to deleverage from new store occupancy and distribution center costs. 2. Near-term cost pressures are significant, with guidance indicating a high 10% same-store sales growth is needed in FY27 to leverage watching, occupancy, and distribution costs. 3. Q1 FY27 EPS is guided to decline year-over-year to $1.71 from $1.74, citing a difficult comparison against an extremely strong prior-year quarter and higher freight costs.
rows.key_quote: men's and ladies apparel increased double digits, led by low-teens growth in denim.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Regulatory Progress: FCC advanced the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) to the interagency review process, a key milestone. 2) Technical Advancement: Ongoing 5G PNT network testing in Santa Clara and joint railroad testing in Pueblo mark important steps toward commercialization. 3) New Applications & Partnerships: Joined OCUDU foundation for drone sensing and seeing improved commercial interest from carriers, satellite, and big tech for low-band spectrum.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) Increased Opposition: Acknowledged a 'significant increase in opposition activity,' including a recent attempt to stall the NPRM through the House Appropriations Committee. 2) Regulatory Uncertainty: The timing for the final NPRM is not fixed and 'remains subject to these ongoing reviews' by interagency bodies like OIRA. 3) Implied Cash Burn: As a pre-revenue company, it reported a net loss of $10.6M, indicating ongoing cash usage until commercialization.
rows.key_quote: The commercial environment has only improved as interest continues to expand for access to low-band spectrum.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Expecting material oil-weighted production growth from H2 2026 into 2027, driven by specific well developments in the Permian and Powder River Basins. 
2. Strengthened balance sheet with $10M in debt reduction and non-core asset sales totaling $6.9M, funding growth initiatives. 
3. Implementing PRB operational efficiencies, including compressor downsizing (35% monthly savings) and rod pump conversions (10% production increase per well), set to lower unit costs.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Q1 earnings materially impacted by noncash, unrealized hedge losses due to the quarter's dramatic rise in oil prices. 
2. Unit operating costs were temporarily high in Q1 (high-teens to low-20s per BOE in PRB) due to the fixed cost base of newly acquired assets before new production comes online. 
3. Service cost inflation is a risk, with management noting that rig availability is tightening and rig rates are 'creeping up' in the Powder River Basin.
rows.key_quote: We expect to deliver meaningful production growth year-over-year, with the oil-weighted ramp in the Permian and Powder River basins building through the year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Superior Book Value Growth: Grew book value per diluted share by 7.2% in the quarter to $26.22, driven by a strong 86.6% combined ratio and accretive share repurchases ($219M).
2. Effective Capital Allocator Model: Gross written premiums grew 7%, driven by new underwriting partnerships in both Insurance (+13%) and Reinsurance (+7% ex-reinstatements), demonstrating the model's flexibility to find growth.
3. Profitable Niche Opportunities: Successfully capitalized on market dislocations, noting a 'step change in marine war rents, driven by conflict in the Middle East' and strong performance in Property with a sub-40% loss ratio over 3 years.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Increased Market Competition: Acknowledged a more competitive market, particularly in property lines, with 'mid- to high single digits, low double-digit reductions' in pricing.
2. Baltimore Bridge Loss Impact: Recognized increased loss estimates related to the Baltimore Bridge collapse, which created adverse prior year development, though overall PYD remained favorable.
3. Pressure in Cyber Market: Non-renewed a cyber policy because the partner was unwilling to provide a loss ratio cap at an acceptable level, indicating pressure on terms.
rows.key_quote: In Marine, we saw strong new business flow with a step change in marine war rents, driven by conflict in the Middle East.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Gross margin expanded 530 basis points to 67.9% due to inventory resets and higher full-price sales. 2. Key markets showed strong momentum with Greater China and the Americas both delivering 10% comparable sales growth in Q4. 3. Adjusted operating profit surged to GBP 160 million from GBP 26 million last year, and net debt-to-EBITDA improved from 2.3x to 1.6x.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. EMEA region declined 2% in Q4, reflecting continued weaker tourism. 2. Japan sales declined 6% in Q4 due to reduced inbound tourists. 3. For the full year, wholesale revenue was down 4% and licensing revenue was down 9%.
rows.key_quote: ...quality of sales growth, combined with decisive actions to reset inventory has allowed us a substantial improvement in gross margin...

rows.positive_highlights: Explosive AI cloud business growth with Annual Recurring Revenue reaching $43 million by quarter-end and GPU utilization climbing to 94%. Strategic pivot to AI data center colocation is progressing, with the Tydal, Norway site conversion underway and advanced lease negotiations with a potential tenant. Strengthened balance sheet with a $375 million convertible note offering, ending the quarter with $298 million in cash.
rows.negative_highlights: Reported a significant gross margin deterioration to -20.7% and an operating loss of $159.5 million, driven by lower bitcoin prices and high costs. Margin headwinds from $70 million in non-cash depreciation related to rapid miner deployment and high seasonal electricity costs. Disclosed potential construction delays at the key 570 MW Clarington, Ohio site due to litigation.
rows.key_quote: The supply and demand imbalance for AI compute has widened, and we expect this shortage to persist well into 2027 and beyond.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. **Northern Data Acquisition Progress**: Secured ~81% of shares and all regulatory approvals for the transformative acquisition, which is on track to close in Q2. Northern Data itself reported record Q1 revenue. 2. **Strong MAU Growth**: Monthly active users grew sequentially to 56 million, driven by international expansion and the fast-growing, though unmonetized, Rumble Shorts feature. 3. **Cloud Business Traction**: Secured institutional-grade customer Anchorage Digital for Rumble Cloud and is in active negotiations with multiple other customers for GPU-as-a-Service.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. **Deepening Net Loss**: Net loss widened significantly to $30.3 million compared to $2.7 million in the prior year, driven by non-cash charges and acquisition costs. 2. **Negative Gross Margin**: Cost of services ($27.0 million) exceeded revenue ($25.5 million), resulting in a gross loss of $1.5 million for the quarter. 3. **ARPU Dilution**: The rapid growth of the unmonetized Rumble Shorts feature had a negative impact on the average revenue per user (ARPU).
rows.key_quote: Cloud will become a pillar alongside video. And from early indications, Cloud should be the largest generator of revenue.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. RGX-202 pivotal trial met its primary endpoint with 93% of patients exceeding the 10% microdystrophin expression threshold. 
2. Showed a landmark, highly statistically significant correlation (coefficient > 0.9) between microdystrophin expression and functional improvement. 
3. The partial clinical hold on RGX-121 for Hunter syndrome was fully lifted, and a $100 million milestone payment from AbbVie is anticipated in Q2.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant uncertainty regarding the regulatory path, as the FDA has previously context a randomized controlled trial (RCT) for approval. 
2. Two treatment-related serious adverse events (SAEs) were reported in the trial (myocarditis and liver injury), though both were resolved. 
3. Interim functional data, while very positive, is based on a small sample of only 9 patients.
rows.key_quote: RGX-202 demonstrated a highly statistically significant correlation between microdystrophin expression and functional improvement, a landmark distinction in Duchenne gene therapy.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Champions brand revenue grew 17% driven by new site openings and incremental pricing. 2. Targeted marketing investments resulted in a 15% inquiry increase in key areas and 3% overall. 3. The 'opportunity region' demonstrated successful turnaround potential with an 8% year-over-year enrollment increase.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Core ECE center enrollment declined 3% year-over-year, remaining the primary pressure point on the business. 2. Same-center occupancy fell 310 basis points, causing a significant drop in adjusted EBITDA to $52 million from $83 million a year ago. 3. The company plans to close a higher-than-usual number of underperforming centers, creating near-term revenue variability not yet reflected in guidance.
rows.key_quote: Enrollment in our ECE centers remain below prior year levels, down about 3%,...it continues to be a primary pressure point on the business.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong AI Pods momentum: Reached $32.8M in ARR with a $352M pipeline and adoption in 40% of top 20 accounts, offering structurally higher margins. 2. Top client recovery: Top 50 clients grew 5.2% YoY and top 10 grew 4% YoY, significantly outperforming the company average and signaling a rebound led by strategic accounts. 3. Strong cash flow and capital return: Generated $36.1M of free cash flow (vs negative in prior year's Q1) and authorized a new $125M share repurchase plan.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Gross margin pressure: Adjusted gross margin of 37% was negatively impacted by strong LatAm currencies (Mexican and Colombian pesos, Brazilian real) and other cost increases. 2. Modest revenue decline: Reported revenue declined 0.7% YoY to $607.1 million, though this marked a significant improvement in trajectory from the prior quarter. 3. Macro headwinds: Management cited risks from volatility in the Middle East and rising fuel prices affecting airline clients, creating uncertainty reflected in the guidance range.
rows.key_quote: Our Data and AI studio is growing north of 25% year-over-year, reflecting the priorities shaping enterprise technology investment today.

rows.positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 25% driven by strong royalty streams and proprietary product sales, with EPKINLY sales increasing 52% to $137 million. The pivotal Phase III trial for Rina-S (RAINFOL-02) in ovarian cancer completed enrollment ahead of schedule, accelerating the data readout into 2026 from 2027. EPKINLY's U.S. label was updated to remove the hospitalization context, expected to broaden community adoption.
rows.negative_highlights: The pivotal frontline petosemtamab study size was increased by 40% to 700 patients, prompting multiple analyst questions about the trial's underlying assumptions. Management anticipates potential tax rate volatility over the next 12-18 months due to the integration of Merus operations. The company noted a "hypercompetitive space" for key assets like Rina-S, indicating significant competitive pressures.
rows.key_quote: Revenue grew by 25%, driven by strong royalties from DARZALEX and Kesimpta. And importantly, this growth was also driven by product sales.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Profitability growth despite headwinds: Adj. OP grew 2% to JPY 493.7B and net profit grew 15%, driven by JPY 72B in cost reductions that offset a JPY 25B tariff impact.
2. Key regional margin expansion: North America's adj. OP margin improved 1.5 pts to 11% and Europe's improved over 2 pts to 5.5% due to business rebuilding.
3. Strong cash flow and shareholder returns: Free cash flow increased by JPY 141.7B to JPY 435.5B, and the dividend for FY25 was increased by JPY 20 to JPY 230 per share.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant tariff impact: Faced a JPY 25B profit hit from U.S. tariffs in FY25, with the impact projected to more than double to JPY 55B in FY26.
2. Weakness in South America: The region's profit declined significantly, barely achieving breakeven due to low-end import competition and reduced export efficiency.
3. Sluggish top-line pressure: Overall revenue grew only 2%, with sales declining 3% in North America due to sluggish demand and 2% in Asia due to currency/strategy.
rows.key_quote: Business cost reduction activities also generated effects of approximately JPY 72 billion in fiscal '25, contributing to improved profitability.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Secured a new $150M debt facility with Oaktree, improving loan terms and projecting over $150M in cash for the Anaphylm launch.
2. Made significant regulatory progress on Anaphylm, completing an FDA Type A meeting and guiding to a Q3 resubmission, with key data expected in August.
3. Revenue grew 66% YoY to $14.4M and net loss narrowed substantially to $8.1M from $22.9M, demonstrating improved financial performance.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. A large portion of Q1 revenue growth stemmed from a one-time $5.4M royalty payment from Zevra, which is not a recurring run rate.
2. The Anaphylm resubmission timeline is entirely dependent on receiving timely and constructive feedback from the FDA on the required human factors study protocol.
3. Management explicitly stated that achieving broad payer coverage for Anaphylm post-launch will be a challenge that will "take time."
rows.key_quote: We currently expect to have our human factors data and... pharmacokinetic data for Anaphylm available in time for our August earnings call.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Q1 gross margin of 25.1% strongly exceeded guidance, aided by a one-time tariff refund that contributed 860 basis points.
2. Energy storage business has a contracted backlog of $3.5 billion and is expecting record deliveries in the second half of 2026.
3. U.S. manufacturing expansion is progressing, with the HJT solar cell factory in trial production and capacity being increased to 6.3 GW in response to strong demand.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Reported a net loss of $32 million ($0.71 per share) due to high opex, foreign exchange losses, and tax expenses.
2. Q2 gross margin guidance is very weak at 13%-15%, a significant drop from Q1, reflecting ongoing solar market challenges.
3. The Recurrent Energy (project development) segment posted an operating loss of $60 million as part of its strategy to monetize assets and deleverage.
rows.key_quote: Gross margin of 25.1% ... increased both sequentially and year-over-year due to the accrual of tariff refunds, which contributed 860 basis points.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong Asia Performance: Core earnings in Asia increased 22% year-over-year, driven by double-digit APE sales growth in Hong Kong, Japan, and Singapore.
Robust Future Earnings Pipeline: New business CSM (contractual service margin) grew 16%, with double-digit growth from each insurance segment, strengthening future earnings potential.
U.S. Sales Momentum: U.S. segment APE sales grew 29% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for accumulation products, leading to robust growth in new business CSM.
rows.negative_highlights:
Wealth Management Outflows: The Global Wealth and Asset Management (GWAM) division recorded net outflows of $4.4 billion, driven by higher redemptions in North American retail active mutual funds.
Canadian Insurance Challenges: Canadian core earnings declined 6% year-over-year due to unfavorable experience in group long-term disability, including higher claims incidence and lower recoveries.
ALDA Investment Underperformance: The ALDA portfolio recorded a $242 million negative charge from lower-than-expected returns, including a one-off CAD $50 million charge from a fire at an Australian timber asset.
rows.key_quote: This reflects strong growth in Asia, where core earnings increased 22% year-over-year, as well as the positive impact of share buybacks.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Achieved record product sales of $24.3 million, up 73% year-over-year, driven by broad-based growth from the existing rare disease portfolio.
2. Raised full-year revenue guidance to exceed $120 million, up from the previous $110 million, reflecting strong momentum and new product launches.
3. Successfully launched two new products, DESMODA and HEMANGEOL, with HEMANGEOL projected to potentially become the company's largest product by 2027.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Adjusted gross margin decreased to 67% from 69% in the prior-year period, diluted by lower-margin ex-U.S. INCRELEX sales.
2. Non-GAAP G&A expenses increased 22%, driven in part by higher FDA annual program fees as the company no longer qualifies for orphan exemptions.
3. The newly launched HEMANGEOL is expected to have 60-65% of its volume be near-zero revenue due to patient assistance programs, and will have limited revenue contribution in Q2.
rows.key_quote: Our growth continues to be driven by contributions across the product portfolio, including INCRELEX, ALKINDI, GALZIN and Carglumic Acid.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Strong operational execution, with port exports of 3.3M tonnes ahead of the prior year. 2) Growth in diversified earnings streams, with bulk materials handled up to 1.5M tonnes and animal nutrition sales up 5%. 3) Maintained strong balance sheet and reaffirmed full-year guidance, declaring a $0.14 interim dividend.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) Significant margin compression due to a global oversupply of grain, which is the primary driver of lower H1 results. 2) Lower reported result in Nutrition & Energy, driven by a negative $12M YoY swing from mark-to-market timing on derivatives and softer edible oil volumes. 3) Reduced grower watching activity due to low global grain prices, leading to lower grain receivals.
rows.key_quote: We have seen a global oversupply of grains, which have constrained margins in the first half of '26.

rows.positive_highlights:
Smartphone Qualification Progress: Aligned with lead customer Honor to remove the legacy 0.7C discharge test, replacing it with a more realistic 0.2C cycle test, which was a key gating item.
New Product Launch & Pipeline: Formally launched the MX1 drone battery with 360 Wh/kg energy density and announced a global pipeline exceeding $130 million for products from its Korean facility.
Technology & Manufacturing Advances: Developed AI2 engineering samples with >20% higher energy density for smart eyewear and a new mechanical dicing process to improve manufacturing throughput.
rows.negative_highlights:
Smartphone Commercial Launch Timeline: Broader commercial launch with Honor is not planned until 2027, with only small-volume field testing in H2 2026, as the new 0.2C test takes longer to run.
Operating Losses and Cash Burn: Reported a non-GAAP loss from operations of $28.8 million and a free cash flow outflow of $36.3 million, indicating continued high expenditures to fund R&D and scale-up.
Technical Challenges Remain: Still working through corner-case performance issues for smartphone batteries, such as power output at below-freezing temperatures for silicon anodes.
rows.key_quote: The 0.7C legacy test requirement has been removed as a gating item; we're now working on a 0.2C test which better reflects real-world usage.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. U.S. Acceleration: Organic revenue growth in the U.S. accelerated to 30% (from 25% in FY25), validating disciplined execution and leading to a new $55M brand investment.
2. Strong Revenue Growth: Group revenue grew 31% to $2.75B (21% organic), with customer adds of over 500,000.
3. Payments Scaling: Total payments revenue (pro forma) grew 53%, with Melio BillPay adding $4.24 to group ARPC, significantly shifting the revenue model toward consumption.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Gross Margin Compression: Consolidated gross margin declined by 5.1 percentage points to 83.9%, entirely due to the mix effect from the lower-margin Melio payments business.
2. Melio Losses: The Melio acquisition is currently dilutive to profitability, with losses increasing in H2 FY26 and a breakeven target not expected until H2 FY28.
3. Increased Churn: Headline MRR churn increased to 1.14%, driven by a strategic mix shift toward a higher-churn direct channel, although management noted cohort churn was flat.
rows.key_quote: In the U.S., organic growth accelerated to 30% through disciplined execution in target segments and improving product market fit.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Sports Data Services revenue grew 13% YoY, driven by the OpticOdds B2B product which saw 94% new deal growth and 178% international partner growth.
2. Non-SEO revenue represents over 50% of marketing revenue for the second consecutive quarter, indicating successful traffic diversification.
3. Announced a strategic restructuring to an "AI-first" model, expected to deliver $13 million in annualized cost savings, driving margin expansion in H2 2026.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Marketing business revenue declined 5% due to persistent negative SEO trends and worse-than-expected regulatory headwinds in the U.K. and Finland.
2. Adjusted EBITDA margin collapsed to 22% from 39% YoY, driven by a shift to lower-margin revenue and higher cost of sales.
3. Lowered full-year guidance for both revenue (to $165M-$170M) and Adjusted EBITDA (to $45M-$50M) due to the accelerated negative mix shift.
rows.key_quote: Revenue of $29.2 million in Q1 reflects the negative SEO trends we have been discussing for several quarters.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Real Estate Leasing Strength: Signed 2.6M sq ft of global office leases with average net rents 15% above expiring levels, including a >100% increase in the U.S.
2. Asset Management Momentum: Raised $67B of capital year-to-date, with fee-related earnings up 11% to $772M, positioning the company for a record fundraising year.
3. Wealth Solutions Expansion: Closed the acquisition of Just Group, adding $40B in assets and scaling its presence in the U.K. pension risk transfer market.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Residential Real Estate Lag: North American residential performance was down y/y due to the absence of a prior year gain and delayed lot sales in the quarter.
2. Annuity Market Softening: Management noted that overall U.S. demand for fixed annuities was down 9-10% year-over-year, though the company gained market share.
3. Planned Annuity Outflows: The company expects $10-12 billion in annual outflows from its annuity business, a natural consequence of its liability duration profile.
rows.key_quote: In office, we signed 2.6 million square feet of leases globally with average net rents 15% above the expiring levels.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong Gaming Performance: Domestic games gross receipts grew at a teens percentage rate, with Honor of Kings and Peacekeeper Elite achieving record highs. 2. Advertising Re-acceleration: Marketing Services revenue grew 20% YoY, driven by increased ad inventory and demand from Video Accounts. 3. AI Progress & Early Monetization: Hunyuan 3 model is driving usage across 131 internal products, and AI-related cloud demand is contributing to Business Services' 20% YoY revenue growth.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Increased CapEx and R&D Costs: Operating CapEx rose 18% YoY with a "substantial increase" planned for H2 to fund AI infrastructure. R&D expenses rose 19% YoY. 2. Social Network Revenue Decline: The segment's revenue decreased 2% YoY, primarily due to the timing of the Spring Festival impacting game item sales revenue recognition. 3. Nascent AI Monetization: While showing promise, large-scale monetization of new AI agent products is in its very early stages, with management noting the upturn is only weeks old.
rows.key_quote: For Tencent Cloud, AI-related demand contributed to increased revenue year-on-year across GPU, CPU and storage.

rows.positive_highlights:
Symvess commercial sales grew to $0.5M, a 400% increase from $0.1M in the prior-year quarter.
Received a $1.475 million purchase commitment from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for clinical evaluation and outreach programs.
Nearing top-line interim results for the Phase III V012 trial in dialysis access (expected June 11, 2026), with plans to file a supplemental BLA in H2 2026 if positive.
rows.negative_highlights:
Slow commercial uptake of Symvess necessitated a significant restructuring, including a ~25% workforce reduction and a revamp of the commercial leadership team.
Reported a significant negative gross margin due to a $1.6 million inventory reserve and costs from unused production capacity.
Net loss was $17.6 million, a major unfavorable swing from a $39.1 million net income in the prior-year period, primarily due to non-cash accounting changes.
rows.key_quote: While we've seen expansion in the commercial uptake of Symvess, we also recognize that more rapid product uptake and sales growth is necessary.
